title: The complexity of provoked venous thromboembolism: one treatment plan does not fit all.
abstract: The decision of whether to continue patients diagnosed with venous thromboembolism (VTE) on anticoagulation after the initial treatment period is often nuanced. Many patients will have ≥1 transient risk factor associated with a time-limited increased risk of VTE. Transient risk factors are further divided into major factors, such as joint replacement, or minor factors, such as prolonged travel, which determine the magnitude of risk for an initial VTE. In addition, major transient risk factors generally carry a lower risk of recurrent VTE than minor transient risk factors. However, many patients will also have ≥1 persistent VTE risk factor, which further increase the risk for recurrence. Some persistent risk factors, such as inflammatory bowel disease, are associated with a sufficiently high risk of recurrent VTE, for which guidelines recommend indefinite anticoagulation. There are multiple other persistent risk factors that carry a lower risk of recurrent VTE, such as chronic renal insufficiency and obesity. The HI-PRO (High-Risk Patients with Provoked Venous Thromboembolism) trial sought to assess the efficacy and safety of extended thromboprophylaxis for the prevention of recurrent VTE in patients with an initial provoked VTE and at least 1 persistent risk factor. The study found a lower risk of recurrent VTE in the thromboprophylaxis cohort, challenging the traditional time-limited treatment for provoked VTE, but heterogeneity of the study population and small sample size preclude identification of which subsets of patients could safely discontinue anticoagulation. We consider the conundrum of provoked VTE in this review.

title: Association Between Cardiovascular Disease and Cataracts: Protocol for a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: There is emerging evidence suggesting shared pathophysiological mechanisms between cataracts and cardiovascular disease (CVD), indicating a potential link between these 2 prevalent noncommunicable diseases. Oxidative stress, resulting from an imbalance between reactive oxygen species production and the body's antioxidant defenses, contributes to lens protein aggregation in cataracts and lipid oxidation in atherosclerosis, a key feature of several CVD subtypes. This shared pathophysiology implies that systemic vascular health may influence cataractogenesis. However, the epidemiological evidence supporting this relationship remains inconclusive. OBJECTIVE: The main objective of this systematic review is to synthesize existing evidence on the odds or risk of developing cataracts in adults with underlying CVD. METHODS: I 2 This systematic review will adhere to the PRISMA-P (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Protocols). Using the population, exposure, comparator, and outcome framework, this review will identify the association between established CVD and the risk of cataract development or needing cataract surgery. Systematic literature searches will be conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase using MeSH terms from database inception to December 31, 2024. Original research articles involving adults (aged ≥18 years) that assess the statistical relationship between CVD and cataracts will be included. Two independent reviewers will screen studies, extract data, and appraise the studies' quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. If deemed feasible, meta-analyses will be conducted using random-effects models to calculate pooled effect estimates, with heterogeneity assessed using thestatistic. RESULTS: This study did not receive any external funding. The literature search, study screening, and data extraction will be conducted in 2026, and data analysis will be performed accordingly. The findings are anticipated to be published in 2027. CONCLUSIONS: This systematic review will provide a consolidated and up-to-date evaluation of the relationship between CVD and cataracts. The findings will highlight the potential importance of integrating cardiovascular risk assessment into routine ophthalmologic care. Continued refinement of study methodologies and standardization of outcome measures may be needed to address observed heterogeneity and strengthen future evidence, ultimately supporting more holistic management of patients with coexisting cardiovascular and ocular conditions.

title: Impact of sarcopenia on clinical outcomes after endoscopic and endovascular interventions for bleeding gastric varices: A multi-center real-world study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The impact of sarcopenia on the clinical outcomes following gastric variceal (GV) hemorrhage in cirrhosis remains unclear. METHODS: 2 2 2 2 We retrospectively analyzed patients with cirrhosis and GV bleeding from six centers in India (January 2017-January 2023). Baseline demographics, further decompensation events-rebleeding, ascites and hepatic encephalopathy (HE) and mortality-were reviewed. Cross-sectional imaging was used to assess skeletal muscle index (SMI). Sarcopenia was defined using gender-specific SMI thresholds (men, < 42 cm/mand women, < 38 cm/m). Competing risk analysis was used to evaluate predictors of rebleeding and further decompensation with mortality as a competing event. RESULTS: Total 318 patients (214 males, 67.3%) were included. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (49/79, 62%) was the leading cause for cirrhosis in patients with sarcopenia. Sarcopenia was associated with higher risk of rebleeding (sHR, 1.62, 95% CI, 1.03-2.52; p = 0.03), further decompensation (sHR, 2.02, 95% CI, 1.43-2.85; p < 0.001) and a one, two and three-year probability of mortality of 15.3%, 24.9% and 41.1% as compared to 9.1%, 14.9% and 14.9% in non-sarcopenic patients. On multi-variate analysis, sarcopenia was an independent predictor of both further decompensation (sHR, 2.03, 95% CI, 1.39-2.97; p < 0.01) and mortality (HR, 1.98, 95% CI, 1.11-3.54; p = 0.020). CONCLUSION: The presence of sarcopenia is a risk factor for further decompensation and mortality after GV hemorrhage in cirrhosis.

title: Immunothrombosis Biomarkers and Multi-Omics Profiles After Successful Recanalization in Patients Receiving Ischemic Postconditioning: An Exploratory Analysis of the INSPIRE Trial.
abstract: Successful recanalization after endovascular thrombectomy does not always restore microvascular perfusion, highlighting the need for adjunctive strategies. Ischemic postconditioning (IPostC) involves brief, controlled​ cycles of flow interruption and restoration at the onset of reperfusion to attenuate ischemia-reperfusion injury. In the parent INSPIRE trial, IPostC, delivered in situ as four cycles of 2-minute balloon inflation followed by 2-minute deflation at the previously occluded arterial segment immediately after successful recanalization, reduced infarct growth from baseline to 48 h. This exploratory secondary analysis included all 60 randomized patients. We investigated whether IPostC was associated with early changes in immunothrombosis, coagulation, and microvascular transit and explored associated plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiles. Arterial blood obtained approximately 15 min after successful recanalization was analyzed using flow cytometry and thromboelastography. Quantitative digital subtraction angiography-derived microcirculation time was analyzed in 55 patients, and plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiling was performed in 29 patients. Compared with controls, patients receiving IPostC had lower neutrophil CD11b expression (median, 52.15 versus 64.27 mean fluorescence intensity ×10²; P = 0.011), a lower thromboelastography α-angle (65.15° versus 67.95°; P = 0.037), and shorter microcirculation time (2.11 versus 3.03 s; P = 0.020). Longer microcirculation time was associated with greater infarct growth (r = 0.533; P < 0.001). Proteomic and metabolomic analyses identified signals involving blood-brain barrier and extracellular-matrix organization and mitochondrial bioenergetics. Biomarker comparisons were not adjusted for multiple comparisons; in the omics analyses, no protein and 17 metabolites remained significant after false discovery rate correction. In summary, IPostC was associated with lower neutrophil activation, slower clot propagation, and faster microvascular transit after recanalization, and multi-omics profiling pointed to blood-brain barrier integrity and mitochondrial bioenergetics as candidate pathways. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger studies. Trial registration: NCT06545734, registered 9 August 2024.

In the parent INSPIRE trial, IPostC, delivered in situ as four cycles of 2-minute balloon inflation followed by 2-minute deflation at the previously occluded arterial segment immediately after successful recanalization, reduced infarct growth from baseline to 48 h.

title: Radiomics performance to identify high-risk carotid artery plaques: a systematic review.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Stroke is a leading cause of mortality worldwide, with 15-20% of ischemic strokes caused by extracranial carotid atherosclerotic disease. Risk stratification has traditionally relied on luminal stenosis severity, which inadequately reflects plaque vulnerability. Radiomics offers an emerging solution by extracting high-dimensional quantitative data from standard medical images. This systematic review evaluated the performance of radiomics-based models for identifying high-risk carotid plaques. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across multiple databases. Studies were included if they developed or validated radiomics-based models for carotid plaque assessment and reported performance metrics, specifically the area under the curve (AUC). Data were extracted on study design, imaging modalities, segmentation methods, and modeling techniques. RESULTS: Twenty-eight studies involving 6,108 patients (72.4% male) were included. Computed tomography angiography was the most commonly used imaging modality (n = 16), and manual region-of-interest segmentation was performed in 27 of 28 studies. Radiomics models showed strong predictive performance. Internal validation AUCs were as high as 0.984, whereas combined models incorporating radiomics with clinical and/or conventional radiological features achieved the best predictive accuracy, often exceeding 0.90. However, only four studies included external validation cohorts. CONCLUSION: Radiomics is a powerful, non-invasive tool for identifying high-risk carotid plaques, offering superior discriminative power over conventional stenosis-based assessments. Despite these promising results, the field faces significant hurdles, and future research must prioritize prospective multicenter trials, the development of automated segmentation workflows, and the correlation of radiomic features with histopathological findings to ensure clinical reproducibility and transition into routine stroke prevention. KEY POINTS: Question Standard carotid atherosclerotic disease assessments fail to capture biological plaque complexity and vulnerability, necessitating objective, reproducible, and non-invasive methods to improve stroke prevention. Findings Radiomics and combined models demonstrate superior capability in identifying high-risk carotid plaques compared to traditional assessments. With four external validations, the field remains exploratory. Relevance statement Radiomics offers a non-invasive tool for personalized stroke prevention. However, technical barriers currently prevent its transition to routine clinical use, including reliance on manual segmentation and low compliance with international standardization guidelines.

title: Radiofrequency ablation with versus without high ligation for primary varicose veins of the great saphenous vein: A comparison of efficacy and outcomes.
abstract: p p p p p p p p p p PurposeThis study compares radiofrequency ablation (RFA) with versus without high ligation (HL) for treating primary varicose veins of the great saphenous vein, assessing differences in surgical efficacy.MethodIn this retrospective cohort study, consecutive patients with lower-extremity varicose veins treated at a single vascular center (July 2023-July 2024) were allocated to RFA (n = 65) or RFA ablation with high ligation (RFA + HL, n = 72). Groups were compared for operative time, blood loss, postoperative pain, hospital stay, symptom relief, and 2-year recanalization and recurrence rates.ResultsBoth RFA and RFA + HL demonstrated favorable therapeutic outcomes, with significant symptom improvement observed in all patients postoperatively. The RFA group demonstrated superior perioperative outcomes, including shorter operative time (60.46 ± 7.89 vs. 65.21 ± 8.28 min,= 0.001), less blood loss (11.92 ± 5.50 vs. 14.46 ± 6.94 mL,= 0.020), lower postoperative VAS scores at 1d and 3d (< 0.01), a shorter hospital stay (2.15 ± 0.67 vs. 2.39 ± 0.64 days,= 0.037), and a lower incidence of impaired wound healing (0.0% vs. 9.7%,= 0.014). In contrast, RFA + HL provided better long-term durability, with significantly lower recanalization rates at both 9-month (1.4% vs. 10.8%,= 0.027) and 12-month (2.8% vs. 12.3%,= 0.047) follow-ups, as well as at 18-month (2.8% vs. 13.8%,= 0.017) and 24-month (4.2% vs. 16.9%,= 0.014) follow-ups. Notably, by 24 months postoperatively, clinical recurrence had occurred in 6 patients (9.2%) in the RFA group but none in the RFA + HL group (= 0.010).ConclusionCompared with RFA alone, the combination of RFA and HL for treating GSV incompetence was associated with a longer operative time and a higher risk of incision-related complications in the groin. However, the combined procedure demonstrated a lower venous recanalization rate at the 1-year follow-up, suggesting superior long-term durability of GSV closure.

title: Molecular biomarkers associated with progression and adverse outcomes in human ascending thoracic aortic aneurysm: a systematic review protocol.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This systematic review will identify, classify, and synthesize evidence on molecular biomarkers (circulating, tissue, genetic, epigenetic, proteomic, metabolomic, and inflammatory) associated with the progression and outcomes of ascending thoracic aortic aneurysm (ATAA) in human populations. INTRODUCTION: ATAA is a heterogeneous condition driven by genetic, epigenetic, inflammatory, proteolytic, and metabolic alterations that are not completely understood. Current management relies mainly on aortic diameter and does not incorporate molecular data. Emerging evidence suggests that circulating, tissue, genetic, epigenetic, metabolic, and proteomic biomarkers may support diagnosis, improve prognostic assessment, identify high-risk patients, and clarify mechanisms of medial degeneration. Existing studies are fragmented and inconsistent, and are based on small observational cohorts, highlighting the need for a rigorous synthesis. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: This review will include observational studies that quantify molecular biomarkers in blood or biopsy samples from adult populations with ATAA. METHODS: We will search PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Scopus, Web of Science, trial registries, dissertations and theses databases, preprint repositories, and other gray literature sources for eligible evidence from 2015 to the present. Study selection, critical appraisal, and data extraction will follow the JBI methodology. A narrative synthesis will summarize the findings. Where sufficient clinical and methodological homogeneity exists, meta-analysis will be conducted using random-effects models. The certainty of evidence will be assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach adapted for prognostic and etiological research. REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420251237933.

title: Shockwave Lithotripsy for Severe Calcified Extracranial Vertebral and Carotid Disease Treated With Percutaneous Stenting.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients harboring heavily calcified concentric or eccentric type lesions in the carotid or vertebral artery pose a challenge in placing a stent to reduce the lesion. These lesions yield suboptimal results due to poor stent expansion. Shockwave lithotripsy offers a potential solution for achieving luminal gain. METHODS: We present a retrospective study of all patients at our institution who were treated with lithotripsy for extracranial carotid or vertebral artery stenosis associated with heavily calcified lesions from July 2022 to February 2026. Data were maintained in our procedural database and retrospectively analyzed for patients treated with lithotripsy. All consecutive patients were analyzed for demographic information, procedural data, perioperative complications, and 6-month midterm follow-up imaging for restenosis. RESULTS: A total of 41 patients (8 vertebral artery lesions and 33 carotid lesions) were treated with intravascular lithotripsy at our institution between July 2022 and February 2026. The mean age for the cohort was 70.7 ± 8.7. The mean lesion pretreatment for the carotid stenosis was 77 ± 13% and for the vertebral artery treated patients 81 ± 11%. All patients were successfully treated with stenting and lithotripsy, and the mean stenosis posttreatment was 15 ± 14% for the carotid stenosis and 8 ± 5% for the vertebral artery lesions. There were 2 groin complications (5%) with femoral artery pseudoaneurysms treated with thrombin injection and 1 perioperative stroke (3%) secondary to a dissection in the carotid stent cohort. CONCLUSIONS: The current study demonstrates the feasibility of lithotripsy for heavily calcified lesions treated with transfemoral stenting. Future prospective core laboratory adjudicated studies are warranted to determine the efficacy of this technique.

These lesions yield suboptimal results due to poor stent expansion. Shockwave lithotripsy offers a potential solution for achieving luminal gain.

title: Association Between Hypoperfusion Intensity Ratio and Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy in Posterior Circulation Stroke: A Retrospective Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The prognostic utility of the hypoperfusion intensity ratio (HIR) in posterior circulation stroke is undefined. We investigated the association between pretreatment HIR and outcomes after mechanical thrombectomy for acute posterior circulation large vessel occlusion. METHODS: This post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION (Endovascular Treatment for Acute Basilar Artery Occlusion)/ATTENTION-IA (Intra-Arterial Tenecteplase After Successful Endovascular Recanalisation in Patients With Acute Posterior Circulation Arterial Occlusion) trials included patients with posterior circulation occlusion who underwent mechanical thrombectomy and had baseline computed tomography perfusion. HIR (Tmax>10 s/ Tmax>6 s volume) was analyzed. Functional independence (modified Rankin Scale score, 0-2) at 90 days was the primary outcome. RESULTS: P P Among 139 patients, higher HIR (per 0.1 increment) was independently associated with lower odds of 90-day modified Rankin Scale score of 0 to 2 (adjusted odds ratio, 0.643 [95% CI, 0.422-0.979];=0.039). However, its discriminative ability was the modest (area under the curve, 0.617 [95% CI, 0.521-0.712]). The established anterior circulation cutoff (HIR<0.4) did not predict outcomes (=0.115). CONCLUSIONS: Elevated HIR is independently associated with worse 90-day outcomes after posterior circulation mechanical thrombectomy, but its overall prognostic utility is limited, and the anterior circulation threshold (0.4) could not be validated in this underpowered analysis, highlighting circulation-specific pathophysiological differences.

We investigated the association between pretreatment HIR and outcomes after mechanical thrombectomy for acute posterior circulation large vessel occlusion. title: Percutaneous and endovascular procedures in adrenal disease: indications, technique, and outcomes.
abstract: Adrenal masses are found on roughly 4-5% of abdominal imaging studies, and the proportion rises with age. Most are benign, non-functioning adenomas that need imaging characterization and hormonal screening but no intervention. The remainder, comprising metastases, adrenocortical carcinoma, pheochromocytoma and hormonally active adenomas, raise questions that computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging cannot always settle; in these cases image-guided procedures can help. Percutaneous biopsy is reserved for hormonally inactive lesions whose benignity imaging has not established and whose histology would change management. Adrenal venous sampling remains the reference method for lateralizing aldosterone excess in primary aldosteronism and therefore decides who is offered adrenalectomy, although success depends heavily on operator experience and local protocol. Thermal ablation has produced biochemical and blood-pressure responses in selected aldosterone-producing adenomas and local control of limited metastases, but the evidence is largely nonrandomized and does not establish equivalence with surgery. Transarterial embolization serves three purposes: hemostasis in adrenal hemorrhage, devascularization before resection of hypervascular tumors, and functional treatment of aldosteronism, now supported by one small randomized trial. Each procedure carries hazards peculiar to the gland (catecholamine crisis, adrenal insufficiency after bilateral treatment, non-target embolization) that shape patient selection and periprocedural monitoring. This review covers indications, technique, outcomes and complications for each. Surgery remains the treatment of choice for most operable patients. Interventional radiology is most useful when the indications for sampling, ablation or embolization are recognized early and discussed at the multidisciplinary meeting, not only after surgery has been declined.

title: [Chinese clinical practice guidelines for transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt in portal hypertension (2026 edition)].
abstract: Portal hypertension (PH) is one of the major complications of cirrhosis. Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) is a primary therapeutic modality for complications of portal hypertension, including variceal bleeding and refractory ascites, by establishing an intrahepatic channel between the hepatic vein and the portal vein. TIPS also serves as a bridging therapy for patients with decompensated cirrhosis awaiting liver transplantation. In 2019, the Chinese College of Interventionalists (CCI) issued the Chinese Clinical Practice Guidelines for TIPS in portal hypertension, which have played an important role in standardizing TIPS practice in China. With advances in TIPS techniques, evolving treatment concepts, and the emergence of new high-level evidence, the CCI has revised and updated these guidelines. This updated clinical practice guideline was developed by more than 30 Chinese experts in the field of TIPS application, including specialists in interventional radiology, hepatobiliary surgery, hepatology, and gastroenterology. The recommendations are based on latest evidence, supplemented by relevant domestic expert consensuses and high-quality clinical studies. This guideline provides up-to-date recommendations for TIPS treatment of portal hypertension, with the aim of improving the quality of TIPS clinical practice in China.

Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) is a primary therapeutic modality for complications of portal hypertension, including variceal bleeding and refractory ascites, by establishing an intrahepatic channel between the hepatic vein and the portal vein. TIPS also serves as a bridging therapy for patients with decompensated cirrhosis awaiting liver transplantation.

title: 3-Year Comparison of Sirolimus- Versus Paclitaxel-Coated Balloon Angioplasty in Femoropopliteal Artery Disease: The SIRONA Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sirolimus-coated balloons (SCBs) have emerged as alternatives to paclitaxel-coated balloons (PCBs), but randomized comparative data beyond 2 years are lacking. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare patient-reported outcomes, effectiveness, and safety through 3 years in symptomatic femoropopliteal artery disease. METHODS: SIRONA was a prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial comparing SCB angioplasty with a PCB strategy. Patients were randomized 1:1 after successful predilation. Prespecified 3-year outcomes included walking capacity, health-related quality of life, clinically driven target lesion/vessel revascularization (cdTLR/cdTVR), mortality, major amputation, and amputation-free survival. RESULTS: Among 482 randomized patients (SCB, n = 238; PCB, n = 244), 96.3% had intermittent claudication; 3-year follow-up was completed by 76.5% and 79.6%, respectively. Changes in patient-reported walking distances did not differ between-groups. Three-year freedom from cdTLR was 88.2% (95% CI: 83.1%-91.9%) versus 80.2% (95% CI: 74.1%-85.0%; HR: 0.60, 95% CI: 0.36-0.97; nominal log-rank P = 0.03). Post-hoc analysis suggested time-varying treatment effects (treatment-by-period interaction P = 0.006), with separation after the first year. Freedom from cdTVR (HR: 0.78, 95% CI: 0.50-1.21; nominal P = 0.27) and amputation-free survival (HR: 1.09, 95% CI 0.57-2.09; nominal P = 0.79) did not differ. CONCLUSIONS: Through 3 years, no between-group differences were observed in walking capacity and health-related quality of life or clinical safety outcomes between SCB angioplasty and the PCB strategy. Three-year freedom from cdTLR was higher with SCB angioplasty, with treatment effect that varied over time. Given the exploratory, nonmultiplicity-adjusted 3-year analysis, the cdTLR difference requires confirmation.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare patient-reported outcomes, effectiveness, and safety through 3 years in symptomatic femoropopliteal artery disease. METHODS: SIRONA was a prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial comparing SCB angioplasty with a PCB strategy.

title: Resuscitation and 30-day postoperative mortality in acute type A aortic dissection: A cohort study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Patients with acute type A aortic dissection who experience cardiopulmonary arrest require cardiopulmonary resuscitation before definitive repair, but the prognostic relevance of its duration is unclear. We evaluated the association between resuscitation duration and early mortality after emergency surgery. METHODS: In this retrospective two-centre study, we included all adults who underwent emergency surgery for acute type A aortic dissection. The exposure was the combined preoperative and intraoperative duration of resuscitation until return of spontaneous circulation or initiation of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation or cardiopulmonary bypass, categorised a priori as none, <15 min or ≥ 15 min. Multilevel proportional hazards models and competing-risks regression, with multiple imputation of missing covariates, were used. RESULTS: Of 880 patients, 815 (92.6%), 13 (1.5%), and 52 (5.9%) received no resuscitation, resuscitation for <15 min and resuscitation for ≥15 min, respectively (median recorded duration 29 min, interquartile range 15-43). Thirty-day mortality was 81/815 (9.9%), 3/13 (23.1%) and 42/52 (80.8%), respectively. Resuscitation for ≥15 min was associated with higher 30-day mortality (adjusted hazard ratio 9.59, 95% confidence interval 4.28-21.45; P < 0.001), whereas the estimate for resuscitation for <15 min was imprecise (adjusted hazard ratio 1.68, 95% confidence interval 0.46-6.13; P = 0.43). CONCLUSIONS: Among patients selected for emergency surgery for acute type A aortic dissection, combined preoperative and intraoperative resuscitation for ≥15 min was associated with higher 30-day mortality, and the risk increased with resuscitation duration. These findings provide prognostic information rather than a criterion for withholding surgery.

title: Same-day multiple-cannulation: A promising alternative method for establishing buttonhole tracks in hemodialysis patients-A multicenter randomized controlled trial.
abstract: AIM: This study evaluated a novel same-day cannulation method for creating buttonhole tracks in arteriovenous fistulas of chronic hemodialysis patients. METHOD: Patients were randomized: the control (C) group had one sharp needle cannulation per dialysis, while the intervention (I) group had 4-6 cannulations during the first session to establish the BH track. The primary outcome was 1-year BH survival. Secondary outcomes included pain scores (numeric rating scale); sessions needed to create a BH track, and 1-year AV fistula failure and BH infection rates. RESULTS: BH survival and infection rates did not significantly differ between groups. The I-group had lower pain scores and required fewer sessions for track formation compared to the C-group. CONCLUSION: While the same-day cannulation method did not impact BH survival or infection rates, it improved patient comfort and reduced track formation time, potentially simplifying care for chronic hemodialysis patients. title: 125 Endovascular brachytherapy usingI seeds strand combined with transarterial chemoembolization, lenvatinib, and camrelizumab for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma with hepatic vein tumor thrombus.
abstract: PURPOSE: 125 To evaluate the safety and efficacy of Iodine-125(I) seed strand implantation in combination with transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), lenvatinib, and camrelizumab for the treatment of unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC) with hepatic vein tumor thrombus (HVTT). METHODS AND MATERIALS: 125 From January 2020 to December 2023, 76 uHCC patients with HVTT were included in this single-center retrospective study. Thirty-six patients underwentI seed strand implantation combined with TACE, lenvatinib, and camrelizumab (group A), whereas 40 patients received TACE combined with lenvatinib and camrelizumab (group B). Outcome measures comprised with technique success rate, overall response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), overall survival (OS) time, progression-free survival (PFS) time, and adverse event occurrence rate. RESULTS: 125 The technique was successfully performed in all patients. The mean intended dose (r, irradiation range = 10 mm; z, irradiation duration = 240 days) was 64.0 ± 0.3 Gy. No grade 3 or 4 adverse events related toI seed strand implantation occurred in group A. The ORR and DCR of HVTT were significantly higher in group A compared with group B (ORR, 72.2% vs. 15.0%, p < 0.001; DCR, 88.9% vs. 35%, p < 0.001). And the median OS time and PFS time were significant longer in group A compared with group B (OS, 22.1 ± 2.4 vs. 14.0 ± 1.7 months, p < 0.001; PFS, 17.6 ± 0.3 vs. 8.0 ± 0.6 months, p < 0.001). In the multivariate Cox regression analysis, treatment regimen was an independent prognostic factor for OS. No serious complications related to interventional treatment, including acute hepatic failure, liver abscess, intraperitoneal bleeding, and radiation hepatitis was observed. CONCLUSIONS: 125 I seeds strand combined with TACE, lenvatinib, and camrelizumab as the treatment strategy for uHCC patients with HVTT is safe and effective.

title: Evaluating the SVS 90-Minute Door-to-Intervention Target for Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm: A Single-Centre Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms (rAAAs) are a life-threatening condition requiring rapid surgical intervention for survival. Guidelines from the Society of Vascular Surgery in 2018 advised a door-to-intervention time of ≤90 minutes. We hypothesised that door-to-intervention time would not predict outcomes following rAAA repair, as treatment timelines may reflect differences in physiological severity, diagnostic assessment and operative modality, including the use of EVAR. METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of 29 patients presenting to University Hospitals Plymouth (UHP) who underwent surgical intervention for rAAA between February 2018 and December 2024. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients achieving the SVS-recommended door-to-intervention time of ≤90 minutes. Secondary outcomes were the rates of endovascular repair (EVAR) compared to open repair and the associated mortality and morbidity. RESULTS: Twenty-nine patients were included, of whom only three (10.3%) met the SVS target. Median door-to-intervention time was 182 minutes. Arrival-to-diagnosis time was associated with the greatest delay, with a median time of 84 minutes. Twenty-three patients (79.3%) underwent open repair, with a 60.9% (14/23) mortality rate compared to 16.7% (1/6) for EVAR cases. Shorter door-to-intervention time was associated with higher 30-day mortality, although no association was observed with overall mortality. Morbidity rates were 95.6% (22/23) for open cases and 50.0% (3/6) for EVAR cases. No statistically significant association was identified between overall morbidity rates and door-to-intervention time. However, higher grade complications were statistically significantly associated with both shorter arrival to diagnosis time (p=0.011) and shorter arrival to knife-to-skin time (p=0.039). CONCLUSIONS: 89.7% (26/29) of rAAAs presenting to UHP between February 2018 and December 2024 exceeded the recommended SVS door-to-intervention target of <90 minutes. Shorter timelines were observed among patients with higher grade complications and who subsequently died. Mortality was higher following open repair.

title: Clinical and economic burden of major lower-limb amputations attributable to peripheral artery disease in Italy: A nationwide analysis.
abstract: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) represents a major cause of non-traumatic lower-limb amputation and is associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Despite advances in medical and revascularization therapies, major amputations remain frequent, and comprehensive nationwide estimates of their clinical and hospital-related economic burden within the Italian National Health Service (SSN) are limited. The objectives of this study were to estimate the hospital-related economic burden of major lower-limb amputations attributable to PAD in Italy and to assess revascularization patterns and in-hospital mortality within the SSN. We conducted a nationwide observational study using the Italian National Hospital Discharge Database. Acute hospital discharges between 2015 and 2021 with a major lower-limb amputation and Diagnosis Related Group 113 were identified. Inpatient volumes, length of stay, and costs were estimated by amputation level. A longitudinal cohort of patients amputated between 2015 and 2017 was followed for two years before and after the index hospitalization to assess prior revascularization and in-hospital mortality using age- and sex-adjusted Cox models. A total of 26,417 PAD-attributable major amputations were identified, 75.6% of which were above-knee procedures. Cumulative inpatient expenditure reached €294 million, corresponding to over 511,000 hospital days. Only 46.0% of patients underwent revascularization before amputation. In-hospital mortality increased steeply within the first six months post-amputation and remained higher after above-knee procedures and among patients with diabetes, reaching 16-25% at 180 days and 23-34% at two years. Major lower-limb amputation remains a severe and costly outcome of PAD in Italy. Improved implementation of guideline-recommended PAD management is needed to reduce avoidable amputations and their economic burden on the SSN.

title: Venous thromboembolism after breast cancer surgery: incidence, predictive factors and outcomes in 270,564 patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Breast cancer surgery is generally considered to be low risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE). However, when VTE occurs, it may lead to severe complications and increased mortality. This study aimed to determine the incidence, predictors, and clinical impact of postoperative VTE following breast cancer surgery using a large, multicenter surgical database. METHODS: The American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP) database (2008-2023) was queried to identify female patients undergoing surgery for breast cancer without concurrent reconstruction. Patients were stratified according to postoperative VTE occurrence. Demographics, comorbidities, laboratory values, operative characteristics, and 30-day outcomes were compared. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of VTE and to construct a predictive model, which was internally validated using bootstrap resampling. RESULTS: Among 270,564 patients included, 465 (0.2%) developed postoperative VTE. Of these, 247 (53.1%) had deep vein thrombosis, 177 (38.1%) pulmonary embolism, and 41 (8.8%) both. Patients who developed VTE were older, had higher body mass index (BMI), greater comorbidity burden, and longer operative times (all p < 0.001). They also demonstrated lower preoperative serum albumin, hematocrit, prothrombin time, and albumin-to-creatinine ratio. VTE was associated with significantly longer hospital stays, increased rates of reoperation and readmission, and a more than 20-fold higher crude 30-day mortality (1.9% vs. 0.1%) (all p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, increasing age (OR 1.26 per 10 years), BMI (OR 1.17 per 5 kg/m²), congestive heart failure (OR 2.43), metastatic cancer (OR 2.05), lower serum albumin (OR 0.63 per 1 g/dL), and longer operative duration (OR 1.09 per 30 min) were independently associated with postoperative VTE. Compared with partial mastectomy, total mastectomy (OR 2.58), modified radical mastectomy (OR 2.22), and radical mastectomy (OR 2.80) were associated with significantly higher odds of postoperative VTE. The predictive model demonstrated acceptable discrimination (AUC 0.717; optimism-corrected 0.700) and good calibration. Age, BMI, congestive heart failure, metastatic cancer, mastectomy and operative time remained associated with VTE in all sensitivity analyses. CONCLUSION: Postoperative VTE following breast cancer surgery is uncommon but associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Advanced age, obesity, cardiac comorbidity, metastatic disease, hypoalbuminemia, longer operative duration, and greater surgical extent were independently associated with increased thromboembolic risk. Awareness of these risk factors may support individualized perioperative risk assessment and thromboprophylaxis decisions, as recommended by current consensus guidance, and facilitate earlier recognition of postoperative VTE. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

This study aimed to determine the incidence, predictors, and clinical impact of postoperative VTE following breast cancer surgery using a large, multicenter surgical database.

title: Functional outcomes and quality of life after endovascular thrombectomy in large and extensive infarcts (ASPECTS 0-5): a multicentre registry study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) is established for large infarcts, but remains cautiously applied in extensive infarcts with an Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) of 0-2. Real-life outcome data remain limited. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Retrospective analysis of the German Stroke Registry-Endovascular Treatment comparing extensive (ASPECTS 0-2) and large infarcts (ASPECTS 3-5) in patients with anterior-circulation occlusion and EVT. The primary outcome was the ordinal 90-day mRS distribution; secondary outcomes were mRS 0-3, survival, quality of life (3-level European Quality of Life-5 Dimensions) and living condition. RESULTS: Of 18,069 screened patients, 889 were analysed (ASPECTS 1-2, n = 89; ASPECTS 3-5, n = 800); none had ASPECTS 0. With ASPECTS 1-2, 20.2% achieved mRS 0-3 and 55.1% died within 90 days. In the model including successful reperfusion, no statistically significant association was detected between infarct group and the 90-day mRS distribution (common odds ratio [cOR] 0.80; 95% CI, 0.53-1.23) or mRS 0-3 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.89; 95% CI, 0.64-1.25), whereas successful reperfusion was associated with both (cOR 3.68; 95% CI, 2.31-5.85 and aOR 4.10; 95% CI, 2.45-6.86). Among survivors, median European Quality of Life-5 Dimensions utility index was 0.445 vs 0.541 (n = 27/324), and 51.5% vs 50.9% lived at home (n = 33/411). DISCUSSION: An extensive infarct carried a challenging prognosis, yet acceptable outcome and non-institutional living remained achievable in a relevant minority. An independent association of infarct group with outcome was not detected. CONCLUSION: An acceptable outcome remained attainable in selected patients with extensive infarction, particularly after successful reperfusion. Lacking a medically managed comparator, these data describe prognosis rather than treatment effect.

title: Hypoxia Paradox in Middle Meningeal Artery Embolization for Chronic Subdural Hematoma: A Mechanistic Framework for Treatment Resistance.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The clinical efficacy of middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) in chronic subdural hematoma (CSDH) is increasingly established; yet, recent landmark randomized controlled trials consistently report only a 30% to 50% reduction in recurrence, implying that middle meningeal artery occlusion alone does not fully resolve the pathological microenvironment of the outer hematoma membrane. The mechanistic basis of this incomplete treatment response remains undefined. METHODS: To develop a mechanistic framework for this clinical paradox, we performed a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses-compliant systematic review. Of 876 records identified across PubMed, Embase, and ClinicalTrials.gov, 47 underwent full-text review and 18 studies (16 clinical studies and 2 registry records) published through October 2025 were included, integrating clinical outcomes with pathological and molecular insights. A secondary analysis of a publicly available single-cell RNA sequencing data set of normal human dural tissue was performed to map the cellular infrastructure underlying key molecular drivers. RESULTS: CSDH progression is driven by an interconnected triad of inflammatory infiltration, pathological angiogenesis, and vascular hyperpermeability within the outer hematoma membrane. While MMAE suppresses these pathogenic programs by reducing middle meningeal artery-derived arterial supply, we propose that occlusion-induced ischemic stress may paradoxically stabilize hypoxia-inducible factor 1α, triggering compensatory angiogenesis in cases of incomplete devascularization, a mechanism we formally term the "hypoxia paradox". Secondary single-cell RNA sequencing analysis identified fibroblast-like and endothelial dural populations as the primary cellular platforms for this response, providing a translational cellular basis for the proposed framework. CONCLUSION: The hypoxia paradox represents a testable mechanistic hypothesis, offering a coherent explanation for heterogeneous MMAE outcomes and generates specific, testable predictions regarding post-MMAE molecular signatures in the outer hematoma membrane. Prospective paired tissue sampling integrated with multimodal molecular analyses is essential to validate this model and advance CSDH management toward individualized, mechanism-guided therapy.

The mechanistic basis of this incomplete treatment response remains undefined. METHODS: To develop a mechanistic framework for this clinical paradox, we performed a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses-compliant systematic review.

title: Transcatheter coil embolization for proximal thoracic aortic pseudoaneurysms: a case series with mid-term clinical and imaging follow-up.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Proximal aortic pseudoaneurysms represent a life-threatening complication of cardiac surgery. Traditional redo surgery is associated with substantial operative risk, while conventional endovascular stenting is often precluded by complex anatomy. We evaluated the clinical feasibility, safety, and durability of transcatheter coil embolization for proximal aortic pseudoaneurysms in a high-risk cohort. METHODS: Between September 2020 and February 2024, nine consecutive high-risk patients with proximal aortic pseudoaneurysms underwent transcatheter coil embolization at our institution. Preoperative risk profiles, procedural characteristics, intra-hospital outcomes, and serial computed tomography angiography follow-up datasets were retrospectively analyzed. RESULTS: The cohort was predominantly male (88.9%), with a mean age of 69.1±13 years and a mean Logistic EuroSCORE of 22.82%±18.76%. Patients had undergone a mean of 2.56 previous aortic procedures. Access routes included transfemoral (n = 6), transapical (n = 3), axillary (n = 1), and transbrachial (n = 1) approaches. Stent-assisted embolization was deployed in two cases. Technical success was achieved in all cases, with a median post-procedural stay of six days. Mean follow-up was 16±14.8 months. Serial imaging demonstrated stable sac dimensions in all patients, with no local recurrences. All-cause mortality was 33.3% (n = 3), and all deaths were attributed to sudden systemic events unrelated to target lesion failure or rupture. CONCLUSIONS: Transcatheter coil embolization appears to be a safe, technically feasible, and durable alternative for the exclusion of proximal aortic pseudoaneurysms. In this small high-risk cohort, the technique achieved excellent local control and mid-term structural stability in fragile, multi-operated patients who were not candidates for conventional open surgery.

title: Utilizing evidence-based diagnosis and treatment for central venous thrombosis: closing the gaps where guidelines fail.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Catheter-related thrombosis (CRT) is a frequent complication of central venous catheters and accounts for most upper extremity deep vein thrombosis events. Despite its increasing clinical burden, management remains poorly standardized because recommendations are largely extrapolated from general venous thromboembolism studies rather than CRT-specific evidence. AREAS COVERED: We performed a structured comparative review of major international, European, and North American guidelines, consensus documents, and position statements identified through PubMed, Ovid, and Scopus searches covering January 2016 to March 2026. Nineteen documents from vascular medicine, oncology, and vascular access societies were included. Recommendations on diagnostic strategies, imaging modalities, catheter management, anticoagulant selection, treatment duration, and invasive interventions were systematically compared. EXPERT OPINION: Considerable heterogeneity persists across recommendations. Ultrasound is consistently endorsed as the first-line imaging modality, whereas the role of clinical prediction scores and D-dimer remains uncertain because neither has been validated in CRT populations. Catheters should be preserved when functional, correctly positioned, and free from infection. Anticoagulation for at least 3 months is universally recommended, while invasive procedures should be reserved for selected patients with extensive thrombosis or life- or limb-threatening complications. Prospective studies are urgently needed to validate diagnostic algorithms, optimize anticoagulant strategies, and develop CRT-specific evidence-based pathways.

title: Electrosurgical Septotomy Across the Full Spectrum of Aortic Dissection.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Transcatheter electrosurgical septotomy divides the dissection membrane to reconstitute a single aortic lumen. Reported experience is largely confined to chronic post-dissection aneurysms. We assessed the technique across the full spectrum of descending aortic dissection, including stand-alone treatment of malperfusion. METHODS: A retrospective intention-to-treat analysis of 21 consecutive patients scheduled for septotomy between June 2022 and May 2026. The membrane was crossed by needle re-entry and divided with an electrified through-and-through guidewire at 40-60 W under fluoroscopy, without routine intravascular ultrasound or image fusion. A perfused-lumen index (perfused lumen divided by total aortic diameter) was measured before and after the procedure. RESULTS: Septotomy was performed in 20 of 21 patients (technical success 95% on an intention-to-treat basis). Indications were landing-zone preparation (57%), malperfusion (33%), preparation for open repair, and true-lumen collapse. Malperfusion resolved in all 7 patients treated for that indication, and the perfused-lumen index rose from a median of 0.16 to 0.98 (18 patients, P < .001). There was no stroke, spinal cord ischaemia, or retrograde type A dissection. Thirty-day, in-hospital, and overall mortality were 10%, 14%, and 19%, respectively, with 1 fatal delayed aortic rupture and no intraprocedural death. Three unplanned reinterventions occurred; median follow-up was 5.1 months. CONCLUSIONS: Electrosurgical septotomy was feasible across the full spectrum of aortic dissection and, in selected patients, as stand-alone treatment for malperfusion, using standard electrosurgical equipment. Given the small, heterogeneous cohort and short follow-up, these findings demonstrate feasibility rather than durability.

title: Development and Validation of a Nomogram for Predicting Preoperative Venous Thromboembolism in Patients With Lower Extremity Fractures: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: p = BackgroundPatients with lower extremity fractures (LEF) are at high risk of preoperative venous thromboembolism (VTE). However, existing risk assessment models are not specifically developed and validated for this population.ObjectiveTo develop and validate a prediction model for preoperative VTE in emergency LEF patients, and to compare the performance of traditional logistic regression (LR) with that of machine learning (ML) algorithms.DesignRetrospective cohort study.SettingPeking University Shenzhen Hospital, China.Participants486 patients with LEF admitted between January 2022 and July 2025.MethodsTwo modeling strategies were compared: 1) a traditional LR nomogram using backward stepwise selection, and 2) nine ML algorithms with Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO)-based feature selection. Model performance was evaluated using discrimination (area under the curve, AUC), calibration, classification metrics (accuracy, sensitivity, specificity) and decision curve analysis.ResultsOf 486 enrolled patients, 79 (16.3%) developed preoperative VTE. Among the ML models, LASSO-LR and multilayer perceptron (MLP) achieved the highest validation AUCs (0.709 each), the best calibration and highest net benefit. The traditional LR nomogram showed an identical AUC of 0.709 (95% CI: 0.691-0.718), with superior calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow0.738, calibration intercept = -0.109, slope = 0.921) and better stability. Therefore, this simple five-predictor traditional LR nomogram, incorporating age ≥ 65 years, hemoglobin, glucose, external immobilization, and pre-injury anticoagulant or antiplatelet use, was selected as the optimal model.ConclusionThe traditional LR nomogram appears promising for preoperative VTE risk prediction in LEF patients. External validation is warranted before clinical implementation.

title: SERPINE1 IntegratingGenotype With Clinical Indicators Improves Venous Thromboembolism Risk Prediction in Cancer Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study From Xinjiang.
abstract: SERPINE1 SERPINC1 PROC MTHFR F5 F2 SERPINE1 P SERPINE1 ObjectiveTo develop and validate a venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk prediction model integrating genetic polymorphisms and routine clinical indicators in a cohort of cancer patients from Xinjiang, China.MethodsA retrospective study was conducted on 1135 cancer patients (179 with VTE, 956 without) at Affiliated Cancer Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University between March 2024 and May 2025. Six gene polymorphisms (,,,,,) and clinical predictors were assessed. Chi-square tests and logistic regression identified independent predictors for model construction. Model performance was evaluated using ROC analysis, and three clinically optimized cut-off values were defined.ResultsThe4G allele was identified as a strong genetic risk factor for VTE (4G/4G genotype: OR=2.330, 95%CI: 1.378-3.942; 4G/5G genotype: OR=2.399, 95%CI: 1.411-4.078). No significant associations were found for the other five genes. Age (OR=1.022, 95%CI: 1.008-1.037), D-dimer level (OR=1.288, 95%CI: 1.186-1.399), and hemoglobin level (OR=0.987, 95%CI: 0.979-0.995) were independent clinical predictors (<0.01). The combined model achieved an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.769 (95%CI: 0.731-0.807). Three optimized cut-off values were derived for different clinical contexts: high-sensitivity (90.5%), balanced (Youden index 0.434), and high-specificity (90.1%).ConclusionThe4G allele independently predicts VTE risk in this cohort of cancer patients from Xinjiang. A prediction model integrating this genetic marker with age, D-dimer, and hemoglobin demonstrates good discriminatory performance. The three derived cut-off values may facilitate risk-stratified thromboprophylaxis in clinical practice; however, these findings are based on a retrospective, single-center cohort and internally validated only by ROC analysis.

title: [Aortic root replacement with a stentless xenograft (Freestyle®) in Iceland - indications and outcome].
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Aortic root replacement (ARR) can be performed with a stentless porcine xenograft (Freestyle®) as an alternative to the conventional Bentall-procedure, where mechanical or stented bioprosthetic are sewn into a wov-en tube-graft. We examined early and late outcomes of Freestyle®-ARR in a whole-nation cohort, focusing on indications and surgical outcomes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective analysis that included 44 consecutive Freestyle®-ARR performed at Landspitali 2002-2018. Primary outcomes were 30-day and long-term survival (Kaplan-Meier), with a median follow-up of 111 months. Secondary outcomes included early postoperative complications and late reoperations. RESULTS: A median of three cases was performed per year (range 0-5). The most common indication was dilated aortic root (70%), followed by Type-A aortic dissection (9%) and small aortic annulus during aortic valve replacement (9%). Average age was 62 years and 65% were male. Median EuroSCORE-II was 11% (range 3-71%), cardiopulmonary bypass time 234 min. and cross-clamp time 157 min. The most common postoperative complications were new-onset atrial fibrillation (51%) and perioperative myocardial infarction (14%). Postoperative length of stay was 12 days median and 30-day mortality 14% (n=6). At follow-up, 1- and 5-year survival rates were 81% and 74%, respectively. For patients surviving the first 30 days, 5-year survival was 86%, and at long-term follow-up only three patients (7%) had undergone reoperation. CONCLUSIONS: Freestyle®-ARR is a technically challenging operation and is associated with high short-term mortality rates compared with regular AVR. However, long term survival was favourable, and reoperations were uncommon in those surviving to discharge.

title: Venous thromboembolism after joint arthroplasty: where do we stand with aspirin?
abstract: Venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total joint arthroplasty remains heterogeneous, particularly regarding the role of aspirin within modern fast-track pathways. Although aspirin is widely used in North American arthroplasty practice, European guidelines remain more conservative and often provide limited or non-operational recommendations for its use after total hip and knee arthroplasty. Contemporary evidence supports aspirin as a viable prophylactic option in selected patients, with potential advantages related to its safety profile, cost, ease of administration and reduced treatment burden. The clinical role of aspirin should be interpreted within a risk-stratified framework that accounts for thromboembolic risk, bleeding risk, surgical complexity, early mobilization and duration of prophylaxis. Available evidence, including recent randomized data, supports aspirin-based prophylaxis in appropriately selected patients, both as part of sequential strategies and, increasingly, as monotherapy within contemporary fast-track pathways. This scoping review synthesizes current guideline-level evidence and contemporary clinical data to clarify practical considerations for agent selection, dosing, duration and aspirin-based prophylaxis after total joint arthroplasty.

title: Trends and determinants of peripartum blood transfusions.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Blood transfusion is critical in mitigating blood loss during delivery, but the epidemiology of peripartum blood transfusion in the United States is not fully understood. The objective of this study was to estimate trends in peripartum blood transfusions, including severe hemorrhage, and identify transfusion risk factors. STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: A retrospective cohort was assembled from the Recipient Epidemiology and Donor Study IV Pediatric (REDS-IV-P) database, which includes a network of hospitals and blood centers across four U.S. regional hubs. This included in-hospital deliveries ≥24 weeks gestation from 2019 to 2024, with the outcome being any peripartum (within ±7 days of delivery) blood product transfusion. Bayesian Model Averaging (BMA) was used to examine associations. RESULTS: There were 158,322 deliveries, with transfusion occurring in 4246 (11% were severe hemorrhage). Overall incidence of transfusion increased from ~2% early in the study period to ~3% in later years (p < 0.001). The odds of peripartum transfusion were higher for deliveries where patients had an underlying hemoglobinopathy (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] [95% confidence interval; CI] aOR = 3.35 [2.65, 4.24]), venous thromboembolism (aOR = 3.25 [2.47, 4.26]), received hemostatic factor (aOR = 10.30 [9.58, 11.06]), mechanical ventilation (aOR = 13.91 [8.76, 22.11]), or hysterectomy (aOR = 13.68 [9.86, 18.96]). CONCLUSION: Peripartum transfusions are increasing across the REDS-IV-P hubs and are associated with underlying medical-obstetric risk factors such as bleeding disorders and hemoglobinopathies. Our findings support the importance of early prenatal healthcare and identification of conditions that may help prevent peripartum hemorrhage and associated transfusions.

title: Early and Long-Term Outcomes of Carotid Endarterectomy in Patients With Carotid Near-Occlusion Versus Preocclusive Carotid Stenosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The clinical role of carotid endarterectomy (CEA) in patients with carotid near-occlusion (CNO) remains a subject of ongoing debate, and comparative data regarding its long-term efficacy versus preocclusive carotid stenosis is limited. This study aimed to evaluate and compare the perioperative and long-term outcomes of CEA in these two distinct subsets of high-grade carotid disease. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on a prospectively maintained database of 1775 consecutive CEAs performed at a single center between January 2014 and September 2025. The study cohort included 81 procedures for CNO (Group 1) and 144 for preocclusive carotid stenosis > 95% with distal lumen recovery (Group 2). CNO was defined by distal internal carotid artery caliber reduction and further stratified by the presence of full distal collapse. RESULTS: Results showed that patients in Group 2 were significantly older than those in Group 1 (76 ± 8 vs. 72 ± 8 years; p < 0.001). Symptomatic presentation was more frequent in Group 1 (35.8% vs. 24.3%; p = 0.06), and concordant ipsilateral ischemic brain lesions were significantly more common in CNO patients (24.5% vs. 9%; p = 0.001). Regarding perioperative safety, no 30-day deaths or major neurologic events occurred in Group 1, while Group 2 had a 30-day stroke/death rate of 3.4% (p = 0.08 vs. Group 1). During a median follow-up of 30 months (range 1-140), the estimated 6-year overall survival was 84% for Group 1% and 73% for Group 2 (p = 0.1). Notably, ipsilateral stroke at 6 years occurred in 0% of CNO patients compared with 8.5% in the preocclusive group (p = 0.03). Stroke-free survival at 6 years was 84% in Group 1% and 71% in Group 2 (p = 0.09). While freedom from restenosis was comparable (78.5% vs. 86.3%; p = 0.2), late carotid occlusion was significantly more frequent in the CNO group (6% vs. 0%; p = 0.02). CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center series, patients undergoing CEA for carotid near-occlusion demonstrated favorable perioperative safety and a lower observed incidence of long-term ipsilateral stroke during follow-up compared with those treated for preocclusive stenosis, even in the presence of full distal collapse. The absence of a medically managed control group and the small number of events made these findings hypothesis-generating. However, the higher incidence of late restenosis and occlusion in near-occlusion highlights the importance of a personalized, intensified postoperative surveillance, particularly for patients with full distal collapse.

title: A comparison of the efficacy and safety of direct oral anticoagulants with low molecular weight heparin for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total hip arthroplasty : a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: AIMS: To evaluate differences in the efficacy and safety of low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) used for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after elective total hip arthroplasty (THA). METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis reviewed MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL from conception to 13 December 2025, for any randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing the efficacy (VTE risk) and safety (bleeding risk) of LMWH and DOACs after elective THA. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) of VTE, bleeding, reoperation, and mortality risks were assessed. RESULTS: A total of 22 RCTs involving 28,112 participants were included. The risk of VTE in the DOAC group was lower compared with the LMWH group (OR 0.62 (95% CI 0.47 to 0.82); p = 0.002), driven by a reduction in deep vein thrombosis (DVT) risk (OR 0.60 (95% CI 0.42 to 0.86); p = 0.008). The findings remained consistent in the subgroup analysis restricted to anticoagulants and dosages licensed for use in the UK. Overall bleeding risk was higher in the DOAC group (OR 1.19 (95% CI 1.03 to 1.38); p = 0.023), but no difference was seen when comparing only UK-licensed anticoagulants and doses (OR 1.06 (95% CI 0.95 to 1.18); p = 0.279). Reoperation risk (OR 1.21 (95% CI 0.75 to 1.93); p = 0.351) and mortality (OR 1.03 (95% CI 0.46 to 2.33); p = 0.937) did not differ between groups. CONCLUSION: DOACs reduce the risk of VTE and DVT following elective THA compared with LMWH without increasing bleeding risk, for UK-licensed agents and doses. Switching to DOACs could save the NHS £8.6 million per year. New clinical trials are needed to compare the safety and efficacy of UK-licensed DOACs and LWMH with modern postoperative rehabilitation protocols.

title: Effectiveness of Tomazoni Measurement Method for Central Catheter Tip Positioning in Neonates: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Accurate peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC) tip positioning in neonates remains challenging, with high rates of malposition reported using traditional measurement methods. AIM: To evaluate the effectiveness of the Tomazoni method for PICC positioning in neonates compared with the traditional method. STUDY DESIGN: Pragmatic, parallel-group randomised clinical trial with stratified block randomisation, conducted in a neonatal intensive care unit in Brazil between June 2024 and April 2025. RESULTS: Of 62 randomised procedures, 55 were evaluable (27 in the experimental group, 28 in the control group). Central positioning was achieved in 21 of 27 procedures (77.8%) in the experimental group versus 5 of 28 (17.9%) in the control group (p < 0.001). PICC insertion procedures assessed using the Tomazoni method were 4.36 times more likely to achieve central tip placement (RR = 4.36; 95% CI: 1.91-9.88). Catheter withdrawal was required in 3 of 27 procedures (11.1%) in the experimental group versus 16 of 28 (57.1%) in the control group (p = 0.001; RR = 0.19; 95% CI: 0.06-0.59). CONCLUSIONS: The Tomazoni measurement method was associated with substantially higher rates of central PICC tip positioning and reduced need for catheter withdrawal compared with the traditional method. RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: The Tomazoni method offers a reproducible, low-cost measurement strategy that can be implemented in neonatal intensive care units to improve catheter positioning accuracy and reduce procedure-related manipulations, with potential implications for patient safety. The trial, titled 'Comparison between measurements of peripherally inserted central catheters in children and newborns', was registered in the Brazilian Clinical Trials Registry under the identifier RBR-55zwb45. TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial is registered in the Brazilian Clinical Trials Registry (ReBEC) under the identifier RBR-55zwb45.

title: Reducing Central Line-Associated Bloodstream Infections in ICUs: A Systematic Review of Barriers and Facilitators and Intervention Measures.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite established guidelines, central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI) remains a severe ICU complication due to cognitive and resource barriers hindering healthcare worker compliance. A systematic evaluation of these barriers and facilitators is currently lacking but is important for informing targeted implementation strategies for CLABSI prevention. AIMS: To explore the barriers and facilitators to implementing CLABSI prevention in ICUs using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) to provide evidence-based strategies for improvement. STUDY DESIGN: A PRISMA-guided systematic review was performed using PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, VIP, Wan fang, and CBM databases, up to August 2026. Eligible studies included qualitative, quantitative, or mixed-methods research on the barriers and facilitators to CLABSI prevention implementation among ICU healthcare workers. Two researchers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed quality using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Data synthesis and intervention development were guided by the CFIR, with targeted strategies mapped using the CFIR-ERIC (Expert Recommendations for Implementing Change) matching tool. RESULTS: The literature search identified 1,780 records, of which 28 studies were ultimately included. The review identified 28 barriers and facilitators, which were synthesized into four major themes and mapped to 16 CFIR constructs across the catheter-care continuum. The most prominent barriers involved staff knowledge gaps, inconsistent adherence to recommended practices, limited resources, and insufficient leadership support. CFIR-ERIC mapping identified 11 Level 1 expert-endorsed implementation strategies, of which four were represented in the included literature and seven were identified as potential implementation gaps. CONCLUSIONS: CLABSI prevention in ICUs is influenced by multilevel implementation determinants spanning individual, organizational, and practice-related factors. A structured implementation-science approach may help healthcare organizations identify context-specific barriers and prioritize targeted strategies to support more consistent implementation of evidence-based CLABSI prevention practices. RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Improving CLABSI prevention may require multilevel strategies that combine targeted education and training, adequate resource allocation, leadership engagement, standardized clinical procedures, and ongoing audit and feedback. These strategies may help strengthen adherence to evidence-based practices, improve quality of care, and enhance patient safety in ICUs.

title: [The Heart Team as a multidisciplinary approach to the management of patients eligible for surgical and transcatheter treatment of aortic valve disease - Consensus document].
abstract: Aortic valve disease, particularly severe symptomatic aortic stenosis, represents a growing public health problem due to the aging population. The increasing complexity of managing this condition - driven by the evolution of surgical and transcatheter techniques and the expansion of treatment indications - requires a multidisciplinary organizational model capable of ensuring quality and safety of care. This consensus document, jointly developed by AGENAS and the leading Italian scientific societies involved in the management of valvular heart disease, defines the principles for the implementation and functioning of the Heart Team as a central element of the decision-making process for patients undergoing evaluation for surgical aortic valve replacement or transcatheter aortic valve implantation. The document describes the composition, responsibilities, and operational procedures of the Heart Team, highlighting the importance of multidisciplinary assessment, patient-tailored treatment, shared decision-making with the patient, and outcome monitoring. The aim is to promote a standardized organizational model across the country, aligned with the scientific evidence and the most recent international guidelines, thereby contributing to improved clinical outcomes and greater efficiency of the Italian National Health Service.

title: [Abdominal aortic aneurysms: diagnosis, risk stratification and treatment strategies].
abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm is defined as a focal aortic dilation ≥3.0 cm in maximum diameter, with rupture-associated mortality approaching 80%. Anatomical classification identifies infrarenal (80%), juxtarenal, pararenal and suprarenal aneurysms. Operative thresholds are 5.5 cm in men and 5.0 cm in women. Endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) provides an early survival benefit, with 30-day mortality of 1.8% vs 4.3% for open repair in the EVAR-1 trial, and substantially comparable long-term outcomes up to 15 years of follow-up, at the cost of a 15-20% reintervention burden and the need for lifelong imaging surveillance. Accordingly, the 2024 European Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines consider EVAR as the preferred treatment in most patients with favorable anatomy, reserving open repair for young patients with long life expectancy, unfavorable anatomy and specific conditions such as connective tissue disease, inflammatory aneurysms, graft infection and failed previous endovascular repair. Treatment selection should be based on the integrated assessment of individual operative risk, aortic anatomy and life expectancy.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Apixaban Thromboprophylaxis According to Baseline Chemotherapy Class in High-Risk Ambulatory Cancer Patients: A Post Hoc Analysis of the AVERT Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in cancer patients. The AVERT trial showed apixaban thromboprophylaxis reduced VTE in intermediate-to-high-risk patients initiating chemotherapy. However, the efficacy and safety of apixaban according to baseline chemotherapy class remain incompletely characterized. METHODS: We conducted a post hoc analysis stratified by chemotherapy class of the randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled AVERT trial comparing apixaban (2.5 mg twice daily) with placebo in ambulatory cancer patients initiating chemotherapy. The primary efficacy outcome was VTE, and the primary safety outcome was clinically relevant bleeding (major or clinically relevant non major bleeding (CRNMB)) per ISTH criteria. A subgroup analysis compared platinum-based with non-platinum chemotherapy. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CI), adjusted for age, sex, and study site. Treatment-by-platinum interaction terms were used to assess effect modification by platinum exposure. RESULTS: A total of 563 patients were included and categorized by one or more chemotherapy classes at randomization. Compared with placebo, apixaban appeared to reduce VTE in patients on platinum (HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.16-0.57), taxane (HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.23-0.75), taxane-platinum (HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.12-0.68), topoisomerase inhibitor (HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.19-0.53), and antimetabolite regimens (HR 0.25, 95% CI 0.12-0.54), without increased bleeding. Among placebo-treated patients, platinum-based chemotherapy was associated with a higher risk of VTE compared with non-platinum regimens (HR 2.25, 95% CI 1.48-3.42), whereas no statistically significant difference was observed among apixaban-treated patients. Treatment-by-platinum interaction testing did not demonstrate significant effect modification by platinum exposure. CONCLUSION: In this exploratory, hypothesis-generating analysis, apixaban thromboprophylaxis was associated with reduced VTE across several chemotherapy regimens with generally acceptable safety outcomes. Patients receiving platinum-based chemotherapy may derive greater absolute benefit from thromboprophylaxis in the setting of higher underlying thrombotic risk.

The AVERT trial showed apixaban thromboprophylaxis reduced VTE in intermediate-to-high-risk patients initiating chemotherapy. However, the efficacy and safety of apixaban according to baseline chemotherapy class remain incompletely characterized.

title: COLLATERAL EMBOLIZATION IN THE ENDOVASCULAR TREATMENT OF PORTAL CAVERNOMA CHOLANGIOPATHY: A POTENTIAL CAUSE OF SEVERE BILIARY OBSTRUCTION.
abstract: Management of complicated portal cavernoma cholangiopathy (PCC) remains nonstandardized. When biliary drainage fails, portal vein recanalization with transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (PVR-TIPS) is increasingly considered and may require collateral embolization during the procedure. This work describes two patients with complicated PCC in whom collateral embolization during or after PVR-TIPS caused severe biliary obstruction requiring long-term biliary drainage. A narrative review was conducted, identifying 18 published studies describing patients with PCC who underwent endovascular treatment. Collateral embolization was inconsistently reported, and its biliary consequences were rarely described. Severe biliary obstruction following peribiliary collateral embolization may therefore be an underrecognized complication; however, its incidence remains unknown based on the available literature. Thus, when collateral embolization is considered during endovascular treatment of PCC, its potential biliary risk should be weighed, and the anatomical relationship between the targeted collaterals and the bile duct carefully assessed.

title: Stent Configurations in Aortoiliac Occlusive disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate which endovascular stent configuration at the aortic bifurcation offers superior outcomes for aorto-iliac occlusive disease (AIOD). METHODS: Studies reporting outcomes for endovascular reconstruction for AIOD, for TransAtlantic Inter-Society Consensus (TASC) C and D lesions were included in the review. Data for primary, primary-assisted and secondary patency were extracted (full-text articles or reconstructed from published Kaplan Meier curves). RESULTS: This review included 12 studies, including 1027 patients (177 Covered Endovascular Reconstruction of the Aortic Bifurcation (CERAB), 850 kissing stent). Most studies were retrospective cohort studies with moderate methodological quality. Median follow-up was 20 months for primary patency, and 48 months for assisted and secondary patency. CERAB and kissing stent techniques showed similar primary patency (p=0.24). Primary-assisted patency was slightly lower for CERAB but not statistically significant (p=0.051). Secondary patency favored CERAB (p=0.045). At two years, CERAB had primary patency of 90%, primary-assisted patency of 87%, and secondary patency of 100%. Kissing stents showed primary patency of 91%, primary-assisted patency of 92%, and secondary patency of 96%. CONCLUSION: Both stent types yielded positive results, but current data does not favor one configuration. Current studies on this topic are low quality. At present, the method of endovascular intervention for AIOD could be left to clinical expertise, although hemodynamic studies may provide insights. Randomized trial data or post-market registries are needed to ascertain superiority of any stent configuration in this disease process.

title: Three working windows posterior midline approach for posterior column tibial plateau fractures.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Isolated posterior column tibial plateau fractures with combined posteromedial and posterolateral compression are challenging because conventional posterior approaches limit instrument trajectories and reduction vectors for distinct posterior fragments. METHODS: Ten patients with isolated posterior column tibial plateau fractures accompanied by combined posteromedial and posterolateral compression were treated using a posterior midline skin incision organized into three working windows. The central window served as the foundational posterior corridor, with medial and lateral windows developed as functional extensions to facilitate region-specific reduction and fixation. Relevant clinical data and outcomes were retrospectively analyzed. RESULTS: Postoperative radiographs of all 10 patients showed satisfactory joint reduction and alignment. Radiographic fracture union was achieved in all cases at a mean of 13.9 weeks, with a mean follow up of 11.8 months. At final follow up, mean knee flexion was 124.0°, and mean knee extension was -2.1°, and the mean Hospital for Special Surgery (HSS) knee score was 90.8 points. One patient developed a superficial wound infection that resolved with antibiotic treatment, and one patient experienced deep vein thrombosis that was successfully treated with anticoagulation therapy. No neurovascular injuries, deep infections, or fixation failures were observed during follow up. CONCLUSION: A posterior midline approach organized into three working windows may provide a feasible option for selected isolated posterior column tibial plateau fractures with combined posteromedial and posterolateral compression, allowing region-specific posterior fixation through a single posterior skin incision.
