title: Intraoperative Measurement of Internal Carotid Artery Blood Flow Using Transit-Time Flowmetry After Carotid Endarterectomy: Results from 196 Consecutive Cases.
abstract: Background/Objectives Methods Results Conclusions p p : Carotid endarterectomy (CEA) is a standard surgical treatment for high-grade symptomatic and asymptomatic internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis. The Transit Time Flowmeter (TTF) provides an easy-to-use tool to quantify intraoperative ICA blood flow in mL/min. This study aimed to (1) describe post-CEA ICA flow quantified with TTF, (2) identify predictors of post-CEA ICA flow, and (3) examine its association with contralateral steno-occlusive disease.: We queried data from our prospective registry of patients who underwent a CEA between January 2019 and July 2024 and had intraoperative registered post-CEA ICA flow measurements using TTF. Preoperative ICA stenosis was graded according to the NASCET criteria. The clinical data was retrospectively collected.: Data from 196 CEAs in 190 patients (median age 74 [67-81]; 25% female) were included. Most patients (86%) had a symptomatic ICA stenosis. The median post-CEA ICA flow was 170 mL/min [IQR 140-242; range 40-800]. Post-CEA ICA flow was not associated with age, sex, comorbidities, symptomatic stenosis, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), or ipsilateral stenosis severity but was significantly higher in patients requiring intraluminal shunt placement during CEA (= 0.010) as well as in those with contralateral steno-occlusive disease (< 0.001).: TTF is a practical intraoperative tool for quantitative flow assessment during CEA. Higher post-CEA ICA flow in patients with an intraoperative shunt placement or with contralateral steno-occlusive disease may reflect a compensatory hyperperfusion, as the ipsilateral ICA serves as a key supplier when collateral pathways are incomplete.

title: Aspirin-Based Thromboprophylaxis Versus Anticoagulant Regimens After Total Hip or Knee Arthroplasty: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
abstract: Background and Objectives Materials and Methods Results Conclusions : Aspirin is widely used for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total hip arthroplasty (THA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA); however, uncertainty remains regarding its efficacy and safety compared with anticoagulant regimens. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated aspirin-based thromboprophylaxis versus anticoagulant regimens following THA or TKA.: PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched through July 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing aspirin-based prophylaxis with anticoagulant regimens. The primary outcomes were any deep vein thrombosis (DVT), symptomatic DVT, and symptomatic venous thromboembolism (VTE). Secondary outcomes included pulmonary embolism (PE), proximal and distal DVT, bleeding outcomes, wound complications, blood transfusion, and mortality. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models. Additional risk-difference sensitivity analyses incorporated CRISTAL's published cluster-adjusted estimates.: Sixteen trials involving 21,265 participants were included. Aspirin was associated with higher risks of symptomatic DVT (RR 1.79, 95% CI 1.35-2.38), symptomatic VTE (RR 1.70, 95% CI 1.33-2.18), PE (RR 1.89, 95% CI 1.33-2.68), and distal DVT (RR 1.47, 95% CI 1.06-2.06). Aspirin was associated with lower risks of minor bleeding (RR 0.47, 95% CI 0.31-0.71) and ecchymosis or bruising (RR 0.60, 95% CI 0.39-0.93). No statistically significant differences were detected for the other assessed outcomes. Additional analyses incorporating CRISTAL's cluster-adjusted risk differences did not identify statistically significant differences for the three primary outcomes or PE.: The main pooled analyses associated aspirin-based thromboprophylaxis with higher risks of symptomatic thromboembolic events. However, the symptomatic DVT and symptomatic VTE associations were no longer statistically significant after exclusion of CRISTAL or restriction to trials at low risk of bias. The low-risk analysis identified a significantly higher risk of any DVT with aspirin. Aspirin reduced minor bleeding and bruising without a statistically significant reduction in major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding. These findings require cautious interpretation given dependence on CRISTAL, sensitivity to trial inclusion and analytical approach, and differences in prophylactic strategies and outcome definitions.

title: The effect of renal denervation on blood pressure in patients with chronic kidney disease (RDN-CKD Study): Results of a multicentre, prospective, randomized, sham-controlled and blinded investigator-initiated trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Endovascular ultrasound renal denervation (uRDN) offers the opportunity to modulate sympathetic nervous system activity, thereby lowering blood pressure (BP) and potentially improving or stabilizing renal outcomes. OBJECTIVE: We hypothesized that in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 3 and uncontrolled hypertension, endovascular ultrasound-based RDN will lower BP after 6 months. METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, randomized, sham-controlled, blinded, clinical trial, investigated the effects of uRDN or sham in patients with CKD stage 3 and uncontrolled hypertension. The primary and secondary endpoints were changes in ambulatory BP (ABP) and office BP at 6 months. The study was prematurely stopped due to slow enrollment. RESULTS: Twenty subjects (uRDN: N = 10, sham: N = 10) completed the 6-month visit. At 6 months, the sham-corrected change from baseline in 24 h systolic ABP was -5.60 mmHg (95% CI -10.7, -0.54 mmHg; P = 0.170). The sham corrected change from baseline in 24-h diastolic ABP was -5.90 mmHg (95% CI -9.25, -2.55; P = 0.035) and from baseline daytime ABP -6.85 mmHg (95% CI -10.6, -3.08; P = 0.030). Sensitivity analysis restricting the analysis to those patients who were fully adherent to medication (N = 7 in each group) found a sham-corrected change from baseline 24-h diastolic ABP of -5.71 mmHg (95% CI -9.40, -2.03; P = 0.053) at 6 months. Based on the composite endpoint of 24 h ABP and office BP for systolic/diastolic BP, a win ratio of 1.71 (95% 1.26-2.34; P = 0.014) was found for systolic BP and a win ratio of 4.59 (95% CI 2.94-7.16, P < 0.001) was found for diastolic BP, indicating significant changes in BP following RDN. Estimated glomerular filtration rate remained stable over 6 months, with no difference between the groups. There were no safety signals associated with uRDN. CONCLUSIONS: This prospective randomized, sham controlled, blinded trial in patients with uncontrolled hypertension and CKD was prematurely stopped, resulted in small number of patients and we did not find a statistically significant effect on systolic BP, whereas a consistent reduction in diastolic BP following uRDN was observed. These data should guide the design of a larger confirmatory trial in patients with CKD.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Endovascular ultrasound renal denervation (uRDN) offers the opportunity to modulate sympathetic nervous system activity, thereby lowering blood pressure (BP) and potentially improving or stabilizing renal outcomes. OBJECTIVE: We hypothesized that in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 3 and uncontrolled hypertension, endovascular ultrasound-based RDN will lower BP after 6 months. METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, randomized, sham-controlled, blinded, clinical trial, investigated the effects of uRDN or sham in patients with CKD stage 3 and uncontrolled hypertension.

title: Challenges of Conducting a Feasibility Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial During COVID-19 Restrictions: Rivaroxaban Versus Acetyl Salicylic Acid in Patients with Multiple Myeloma on Lenalidomide-Based Therapy (RithMM).
abstract: Venous thromboembolism is a serious medical complication with an increased risk in patients with multiple myeloma undergoing combination treatment regimens. Acetylsalicylic acid is routinely used as a method of thromboprophylaxis in multiple myeloma patients treated with lenalidomide, and rivaroxaban has been assessed in small-scale studies in multiple myeloma patients treated with immunomodulatory drugs; yet, no study has compared the two methods. In this pilot, we asked if a full-scale trial would be feasible to assess the benefits of rivaroxaban over acetylsalicylic acid as a thromboprophylactic approach. This pilot recruited patients with multiple myeloma on lenalidomide-based therapy and randomized them to either low-dose acetylsalicylic acid or rivaroxaban, then monitored bleeding and thrombotic events throughout lenalidomide-dexamethasone treatment. A total of 55 patients were recruited across three Canadian centres, with two venous thromboembolic events and two bleeding events, all in the acetylsalicylic acid arm. We conducted a post hoc analysis of active recruitment time as a definition of recruitment feasibility, as we did not achieve our pre-defined feasibility goals. Despite the challenges in enrollment, possibly due to social restrictions during the COVID-19 pandemic, we maintain that a full-scale trial is feasible and offers insight into thromboprophylactic management in this population.

title: Risk factors and clinical outcomes of reocclusion after endovascular treatment for acute ischemic stroke: an updated systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Early reocclusion after endovascular treatment (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is underrecognized; its determinants and impact remain poorly defined. METHODS: Random-effects meta-analysis of early reocclusion after successful EVT (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library through January 2026). Crude odds ratios (ORs) were pooled and certainty rated with GRADE. Post hoc sensitivity analyses included only same-site reocclusion definitions. RESULTS: Ten studies (3,381 patients) were included; 244 (7.2%) reoccluded. Reocclusion was associated with lower 90-day functional independence (OR 0.25, 95% CI 0.17-0.38) and higher mortality (OR 1.86, 1.29-2.68), both moderate certainty. Reocclusion was more frequent with large-artery atherosclerosis (OR 2.24, 1.41-3.55; same-site 3.04, 1.73-5.33) and less frequent with cardioembolism (OR 0.40, 0.28-0.57) and atrial fibrillation (OR 0.39, 0.26-0.59), mutually confounded associations reflecting one embolic-versus-atherothrombotic axis. Prestroke antiplatelet therapy (OR 0.43, 0.28-0.67) lost significance under the same-site definition (0.60, 0.31-1.16). Exploratory data (two cohorts) linked eTICI 2c-3 reperfusion with less reocclusion (OR 0.44, 0.28-0.69). No study reported when etiology was adjudicated; the atherosclerosis association may be partly outcome-induced. CONCLUSIONS: Early reocclusion is uncommon but carries a substantial prognostic penalty. Its determinants appear to lie in the vascular substrate rather than thrombectomy technique; prospective studies with uniform same-site definitions and systematic follow-up imaging are needed.

METHODS: Random-effects meta-analysis of early reocclusion after successful EVT (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library through January 2026). Crude odds ratios (ORs) were pooled and certainty rated with GRADE.

title: De-escalated rivaroxaban in postoperative isolated distal deep vein thrombosis: a propensity score-matched study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In postoperative isolated distal deep vein thrombosis (IDDVT), anticoagulation intensity is frequently constrained by bleeding risk, which may compromise treatment continuity and clinical effectiveness. OBJECTIVES: To compare the effectiveness and safety of a de-escalated (rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily) versus standard-maintenance rivaroxaban regimen for postoperative IDDVT in a real-world surgical cohort. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients diagnosed with IDDVT following urological surgery between 2013 and 2025. Patients received rivaroxaban at either a low maintenance dose (10 mg once daily) or a standard maintenance dose (20 mg once daily) according to routine clinical practice. Propensity score matching (1:1) was applied to balance baseline characteristics, incorporating surgical approach (endoscopic vs. major structural procedures) as a surrogate for surgical trauma and bleeding risk. The primary outcome was thrombus progression to proximal deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism. Secondary outcomes included IDDVT resolution and clinically relevant non-major bleeding (CRNMB). Competing-risk analyses were performed. RESULTS: P P P After matching, 152 patients were included (76 per group). Thrombus progression did not differ significantly between groups (subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR] 1.29; 95% CI 0.48-3.46; = 0.613). No statistically significant difference in IDDVT resolution was detected between the two groups (SHR 0.93; 95% CI, 0.64-1.36; = 0.721). The low-dose regimen was associated with a significantly lower risk of CRNMB (HR 0.31; 95% CI, 0.11-0.85; = 0.023) and fewer early bleeding-related treatment interruptions. Early postoperative hematuria was more frequent in the standard-dose group. CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center retrospective cohort of patients with isolated distal deep vein thrombosis after urological surgery, low-dose rivaroxaban (10 mg once daily) was associated with a lower incidence of clinically relevant non-major bleeding than 20 mg once daily. No statistically significant differences were detected between regimens in thrombus progression or complete thrombus resolution. However, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalent antithrombotic efficacy, given nonrandomized treatment allocation, residual confounding, limited sample size, and wide confidence intervals for thrombotic outcomes. The results are hypothesis-generating and support studies-preferably randomized non-inferiority trials-to determine whether dose de-escalation can provide an acceptable balance between thrombotic protection and bleeding risk in postoperative patients.

title: Perioperative prothrombin time activity trajectories and subsequent mortality after surgical repair of acute type A aortic dissection.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Perioperative prothrombin time activity (PTA) changes rapidly during surgical repair of acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD), but single measurements do not capture heterogeneous longitudinal patterns. We sought to identify recurring perioperative PTA trajectories, characterize their clinical context, and examine their association with subsequent all-cause mortality. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 284 adults who underwent ATAAD repair from 2021 through 2023. Group-based trajectory modeling used the last preoperative and observed postoperative day (POD) 1-7 PTA measurements. Patients required at least three observed PTA measurements for trajectory modeling. Mortality analyses began immediately after POD7. The primary Cox model adjusted for age and sex; Firth regression addressed sparse events. Incremental information beyond last preoperative PTA was evaluated by a prespecified likelihood-ratio comparison. RESULTS: P P P P P The trajectory cohort comprised 268 patients with 1,895 observations and 27 deaths after POD7. Four perioperative PTA trajectory groups were identified: moderate-stable [87 (32.5%)], low-declining [50 (18.7%)], preserved-rapidly-declining [61 (22.8%)], and high-preserved [70 (26.1%)]. Cumulative mortality differed globally (log-rank = 0.00210), and trajectory group remained associated with subsequent mortality in the age- and sex-adjusted Cox model (global = 0.0322) and Firth sensitivity analysis (global = 0.0481). The prespecified direct low-declining-versus-preserved-rapidly-declining comparison did not demonstrate a clear difference. Adding trajectory group to age, sex, and last preoperative PTA did not show clear incremental information (likelihood-ratio = 0.304; Firth = 0.380). After exclusion of mechanical-valve recipients, the principal trajectory structure was largely preserved, although this sensitivity analysis did not exclude treatment-related effects on PTA. CONCLUSION: Four reproducible perioperative PTA trajectories characterized distinct longitudinal patterns and were associated with mortality after the POD7 landmark. These trajectories should be interpreted as composite perioperative patterns reflecting both disease and treatment context rather than as intrinsic coagulation states. They were not ordered mortality-risk tiers and did not show clear incremental prognostic information beyond last preoperative PTA. External validation is required.

We sought to identify recurring perioperative PTA trajectories, characterize their clinical context, and examine their association with subsequent all-cause mortality. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 284 adults who underwent ATAAD repair from 2021 through 2023.

title: Comparison of ultrasound-guided oblique-axis versus short-axis approaches for right internal jugular vein cannulation in the left decubitus position: a prospective, randomized, single-center trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Central venous cannulation in the left decubitus position is more difficult than in the supine position and may be required when patients cannot safely return to supine. Whether the oblique-axis (OA) approach improves the success and safety of right internal jugular vein (RIJV) cannulation compared with the short-axis (SA) approach remains unknown. METHODS: Seventy-four patients (ASA I-III) scheduled for elective surgery in the left decubitus position under general anesthesia requiring RIJV cannulation were randomly assigned 1:1 to the OA or SA group (n = 37 each). Under real-time ultrasound guidance and a 20° Trendelenburg tilt, cannulation was performed by one of three experienced attending anesthesiologists, each with more than 15 years of experience in ultrasound-guided central venous cannulation. Venipuncture attempts and total procedure time were recorded by a separate investigator; patients were blinded by general anesthesia. The primary outcome was first-time puncture success; secondary outcomes were overall cannulation success, procedure time, venipuncture attempts, and mechanical complications. RESULTS: All 74 randomized patients completed the trial and were analyzed. The first-time puncture success rate was higher in the OA group (27/37 [73.0%] vs. 18/37 [48.6%]; risk difference 24.3%, 95% CI 2.8% to 45.9%; P = 0.032, Pearson chi-square test; Fisher exact test P = 0.056). Venipuncture attempts were fewer in the OA group (median 1 vs. 2; IQR 1-2; P = 0.037). Total procedure time did not differ significantly between groups (median 2.79 [IQR 2.46-3.19] vs. 3.01 [2.72-3.45] min; P = 0.060). Mechanical complications occurred in 6 of 37 patients (16.2%) in the SA group (one arterial puncture and five posterior wall penetrations) and in none in the OA group (P = 0.025); overall cannulation success was 100% in both groups. CONCLUSIONS: For RIJV cannulation in the left decubitus position, the oblique-axis approach was associated with a higher first-time puncture success rate than the short-axis approach and with fewer mechanical complications detected during or immediately after the procedure; however, the primary-endpoint evidence was borderline and the complication estimates were imprecise. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400091385; registered 28 October 2024).

title: The Impact of Multiple Biologic Failures on Surgical Outcomes: A Retrospective Cohort Study of Elective Subtotal Colectomy for Ulcerative Colitis.
abstract: Background: Methods: Results: Conclusions: p p p p p Subtotal colectomy (STC) with end ileostomy (EI) is usually the first surgical stage for patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) who fail medical treatment, most often with biological agents. Is there a difference in surgical outcome after failure of one or two biologicals vs. three or four?A retrospective study of all patients who underwent STC with EI for UC (5-2018 to 1-2022). After excluding emergent cases, the elective cohort was divided into patients who failed 1-2 biologicals (group 1-2) vs. patients who failed 3-4 biologicals (group 3-4), and surgical outcomes were compared. Data collected included patients' demographics, preoperative clinical manifestations, and operative and postoperative outcomes.Ninety-eight patients underwent STC for UC, and of them, 53 were elective. Thirty patients failed 1-2 biologics (group 1-2), and 23 failed 3-4 biologics (group 3-4). The groups were similar in average age (37.6 ± 11 vs. 32.7 ± 10), BMI (26.7 ± 6 vs. 27.7 ± 7), number of years with UC (9.5 ± 9 vs. 9 ± 8), rate of steroid dependence (20 (67%) vs. 13 (57%)) but differed in sex; there were 25 (83%) males in group 1-2, and 8 (35%) in group 3-4 (< 0.01). The operative approaches were similar, as was the operative time (217 ± 74 vs. 210 ± 79 min). The length of hospital stay was 3.2 ± 1 days for group 1-2 and 5 ± 6 days for group 3-4 (= 0.14). Postoperative complications were seen in 10 patients (33%) vs. 7 patients (30%) (= 0.82), and of them, two (7%) and two (9%) (= 0.82) had Venous thromboembolism (VTE), respectively. Only 20 patients (67%) in group 1-2 and 16 patients (70%) in group 3-4 (= 0.82) progressed to a second stage of an Ileoanal pouch (IPAA) at 11.1 ± 4 and 9.2 ± 2 months, respectively. The overall average follow-up time was 41.1 months.Ulcerative Colitis patients who fail 3-4 biological agents and choose to go to elective STC with EI have very similar surgical outcomes compared to patients who choose elective surgery after failing only 1-2 biological agents in the same time span of known disease. UC patients with severe colitis and poor quality of life who fail two lines of biological agents may be better off electing surgical treatment than failing more biologics and then going to surgery. On the other hand, patients who try 3-4 biologics may expect no worse surgical outcomes than after 1-2 biologics.

title: Chronic Venous Disease in Pregnancy: Pathophysiology, Diagnostic Pitfalls, and a Trimester-Stratified Management Framework-A Narrative Review.
abstract: Chronic venous disease (CVD) in pregnancy is common, poorly codified, and interpreted with diagnostic thresholds, severity instruments and treatment algorithms all derived outside pregnancy. This narrative review synthesises the mechanistic, epidemiological, diagnostic and therapeutic literature, keeping pregnancy-specific evidence separate from evidence extrapolated from non-pregnant populations. Gestational change is characterised principally by increased venous capacitance and vein-wall distension; ambulatory venous hypertension was not demonstrated in the two pregnancy studies assessing it; and new reflux develops in a minority, undetectable postpartum in the one study reporting it. Physiological adaptation, CVD and thrombotic pathology overlap clinically, deep vein thrombosis and superficial vein thrombosis being at once the principal differential diagnoses and potential complications. Management is correspondingly conservative: compression relieves symptoms but has not been shown to prevent varicose veins, routine initiation of venoactive drugs is not supported, and intervention is deferred other than in exceptional circumstances. A venous finding first detected in pregnancy warrants postpartum reassessment before it is taken for established disease. A trimester-stratified framework spanning preconception to late postpartum reassessment is proposed; it is evidence-informed rather than prospectively validated, and is not a guideline.

title: Coenzyme Q10 for Acute Stanford Type A Aortic Dissection: Protocol for a Prospective, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Single-Center Feasibility Trial.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: Acute Stanford type A aortic dissection (TAAD) is a catastrophic cardiovascular emergency. Emergency surgery is the standard life-saving treatment, but some patients decline operative repair, and no established pharmacological therapy has been shown to stabilize acute TAAD. Preclinical work by our team implicates mitochondrial dysfunction and smooth muscle cell phenotypic switching in aortic dissection and suggests that coenzyme Q10 may reduce dissection-related injury. This study aims to determine the feasibility of a future definitive randomized trial and to obtain preliminary safety and exploratory efficacy information.This prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, single-center feasibility trial will enroll 60 adults with CTA-confirmed Stanford type A aortic dissection within 24 h of symptom onset who decline emergency surgical repair after standard surgical counseling. Participants will be randomized 1:1 to oral coenzyme Q10 100 mg three times daily or matched placebo for 14 days, in addition to the same guideline-directed supportive medical care. The primary feasibility outcome is recruitment feasibility, defined as randomization of 60 participants within 12 months after recruitment initiation. Secondary feasibility outcomes include treatment adherence, follow-up completion, dropout, missingness, outcome-assessment feasibility, and candidate endpoint event rates. The primary exploratory clinical outcome is 14-day all-cause mortality; additional exploratory outcomes include aortic rupture death, false-lumen thrombosis, cardiac tamponade, worsening pericardial effusion, and organ malperfusion syndromes. Safety outcomes include adverse events, serious adverse events, adverse drug reactions, suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions, and prespecified laboratory indices.The trial is designed to establish whether recruitment, blinded treatment delivery, follow-up, outcome collection, and safety monitoring are operationally feasible and to provide estimates for planning a larger confirmatory trial.This feasibility trial will inform the design and conduct of future definitive evaluation of coenzyme Q10 in acute TAAD. Trial registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2600123230.

title: Safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System in acute intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism: the SPIRARE II pivotal trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Percutaneous aspiration thrombectomy can rapidly reduce afterload in acute pulmonary embolism (PE), but catheter stiffness and instability may limit access and prevent effective right ventricle (RV) unloading. The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System with Transforming Fixation (TFX) technology is designed to address current limitations of existing catheter-based systems by separating the flexibility necessary for safe navigation from the support that is essential for procedural control. AIMS: We aimed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System for mechanical aspiration thrombectomy in acute intermediate-risk PE. METHODS: SPIRARE II was a prospective, single-arm, multicentre pivotal investigation conducted at 19 sites in the United States and Europe. Eligible patients had acute PE (≤14 days), a computed tomography angiography-assessed RV to left ventricle (RV/LV) ratio>0.9, and haemodynamic stability (systolic blood pressure ≥90 mmHg). Co-primary endpoints were composite major adverse events (MAE) within 48 hours and core laboratory-assessed RV/LV change from baseline to 48 hours. Prespecified secondary endpoints were collected immediately pre- and post-procedure in all patients including mean pulmonary artery pressure, total pulmonary vascular resistance, and cardiac index. RESULTS: In 123 patients, the 48-hour composite MAE rate was 2.4% (3/123), meeting the prespecified performance goal (one-sided p<0.0001). The mean RV/LV diameter ratio decreased from 1.44±0.33 at baseline to 1.05±0.21 at 48 hours, a mean reduction of 0.39±0.33, exceeding the prespecified performance goal (p<0.0001). CONCLUSIONS: The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System met its prespecified safety and effectiveness endpoints in acute intermediate-risk PE. TFX delivered precise, stable control with reliable vessel access, enabling consistent right ventricular unloading. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06576427).

AIMS: We aimed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System for mechanical aspiration thrombectomy in acute intermediate-risk PE.

title: Heterogeneity in Time-Outcome Associations After Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Binational Registry Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although "time is brain" remains a core principle in acute stroke care, the association between treatment timing and functional outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) varies across patients. Some individuals treated in extended time windows still achieve favorable outcomes, a phenomenon termed the "late window paradox." Differences in stroke pathophysiology across etiologies may contribute to heterogeneity in the time-outcome relationship after EVT. We investigated factors associated with heterogeneity in time-dependent EVT responsiveness, with particular attention to stroke etiology. METHODS: We analyzed data from two multicenter registries in Korea (CRCS-K) and Taiwan (TREAT-AIS) from January 2019 to April 2023. Patients with anterior circulation acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism (CE) or large artery atherosclerosis (LAA) were included. Multivariable regression and interaction analyzes were performed to evaluate the association between onset-to-puncture (OTP) time and 90-day functional outcomes and to identify effect modifiers. RESULTS: _interaction Among 4,719 patients (mean age 72.0 years; 42.9% women; median NIHSS 15), longer OTP time was associated with lower odds of 90-day functional independence (adjusted OR per hour, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.96-0.98; p = 0.001). The impact of OTP time varied by stroke characteristics. CE etiology, MCA occlusion, higher NIHSS, and male sex were associated with greater time sensitivity. In CE strokes, each hour of delay reduced the odds of functional independence by 4% (aOR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.94-0.97; p < 0.001), whereas no significant association was observed in LAA strokes (P=0.028). CONCLUSION: The association between EVT timing and functional outcome varies according to stroke etiology and clinical characteristics, highlighting heterogeneity in time-outcome relationships among EVT-treated patients and providing observational insight into outcome variability in extended treatment windows.

title: Clinical Risk Factors and Inflammatory Markers as Predictors of Postoperative Delirium in Patients Undergoing Acute Type A Aortic Dissection Surgery.
abstract: Background: Methods: Results: Conclusions: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a common and serious neurological complication following acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) repair, contributing to increased morbidity and mortality. Given the critical role of systemic inflammation in POD pathogenesis, this study aimed to evaluate perioperative inflammatory profiles in patients undergoing ATAAD repair and to develop a predictive nomogram for early POD risk stratification.This retrospective, single-center study included 355 patients who underwent total arch replacement for ATAAD. Serial inflammatory markers were assessed across multiple perioperative time points. A two-stage variable selection process, incorporating variance inflation factor (VIF) and the Boruta algorithm, was utilized to identify robust predictors. A predictive nomogram was constructed via multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration plots, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Internal validation was performed using 1000 bootstrap resamples.POD occurred in 29.86% of the cohort. Patients who developed POD had higher inflammatory marker levels at several individual postoperative time points compared to the non-delirium group. The final predictive model integrated 11 key variables: age, EuroSCORE I, CPB time, SIRI_6h, PLR_6h, IL-10_6h, IL-8_6h, IL-8_pre, IL-6_6h, IL-6_pre, and PCT_6h. The nomogram demonstrated acceptable internal discrimination with an AUC of 0.835 (95% CI: 0.794-0.876) and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.811. Notably, IL-6_6h and PCT_6h emerged as strong independent risk factors, while SIRI_6h demonstrated an inverse association with POD. Calibration and DCA analyses confirmed the model's acceptable performance and potential clinical utility, though independent external validation remains essential prior to any clinical translation. An exploratory, web-based risk calculator was developed to facilitate bedside implementation.This study develops and internally validates an exploratory biomarker-based prediction model for POD in ATAAD patients. By integrating early inflammatory profiles with established clinical variables, this preliminary model provides a preliminary foundation for early risk stratification, though rigorous prospective multicenter external validation is required before real-world clinical implementation can be considered.

title: Magnetic resonance imaging vs computed tomography for baseline imaging evaluation in acute basilar artery occlusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The optimal imaging modality, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT), for identifying good treatment candidates among patients with acute basilar-artery occlusion (BAO) remains unclear. METHODS: This was a post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION trial. Patients were categorized into MRI or CT groups according to the baseline imaging modality. The primary outcome was mRS 0-3 at 90 days. The secondary outcomes included mRS score shift on an ordinal scale, early neurological deterioration, time from stroke onset to arterial puncture, and time from onset to randomization. The safety outcome was mortality within 90 days. Clinical outcomes and workflow times were compared between the two groups. RESULTS: Among 340 patients (CT: n = 277; MRI: n = 63), baseline imaging was not significantly associated with 90-day mRS 0-3 in the overall cohort (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.50-1.95; P = 0.976). It remained highly consistent across both the endovascular treatment and best medical management subgroups. Baseline MRI assessment was not associated with significant workflow delays compared with CT, including time from stroke onset to randomization (mean difference [MD] 5.23 min; P = 0.843) and time to puncture (MD 13.16 min; P = 0.701). Furthermore, the association between imaging modality and outcomes was consistent across different time windows. DISCUSSION: In patients with acute BAO, we did not observe evidence supporting the preferential use of MRI over CT as the primary imaging strategy for patient selection. Conventional imaging appears sufficient as a first-line tool for selecting patients in clinical practice.

METHODS: This was a post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION trial. Patients were categorized into MRI or CT groups according to the baseline imaging modality.

title: Vein of Galen malformation in newborns and children: contemporary advances and future directions.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Vein of Galen malformation is a rare and complex cerebrovascular disorder associated with significant morbidity and mortality from the fetal period through childhood. Advances in perinatal care, neuroimaging, endovascular therapy, and multidisciplinary management have improved survival and expanded therapeutic options, while generating new challenges in clinical strategies and long-term outcomes. OBJECTIVE: This review integrates evidence and expert perspectives presented during the II International Meeting on Vein of Galen Malformation in Newborns and Children, held in Camogli, Italy, in October 2025 and summarizes current advances, emerging developments, and priorities for research and clinical innovation. RECENT ADVANCES: Current developments include improved fetal and neonatal imaging, emerging prognostic biomarkers, fetal intervention, advances in endovascular treatment, and increasing understanding of underlying genetic and molecular mechanisms. Contemporary management increasingly integrates cardiovascular and neurological assessment, advanced neuroimaging, individualized endovascular strategies, and structured long-term neurodevelopmental follow-up. The development of a disease-specific registry reflects the growing impact of international collaboration. FUTURE DIRECTIONS: Major priorities include validation of risk-stratification tools, development of standardized imaging and neurodevelopmental biomarkers, refinement of fetal and neonatal interventions, improved understanding of disease biology, and multicenter data sharing. Family-centered care and standardized long-term outcome assessment should remain integral components of future VOGM research and clinical practice. CONCLUSIONS: VOGM management is rapidly evolving from survival-focused treatment toward individualized, multidisciplinary care extending from fetal diagnosis through childhood and adulthood. This review provides a comprehensive overview of current knowledge and emerging developments in this field, while defining a multidisciplinary, internationally informed roadmap for future research.

title: Development and internal validation of a parsimonious model for neurological deterioration at 48 h after endovascular thrombectomy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The incremental value of routine admission measurements for predicting early neurological deterioration after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) remains unclear. METHODS: This retrospective single-center reanalysis used a 2020-2022 registry. END48 was defined as an increase of at least 4 National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) points from admission to the fixed 48-h postoperative assessment. The conservative primary cohort excluded an unresolved longitudinal data segment. A revision-stage locked five-predictor logistic regression model included admission NIHSS scores, age, glucose levels, white blood cell count, and ln triglyceride value, with the NIHSS-only model serving as the comparator. Internal validation used 1,000 bootstrap samples and paired nested intervals of 1,000 outer × 100 inner samples. RESULTS: Post-hoc Of the 253 records representing 251 unique patients, 214 adults entered the primary cohort; 51 (23.8%) had END48. The primary model had an apparent area under the curve (AUC) of 0.651 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.601 (0.511 to 0.723). The corrected AUC difference vs. the NIHSS-only model was 0.038 (-0.025 to 0.171). The corrected Brier score was 0.180, compared to a prevalence-only reference of 0.182, resulting in a Brier skill score of 0.9%. The corrected primary calibration slope was 0.731 (0.519 to 0.892). Incremental net benefit was -0.015, 0.036, and 0.013 at 10%, 20%, and 30% thresholds, respectively; all corresponding 95% confidence intervals crossed zero.Riley assessments across plausible model-fit assumptions indicated that the available cohort was below the sample size desirable for model development. The reconstructed cohort sensitivity analysis did not change the overall interpretation. CONCLUSION: Discrimination was limited, improvement in probability accuracy was marginal, and incremental discrimination and net benefit were uncertain. The model should be regarded as exploratory rather than clinically implementable; independent validation and improved outcome ascertainment are required.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center reanalysis used a 2020-2022 registry. END48 was defined as an increase of at least 4 National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) points from admission to the fixed 48-h postoperative assessment.

title: Prognostic Value of Serial Alkaline Phosphatase-to-Albumin Ratio for Mortality After Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt.
abstract: Background: Methods: Results: p p p Conclusions: Prognostic assessment after transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) remains challenging, and currently available scores are based mainly on pre-procedural variables. The alkaline phosphatase-to-albumin ratio (APAR) is a simple laboratory-derived marker that may provide additional prognostic information during the early post-TIPS period.This retrospective, single-center cohort study included 45 adults who underwent TIPS between February 2019 and December 2024. APAR was calculated at baseline, 48 h, and 1 week after the procedure. The primary outcome was one-year all-cause mortality; 90-day mortality was a secondary outcome. Prognostic performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and associations with mortality were examined using Cox regression adjusted for age and baseline MELD score.Within one year, 17 patients (37.8%) died; nine (20.0%) died within 90 days; and 22 (48.9%) died during overall follow-up. Median APAR was higher in patients who died within one year than in those alive at one year at baseline (5.98 vs. 3.89;= 0.006), 48 h (10.79 vs. 3.78;< 0.001), and 1 week (13.93 vs. 4.57;< 0.001). ROC areas under the curve were 0.748 (95% CI, 0.578-0.893), 0.876 (0.748-0.964), and 0.873 (0.726-0.977), respectively. After adjustment for age and MELD, APAR remained associated with one-year mortality at baseline (hazard ratio [HR] 1.140; 95% CI, 1.049-1.238), 48 h (HR 1.225; 1.111-1.350), and 1 week (HR 1.193; 1.092-1.302).Serial APAR measurements were associated with one-year mortality after TIPS and may support early post-procedural risk assessment. Prospective multicenter validation is needed before clinical implementation.

title: Pharmacokinetics, Safety, and Exploratory 12-Month Clinical Follow-Up of a Novel BIOtorcin™-Coated Balloon for Femoropopliteal Artery Disease: The BRight PK Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: n Drug-coated balloons (DCBs) provide local antiproliferative therapy during endovascular revascularization without leaving a permanent vascular scaffold. Sirolimus is an attractive cytostatic antiproliferative agent, although its relatively low lipophilicity creates challenges for rapid arterial uptake and sustained tissue residence following balloon delivery. The BRight DCB is a novel peripheral DCB coated with BIOtorcin™ (CRC-015), a highly lipophilic synthetic derivative of sirolimus. The BRight PK study primarily evaluated the systemic pharmacokinetics of BIOtorcin™ and its metabolite sirolimus following treatment of femoropopliteal disease and secondarily assessed procedural performance, safety, patency, and functional outcomes over 12 months.BRight PK was a prospective, single-center, non-randomized pharmacokinetic study involving six adults with symptomatic peripheral artery disease (PAD; Rutherford-Becker category 2-4) caused by de novo superficial femoral and/or proximal popliteal artery disease. Following mandatory predilatation, lesions were treated with one or two BRight DCBs. Whole-blood BIOtorcin™ and sirolimus concentrations were measured before treatment and serially from 5 min to 24 h after removal of the final DCB. Non-compartmental pharmacokinetic analysis was performed. Angiography and duplex ultrasound were independently assessed by a core laboratory, and endpoint-related clinical events were independently adjudicated.All six participants completed 12-month follow-up. Mean age was 70.8 ± 7.4 years, and four (66.7%) were male. Seven BRight DCBs treated six lesions. Mean core-laboratory lesion length was 140.85 ± 136.23 mm, and baseline diameter stenosis was 78.50 ± 23.39%. Mean BIOtorcin™ exposure was 3976.8 ± 1665.7 µg (0.051 ± 0.0188 mg/kg). BIOtorcin™ Cmax was 23.60 ± 9.88 ng/mL at 5 min, terminal half-life was 21.87 ± 10.17 h, AUC0-t was 28.30 ± 12.19 h·ng/mL, and AUC0-∞ was 47.47 ± 18.27 h·ng/mL. Sirolimus Cmax was 0.692 ± 0.462 ng/mL at 24 h, when concentrations remained on the ascending portion of the concentration-time curve, indicating that the 24 h sampling window captured only early systemic sirolimus exposure rather than a complete pharmacokinetic profile. Device success was 100% (7/7); core-laboratory technical and procedural success were each 66.7% (4/6). No deaths, major or minor amputations, clinically driven target lesion revascularizations (cd-TLR), or clinically driven target vessel revascularizations (cd-TVRs) occurred. Visit-based 12-month primary patency was 83.3% (5/6); the single binary restenosis was detected at day 391, resulting in Kaplan-Meier primary patency of 100% at calendar day 365. The mean overall Walking Impairment Questionnaire (WIQ) score increased from 21.87 ± 19.16 at baseline to 62.28 ± 38.78 at 12 months.BIOtorcin™ demonstrated rapid systemic appearance following BRight DCB treatment, followed by a progressive decline in circulating parent drug concentrations and low systemic exposure to its metabolite, sirolimus. These pharmacokinetic findings, together with successful device delivery and the absence of major safety concerns over 12 months, demonstrate procedural feasibility and support continued clinical evaluation of the BRight DCB. Given the pharmacokinetic study design and small sample size (= 6), the 12-month clinical, functional, and patency findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as evidence of clinical efficacy.

Sirolimus is an attractive cytostatic antiproliferative agent, although its relatively low lipophilicity creates challenges for rapid arterial uptake and sustained tissue residence following balloon delivery. The BRight DCB is a novel peripheral DCB coated with BIOtorcin™ (CRC-015), a highly lipophilic synthetic derivative of sirolimus.

title: Comparative outcomes of arteriovenous accesses with and without tunneled hemodialysis catheters: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: This study compared patency rates of arteriovenous accesses with and without concurrent tunneled hemodialysis catheter (THC) use, addressing limited research on combined outcomes. A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted on patients undergoing arteriovenous access creation at a single hospital between January 2021 and December 2022. Primary outcomes were the 6-month primary patency rate and functional dialysis success. Secondary outcomes were the factors associated with each of these endpoints. Statistical analyses employed t tests, chi-square tests, logistic regression, and Kaplan-Meier survival curves. A total of 319 vascular accesses were included. The 6-month patency rate was significantly higher in the access-only group than in the access + THC group (87.04% vs 78.20%, P = .04). THC usage (odds ratio [OR] = 0.49, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.25-0.95, P = .03), graft usage (OR = 0.38, 95% CI: 0.18-0.82, P = .01), and higher hemoglobin levels (OR = 0.80, 95% CI: 0.65-0.96, P = .02) were associated with reduced patency rates. Functional dialysis success at 6 months did not differ significantly between groups (87.96% vs 83.89%, P = .21). However, older age (OR = 0.96, 95% CI: 0.93-0.99, P = .01), use of a cubital artery to an autologous vein (OR = 0.39, 95% CI: 0.19-0.82, P = .01) or graft (OR = 0.40, 95% CI: 0.17-0.97, P = .04), and higher hemoglobin levels (OR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.66-0.99, P = .03) were associated with a lower likelihood of functional dialysis success. Concurrent THC use was independently associated with reduced 6-month primary patency without a corresponding reduction in the short-term delivery of dialysis, suggesting an increased need for interventions to maintain the access. Judicious use of THCs and careful consideration of the vascular access type are important to optimize vascular access outcomes in patients undergoing hemodialysis.

A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted on patients undergoing arteriovenous access creation at a single hospital between January 2021 and December 2022. Primary outcomes were the 6-month primary patency rate and functional dialysis success.

title: Apparent Diffusion Coefficient Composition and Tissue Heterogeneity as Predictors of Functional Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy in Patients With Large Ischemic Core.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Recent trials established endovascular thrombectomy efficacy in large ischemic cores, yet outcomes remain heterogeneous despite similar infarct volumes, suggesting that current volumetric assessments may not fully capture tissue viability. We examined whether tissue composition quantified by apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) distribution and tissue heterogeneity within baseline diffusion-weighted imaging lesions are associated with functional outcomes in large-core patients after successful endovascular thrombectomy. METHODS: -6 2 We retrospectively analyzed patients with large vessel occlusion with large ischemic cores (diffusion-weighted imaging candidate volume ≥50 mL) achieving successful reperfusion after endovascular thrombectomy. We quantified ADC tissue composition as proportions within 3 ADC ranges relative to total diffusion-weighted imaging lesion volume: low (<540), mid (540-700), and high (>700 × 10mm/s). Separately, tissue heterogeneity was assessed using Shannon entropy, a metric quantifying ADC distribution heterogeneity. The primary outcome was 3-month good functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score of 0-3), analyzed via adjusted logistic regression. RESULTS: P P Among 126 patients (age, 70.8±12.4 years; 60.3% men; diffusion-weighted imaging candidate volume, 93.7±41.2 mL), 39.7% achieved a good functional outcome. Both tissue heterogeneity (adjusted odds ratio, 1.45 per 0.1-unit increase, 1.09-1.93,=0.011, area under the curve, 0.671) and mid-ADC fraction (adjusted odds ratio, 1.78 per 5% increase, 1.20-2.63,=0.004, area under the curve, 0.688) were associated with good functional outcomes. Neither low-ADC nor high-ADC fractions showed significant associations with functional outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: -6 2 Higher mid-ADC (540-700 × 10mm/s) fraction and greater tissue heterogeneity predicted favorable outcomes in patients with large ischemic core, indicating that tissue composition within the ischemic core, beyond its volume, is associated with functional outcome after reperfusion. Among large-core patients who achieved successful reperfusion, ADC-based tissue characterization may help predict functional outcome.

We examined whether tissue composition quantified by apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) distribution and tissue heterogeneity within baseline diffusion-weighted imaging lesions are associated with functional outcomes in large-core patients after successful endovascular thrombectomy. METHODS: -6 2 We retrospectively analyzed patients with large vessel occlusion with large ischemic cores (diffusion-weighted imaging candidate volume ≥50 mL) achieving successful reperfusion after endovascular thrombectomy.

title: Anxiety in patients with lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis: a patient-centred sequential explanatory mixed-methods study of prevalence, associated factors, and patient experiences.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Lower extremity deep vein thrombosis (LEDVT) is associated with substantial psychological burden. Anxiety after DVT may reflect not only an emotional consequence of thrombosis, but also a signal of unmet informational, functional, and supportive care needs. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence and factors associated with anxiety among LEDVT patients and to explore their lived experiences, perceived triggers, and support needs using a mixed-methods design. METHODS: A sequential explanatory mixed-methods study was conducted. In the quantitative phase, 175 LEDVT patients completed the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7), Brief Illness Perception Questionnaire (B-IPQ), and Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support (MSPSS). Clinical and care-process variables were collected, including the perceived adequacy of structured counselling at diagnosis using an 8-item checklist. Clinically significant anxiety was defined as GAD-7 score ≥10. Multivariable logistic regression was performed according to a prespecified conceptual framework. In the qualitative phase, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 15 purposively selected participants; data were analyzed using thematic analysis. RESULTS: P P P P The prevalence of clinically significant anxiety was 41.1% (72/175; 95% CI: 33.9%-48.6%). Younger age (OR = 0.95, 95% CI: 0.92-0.98, = 0.002), higher B-IPQ score (OR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.11-1.26, < 0.001), lower MSPSS score (OR = 0.94, 95% CI: 0.90-0.98, = 0.005), and adequate counselling at diagnosis (OR = 0.42, 95% CI: 0.20-0.88, = 0.022) were independently associated with anxiety. Qualitative analysis generated five major themes: fear of complications, treatment-related anxiety, role and functional impairment, information delivery and illness meaning-making, and insufficient emotional and social support. CONCLUSION: Anxiety affects approximately two in five LEDVT patients in this single-centre cross-sectional cohort. Anxiety was associated not only with younger age, negative illness perception, and low social support, but also with symptom burden and perceived inadequacy of counselling at diagnosis; qualitative findings additionally highlighted symptom burden and functional limitations as key experiential drivers of anxiety. Integrated DVT care should address anticoagulation management, structured education, risk communication, cognitive reframing, functional recovery, and psychosocial support.

title: Risk factors of major bleeding associated with direct oral anticoagulant treatment in patients with venous thromboembolism: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are commonly prescribed for venous thromboembolism (VTE), but major bleeding (MB) remains an important complication of treatment. Despite their widespread use, systematic evaluations of prognostic factors associated with major bleeding during DOAC treatment remain scarce. To address this gap, we conducted a systematic review to identify prognostic factors associated with major bleeding during DOAC treatment in patients with VTE. This study seeks to enhance the safety and efficacy of anticoagulation therapy for VTE patients. METHOD AND RESULTS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted to search the PubMed and Web of Science databases for studies published before September 18, 2026. The review adhered to predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria to identify studies that investigated risk factors for major bleeding associated with DOAC treatment in patients diagnosed with VTE. Among the evaluated prognostic factors, quantitative pooling was possible only for age, which was reported in two studies; the remaining factors were summarized individually. Low-certainty evidence from a single study suggested a possible association between non-recommended dosing regimens and major bleeding. Evidence regarding declining adherence was also limited and of very low certainty. For age, very low-certainty evidence from the pooled analysis of two studies did not demonstrate a statistically significant association with major bleeding. CONCLUSION: The available evidence suggests possible associations between several prognostic factors and major bleeding in patients with VTE treated with DOACs; however, most findings are supported by low- or very low-certainty evidence and frequently by single studies. These findings should therefore be interpreted cautiously and require validation in larger, high-quality prospective studies.

To address this gap, we conducted a systematic review to identify prognostic factors associated with major bleeding during DOAC treatment in patients with VTE.

title: Case Report: Brucella-associated complications following thoracic endovascular aortic repair: a case series of three patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Brucellosis is a rare but potentially fatal cause of vascular graft infection. Evidence regarding Brucella-associated complications after thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) remains limited. Case presentation: We report three elderly male patients who developed severe aortic complications following TEVAR, including pseudoaneurysm formation and aorto-esophageal fistula. All patients had a history of epidemiological exposure to Brucella and were diagnosed with active infection through serological testing (Rose Bengal test, serum agglutination test, Brucella IgG and IgM antibodies). Endovascular re-intervention combined with targeted anti-brucellosis therapy was performed in all cases. RESULTS: One patient achieved sustained clinical remission after repeat endovascular repair and prolonged antimicrobial therapy. Two patients developed catastrophic infectious complications, including mediastinal abscess and aorto-esophageal fistula, resulting in death despite aggressive management. CONCLUSIONS: Brucella infection should be considered in patients presenting with unexplained symptoms after TEVAR, especially in endemic regions. Endovascular repair plays a critical role in acute stabilization; however, long-term outcomes remain highly dependent on effective infection control.

title: Aneurysm Sac Expansion After EVAR: Associated Factors, Prognostic Impact, and Preventive Strategies-A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: Aneurysm sac expansion is an adverse marker of durability after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). We assessed factors associated with expansion, its prognostic significance, and the effect of preventive embolisation.PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched through 23 August 2026 (PROSPERO CRD420261386132). Random-effects meta-analyses analysed odds ratios (ORs), hazard ratios (HRs), and risk ratios (RRs) separately; risk of bias and certainty were assessed with RoB 2, ROBINS-I, QUIPS, and GRADE.Thirty-three reports (20 independent quantitative studies) were included. Type II endoleak (OR 5.16, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.53-10.50; HR 3.08, 95% CI 2.11-4.49) and type I endoleak (OR 11.94, 95% CI 5.30-26.90) were associated with expansion (low certainty). Expansion was associated with higher late mortality in a single independent adjusted cohort (HR 1.31, 95% CI 1.14-1.51; very low certainty). Preventive embolisation was associated with lower risks of persistent type II endoleak (RR 0.58, 95% CI 0.34-0.97; low certainty) and reintervention (RR 0.44, 95% CI 0.24-0.82; very low certainty), but neither association remained statistically conclusive in sensitivity analyses.Endoleaks are consistently associated with sac expansion, which appears to identify patients at increased late risk. Effects of preventive embolisation on surrogate outcomes are not robust; prevention of sac expansion and clinical events is unproven.

title: In-hospital vascular surgery consultation is associated with improved follow-up and earlier identification of aneurysmal degeneration after acute Type A aortic dissection.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Acute Type A aortic dissections (TAAD) are historically managed by cardiac surgery. However, subsequent treatment of residual dissection within the thoracoabdominal aorta often requires vascular surgical intervention and lifelong surveillance. This study assesses long-term outcomes by completeness of follow-up after operative intervention for acute TAAD. METHODS: Patients who underwent surgical intervention for acute TAAD from 2014 to 2025 were identified. Patients who experienced death within 30-days or those with dissection limited to Zone 0/Zone 1 were excluded. Vascular surgery evaluation and time to consultation (index-hospitalization, outpatient, none) was documented. Follow-up was classified as complete, incomplete, or lost (LTF) according to the frequency of contrasted thoracoabdominal imaging, consistent with clinical practice guidelines. Trends in completeness of follow-up were described. Demographics, anatomic/operative characteristics, and perioperative outcomes were compared between complete follow-up and incomplete follow-up/LTF groups. Long-term outcomes (aortic degeneration, planned secondary intervention, survival) were assessed with Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox regression analysis. RESULTS: 241 patients were included; 80% had vascular surgery consultation (70% inpatient, 30% outpatient) and 86% of consultations occurred within 1-year of index procedure. In total, 46% of patients had complete follow-up, 41% had incomplete follow-up, and 13% were LTF. In-hospital consultation increased by 58% over the study period. Demographics, comorbidities, and anatomic characteristics were similar between groups. Patients with complete follow-up had higher rates of complex arch repair (Zone 1-3) (complete 56% vs. incomplete/LTF 27%, p<0.001), were more likely to undergo genetic testing (complete 52% vs. incomplete/LTF 18%, p<0.001), in-hospital TEVAR extension (7% vs. 2%, p=0.028), and TEVAR extension within 3 months (complete 17% vs. incomplete/LTF 5%, p=0.002). In time-to-event analysis, complete follow-up was associated with more planned secondary interventions (complete: 12% vs. incomplete: 5%, p=0.007) and identified aneurysmal degeneration (32% vs. 15%, p=0.002) within 1-year of acute dissection. Long-term survival differed by completeness of follow-up; 1-year (complete: 97% vs. incomplete: 97% vs. LTF: 91%), 3-years (complete: 92% vs. incomplete: 95% vs. LTF: 81%, p=0.021). There were no aortic-related deaths for patients with complete follow-up and five aortic-related deaths (5%) in patients with incomplete follow-up (p=0.13). In-hospital vascular surgery consultation was associated with complete follow-up (HR 2.87, 95% CI 1.6-5.1) and planned secondary interventions (HR 2.07, 95% CI 1.1-3.9). CONCLUSION: Vascular surgery consultation is associated with increased identification of aneurysmal degeneration, planned secondary interventions, and mid-term survival. These data suggest that longitudinal vascular surgical care, starting with in-hospital consultation, is a critical component of care following acute TAAD and should be strongly considered to ensure appropriate postoperative surveillance and improve long-term patient outcomes.

title: Optimizing Vessel Preparation in Femoropopliteal Lesions: Does the Chocolate Balloon Deliver on Its Clinical Promise?
abstract: The "leave nothing behind" paradigm using drug-coated balloons (DCBs) has reshaped femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease treatment, though clinical success remains heavily contingent upon optimal vessel preparation. In a recent issue of The American Journal of Cardiology, Li and colleagues address the limitations of conventional plain old balloon angioplasty (POBA) through a propensity score-matched analysis of 508 patients from the multicenter PROMISING registry, comparing specialized vessel preparation using the nitinol-constrained Chocolate balloon against POBA before DCB angioplasty. The Chocolate balloon significantly reduced the primary endpoint of bailout stenting (20.47% vs 29.92%) and facilitated larger final DCB diameters, though these acute mechanical advantages did not translate into statistically significant differences in clinical outcomes at 12 months. This commentary examines this striking "procedural-to-clinical paradox," highlighting how the potent antiproliferative effect of DCBs and the acute compensatory function of bailout stents may temporarily mask early clinical divergence. Given that cumulative mechanical failures of permanent metallic implants typically emerge beyond one year in hostile biomechanical environments, longer-term observation remains essential to capture the true clinical dividend of a stent-free strategy.

title: The Moderating Effects of Race and Ethnicity on a Motivational Interviewing Intervention for Improving Physical Health Among Patients With Peripheral Artery Disease: Secondary Analysis of a Pilot Randomized Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In a pilot randomized trial, face-to-face or telephone motivational interviewing (MI) was more efficacious than a smartphone app after 3 months for increasing 6-minute walk distance (primary outcome) and reducing body weight (secondary outcome) in patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD). Little is known about intervention heterogeneity related to social determinants of health (SDOH). OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore whether SDOH are associated with the MI intervention effects on walking distance and weight loss and generate intervention heterogeneity hypotheses. METHODS: Community dwellers in Wichita, Kansas, were recruited through community outlets and screened for PAD. Consented participants were randomly assigned to MI (n=16) or an app (n=13). Survey instruments were used to measure SDOH, demographics, and adverse childhood experiences, which were assessed for their associations with 6-minute walk distance change and weight loss. Difference-in-differences (DiD) comparisons of median changes between SDOH strata were conducted using Wilcoxon and Kruskal-Wallis nonparametric tests. RESULTS: For 6-minute walk distance, pretest-posttest changes were significantly greater among participants of "other" race and ethnicity than among non-Hispanic White participants (DiD=44.0 m, 95% CI 19.2-164.2; P=.004), and no DiDs for other SDOH were significant. Significant median pretest-posttest increases in walking distance were observed in those with a college or higher educational attainment (48.8 m, 95% CI 28.0-61.4), unmarried individuals (40.4 m, 95% CI 0.5-56.0), those living with family (55.7 m, 95% CI 30.5-199.5), those who talked to and saw family or friends 3 or more times a week (46.4 m, 95% CI 17.2-69.4), and those without unmet daily needs (46.5 m, 95% CI 7.6-67.1). For weight loss, we did not observe significant DiDs with any SDOH. However, a significant median weight loss was observed in every SDOH stratum where we observed a significant increase in 6-minute walk distance. Significant weight loss was also observed in 5 additional SDOH strata: male individuals, household income below US $30,000, never served in military, employed status, and no stress. The improvements in weight loss and walking distance were highly consistent in both direction and size across SDOH strata. CONCLUSIONS: This pilot study was the first to explore potential SDOH-related intervention effect modification and heterogeneity. The significant association between walking distance and race and ethnicity suggested a potential effect modification. Significant pretest-posttest improvements in both outcomes were found in the same SDOH strata. The highly consistent evidence across both outcomes and all SDOH strata provided confidence in potential intervention efficacy and heterogeneity despite the small sample size. Our findings were consistent with established associations between SDOH and general functions in patients with PAD, suggesting likely mediation pathways through health literacy and social support. Future interventions should consider heterogeneity to target socially disadvantaged patients with PAD to bridge disparities and maximize benefits. title: Association between elevated lipoprotein (a) and venous thromboembolism: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established cardiovascular risk factor linked to atherogenesis, inflammation, and thrombosis; however, its association with venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain, with inconsistent findings across observational studies. AIMS: To systematically evaluate the association between elevated Lp(a) levels and VTE risk and to examine differences by study design. METHODS: 2 2 PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception through January 2026 for observational studies assessing Lp(a) and VTE. Effect estimates (odds ratios [ORs] or hazard ratios [HRs]) were pooled using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Heterogeneity was assessed using Iand τ. Risk of bias was evaluated with ROBINS-E, publication bias with funnel plots, Egger's and Begg's tests, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. The primary outcome was VTE; secondary outcomes included deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), and recurrent VTE. RESULTS: 2 2 2 Eleven studies (6 case-control, 5 cohort; 63,325 participants; 3581 VTE events) were included. Elevated Lp(a) was associated with a borderline increased VTE risk (pooled OR/HR 1.34 [95% CI 1.00-1.80]; P = 0.049), with high heterogeneity (I = 77.8%) and a wide prediction interval (0.56-3.21). In stratified analyses, case-control studies showed a significant association (OR 1.88 [1.25-2.81]; I = 57.2%), whereas cohort studies showed no association (HR 0.99 [0.85-1.15]; I = 0%), with significant between-group differences (p < 0.0001). CONCLUSIONS: The association between elevated Lp(a) and VTE appears limited to case-control studies and is not supported by prospective cohort data, suggesting potential bias or residual confounding. Further large-scale and genetic studies are warranted to clarify this relationship.

title: Saint-Bonnet Doppler waveform classification system: a scoping review and evidence-based appraisal using AGREE II and AGREE-REX.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Doppler waveform interpretation is central to the diagnosis and surveillance of lower limb peripheral arterial disease (PAD). Despite widespread clinical use of duplex ultrasound (DUS) and hand-held Doppler (HHD), waveform terminology remains highly variable and non-standardised across institutions. The Saint-Bonnet classification, proposed by the French College of Teachers in Vascular Medicine (CEMV), offers a structured eight-category morphological framework mapped to haemodynamic severity. Its evidence base and methodological quality have never been formally appraised. METHODS: A scoping review was conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). MEDLINE (Ovid) and Embase (Ovid) were searched from 1946 to November 2025. Studies describing, applying, validating, or evaluating the Saint-Bonnet classification were eligible. Data were extracted using a standardised form. Methodological quality was appraised using AGREE II (six domains) and AGREE-REX (three domains), independently by two reviewers (H.A. and F.A.). RESULTS: κ κ κ Seven studies met the inclusion criteria; all published between 2017 and 2022 from a single French vascular research group. The Saint-Bonnet classification achieved a categorisation rate of 98.2% across 1,033 waveforms, outperforming alternative systems. Inter-rater reliability was moderate ( ≈ 0.55). Waveform grade independently correlated with maximal walking distance, and waveform-guided ankle-brachial index (ABI) selection achieved near-perfect agreement with guideline standards (up to 1.00). Automated neural network classification reached = 0.79, approaching expert agreement. AGREE II appraisal revealed high scores for Clarity of Presentation and Scope & Purpose (97% and 83%), but low scores for Rigour of Development and Applicability (44% and 40%). AGREE-REX demonstrated high Clinical Applicability and Implementability. CONCLUSION: The Saint-Bonnet classification is a promising and practical framework for Doppler waveform interpretation, with consistent findings across the available studies. Low AGREE II scores for Rigour of Development and Applicability reflect gaps in its documented development and reporting rather than evidence against its clinical performance. However, all supporting evidence originates from a single, non-independent French research group, and the classification has not undergone external validation; broader adoption should await independent, multicentre confirmation of these findings.

title: Optimization of direct oral anticoagulant prescribing in primary care: a pharmacotherapeutic review in real-world clinical practice and therapeutic efficiency.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Direct oral anticoagulants are among the first-line treatments for stroke prevention in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation and for the treatment and secondary prevention of venous thromboembolism. The increasing use of these agents poses challenges related to prescribing appropriateness, clinical safety. This study aims to evaluate the impact of a primary care pharmacist-led intervention on the appropriateness of DOAC prescribing, pharmacotherapeutic efficiency, and clinical outcomes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective, quasi-experimental before-and-after study was conducted in the healthcare area of Xarxa Santa Tecla (Tarragonès and Baix Penedès, Spain). 791 patients receiving DOAC therapy were included. The intervention comprised multidisciplinary educational activities, individualized pharmacotherapeutic review, and communication of recommendations to prescribers. RESULTS: The mean age was 78.2 years, and 43.2% of patients had moderate or severe renal impairment. The pharmacotherapeutic review identified 527 patients (66.6%) as candidates for treatment optimization, through a proposed switch from apixaban to dabigatran. The pharmacist intervention was associated with changes in prescribing patterns among newly initiated patients, increasing the use of dabigatran. The economic analysis estimated savings of €75,508.81 from new treatment initiations and €31,288.25 from therapeutic switches, resulting in total savings of €106,797.06 in 2025. The overall bleeding rate remained stable (5.3% in 2024% vs. 5.2% in 2025), with no deterioration in clinical safety. In conclusion, a structured, multidisciplinary, and coordinated primary care pharmacist-led intervention promoted a more efficient use of healthcare resources, while no deterioration in population-level safety indicators was observed. These findings reinforce the role of primary care pharmacists in optimizing anticoagulant therapy.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Direct oral anticoagulants are among the first-line treatments for stroke prevention in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation and for the treatment and secondary prevention of venous thromboembolism. The increasing use of these agents poses challenges related to prescribing appropriateness, clinical safety. This study aims to evaluate the impact of a primary care pharmacist-led intervention on the appropriateness of DOAC prescribing, pharmacotherapeutic efficiency, and clinical outcomes.

title: Abdominal aortic angiosarcoma following endovascular aneurysm repair: case report and analysis of existing literature.
abstract: Abdominal aortic angiosarcoma following endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) is an exceptionally rare and aggressive malignancy that may mimic common EVAR-related complications. We report the case of a 72-year-old man who presented with progressive lower back pain and was initially suspected of having a graft infection. Imaging revealed a periaortic mass involving a previously treated abdominal aortic aneurysm. Biopsy confirmed aortic angiosarcoma. No regional lymph node or distant metastases were identified. The patient underwent neoadjuvant chemotherapy with gemcitabine and docetaxel, followed by radiotherapy and surgical resection of the abdominal aorta and EVAR graft with aortic reconstruction. Histopathological examination demonstrated complete pathological response without evidence of residual angiosarcoma. Our literature review identified only 21 reported cases of abdominal aortic angiosarcoma following EVAR, including the present case, underscoring the exceptional rarity of this entity and the limited evidence available to guide diagnosis and treatment. This case highlights the importance of considering aortic angiosarcoma in patients with persistent symptoms and atypical periaortic findings after EVAR and suggests that early biopsy and a multidisciplinary, multimodal treatment approach may improve outcomes despite the generally poor prognosis associated with this disease.

Imaging revealed a periaortic mass involving a previously treated abdominal aortic aneurysm.

title: Association of red cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio with ICU outcomes in patients with aortic dissection.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Critically ill patients with aortic dissection remain at high risk of adverse ICU outcomes, including ICU mortality. The red cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio (RAR) has been investigated as a prognostic marker in various clinical settings. This study aimed to evaluate the association of RAR with ICU outcomes in patients with aortic dissection. METHODS: Data were extracted from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database. ICU mortality was defined as the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes included sepsis during hospitalization/ICU stay, acute kidney injury (AKI), and renal replacement therapy (RRT) use. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to assess the discriminative performance of RAR for ICU mortality. The optimal RAR cutoff was determined using Youden's index and was considered exploratory. Calibration plots and decision curve analysis were used to evaluate model performance. RESULTS: P P P RAR showed modest discrimination for ICU mortality (AUC: 0.66; 95% CI: 0.552-0.765). The exploratory cutoff value of RAR was 5.182. Compared with the low-RAR group, the high-RAR group had higher ICU mortality (21.8% vs. 6.7%; < 0.001), a higher prevalence of sepsis during hospitalization/ICU stay (82.8% vs. 61.1%; < 0.001), and more frequent RRT use (33.3% vs. 9.4%; < 0.001). The AUC increased from 0.706 for SOFA alone to 0.731 for SOFA plus RAR, indicating only limited incremental discrimination. CONCLUSION: Higher early-ICU RAR was associated with ICU mortality and other adverse ICU outcomes in patients with aortic dissection, but its discrimination was modest, its incremental value beyond SOFA was limited, and external validation is required.

The red cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio (RAR) has been investigated as a prognostic marker in various clinical settings. This study aimed to evaluate the association of RAR with ICU outcomes in patients with aortic dissection.
