title: Long-term graft and patient survival of patients with portal vein stenosis after pediatric liver transplantation: Results from the multicenter multinational PORTAL registry.
abstract: Pediatric liver transplantation (pLT) has become a standard treatment, but it is still burdened by complications such as portal vein stenosis (PVS). PVS can result in compromised graft function and portal hypertension if left untreated. We aimed to assess long-term patient and graft survival after PVS diagnosis following pLT. Our study analyzed data from the Portal Vein Obstruction Revascularisation Therapy After Liver Transplantation (PORTAL) registry, which contains retrospective data from 21 centers across 18 countries, over a 20-year period. Graft and patient survival rates were determined after PVS diagnosis. This study included 239 patients (53% female; median age at pLT 1.1   y) diagnosed with PVS. The median age at diagnosis was 2.7 years. The overall 10-year graft survival was 90%, and the 10-year patient survival was 96%. One-year graft and patient survival were lowest in patients with PVS diagnosed ≤7 days after pLT (80% and 92%, respectively). Initial treatment strategies comprised mostly endovascular procedures (87%), followed by conservative (11%) and surgical treatment (3%). Patient outcomes did not differ between these treatment groups. Within the endovascular group, graft survival in patients treated with stent (n=26) was significantly lower compared with those with percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (n=181) (88% vs. 98%, respectively, p =0.01). Our findings indicate excellent graft and patient survival after PVS diagnosis and its treatment. Further research is needed to determine the safety and efficacy of optimal management strategies, especially in early-onset PVS.

PVS can result in compromised graft function and portal hypertension if left untreated. We aimed to assess long-term patient and graft survival after PVS diagnosis following pLT.

title: Prevalence of Guideline-Recommended Genetic Testing in Patients at Risk for Heritable Thoracic Aortic Disease.
abstract: Heritable thoracic aortic diseases (HTAD) include genetic conditions that increase risk of thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection. The 2022 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) guidelines recommend genetic testing for at-risk individuals, but real-world uptake remains unclear. We evaluated adherence to testing recommendations and demographic differences across major HTAD risk cohorts. We conducted a retrospective study using the TriNetX Research Network (2005-2025). Three guideline-based cohorts were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes: (1) thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection before age 60, (2) family history of thoracic aortic disease, and (3) nonthoracic arterial aneurysms. Genetic testing was defined by ICD-10-CM codes for genetic screening or susceptibility. Testing prevalence was stratified by age, sex, race, and ethnicity, and annual testing incidence (2005-2024) was evaluated. Among 57,935 patients with thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection before age 60, 1,205 (2.09%) underwent genetic testing. Among 2,811,862 patients with a family history of thoracic aortic disease, 66,699 (2.38%) received testing. Among 347,000 patients with nonthoracic arterial aneurysms, 4,913 (1.42%) underwent testing. Testing was consistently higher in females than males and varied across age groups. Annual testing incidence increased over time but remained <0.6% by 2024. In conclusion, genetic testing for HTAD remains markedly underutilized, with <2.5% of at-risk patients tested despite guideline recommendations, highlighting persistent implementation gaps and the need to improve equitable access to genetic evaluation.

The 2022 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) guidelines recommend genetic testing for at-risk individuals, but real-world uptake remains unclear. We evaluated adherence to testing recommendations and demographic differences across major HTAD risk cohorts.

title: From recanalization to recovery: inflammation and futile reperfusion after mechanical thrombectomy.
abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) has markedly improved reperfusion outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by large-vessel occlusion. However, successful angiographic reperfusion does not invariably translate into functional independence. Poor functional outcome despite successful angiographic reperfusion is commonly described as futile reperfusion. This clinical-angiographic mismatch may reflect persistent tissue injury, including inflammatory injury, alongside pretreatment damage and other determinants of outcome. Experimental findings and clinical associations implicate persistent inflammatory activation, thrombo-inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, microvascular no-reflow, and blood-brain barrier disruption as contributors to secondary tissue injury after MT. Here, we examine potential inflammatory contributions to futile reperfusion and consider how inflammatory biomarkers might inform risk stratification after MT. Ischemia activates microglia, endothelial cells, platelets, complement pathways, and circulating immune cells. Subsequent reperfusion may amplify oxidative stress, cytokine signaling, neutrophil-endothelial interactions, neutrophil extracellular trap formation, matrix metalloproteinase activity, and barrier failure. Together, these processes can promote microvascular obstruction, cerebral edema, hemorrhagic transformation, infarct growth, and impaired neurological recovery despite successful angiographic reperfusion. Among circulating biomarkers, the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio has been studied repeatedly, alongside platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, systemic inflammation response index, interleukin-6, matrix metalloproteinase-9, and other molecular markers. Their specificity, incremental predictive value, and clinical utility require further validation in standardized thrombectomy cohorts. We therefore view inflammation as a plausible biological link between macrovascular reperfusion and persistent tissue-level injury after MT. From a translational perspective, the immediate priorities are to standardize sampling protocols, characterize dynamic inflammatory trajectories, develop multimodal prediction models, and test biomarker-guided therapeutic strategies.

However, successful angiographic reperfusion does not invariably translate into functional independence. Poor functional outcome despite successful angiographic reperfusion is commonly described as futile reperfusion.

title: Machine learning-based prediction model for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with venous thromboembolism and acute kidney injury.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypoalbuminemia is a prevalent and critical complication among intensive care unit (ICU) patients with venous thromboembolism (VTE) and acute kidney injury (AKI), significantly associated with increased mortality and prolonged hospitalization. However, reliable tools for early prediction of hypoalbuminemia in this high-risk population remain limited. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning-based prediction model for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with coexisting VTE and AKI. METHODS: n n In this retrospective study, data from 585 ICU patients with VTE and AKI were analyzed. Patients were divided into a training cohort ( = 409) and a validation cohort ( = 176). Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression with standardization was applied for feature selection. Five machine learning models-logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM), and support vector machine (SVM)-were developed and evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Decision curve analysis (DCA), SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and feature importance were performed for the optimal model. The performance of the best machine learning model was compared with conventional ICU severity scores (APSIII, LODs, and OASIS). RESULTS: The standardized LASSO regression identified ten optimal predictors: creatinine (cr), age, tumor/cancer, body mass index (BMI), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), urine output, D-dimer (D_D), Charlson comorbidity index, anticoagulant use, and alanine aminotransferase (ALT). Among the five models, XGBoost achieved the best predictive performance with a validation AUC of 0.882 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.832-0.924], followed by RF (AUC = 0.878), LightGBM (AUC = 0.870), LR (AUC = 0.838), and SVM (AUC = 0.662). The 5-fold cross-validation AUC for XGBoost was 0.901 ± 0.042, with minimal overfitting (CV-test difference = -0.019). Decision curve analysis demonstrated favorable clinical net benefit of the XGBoost model across a wide range of threshold probabilities. SHAP analysis and feature importance consistently identified urine output, age, LDL, BMI, and D-dimer as the top contributors. Compared with conventional ICU severity scores, the XGBoost model significantly outperformed APSIII (AUC = 0.661), LODs (AUC = 0.652), and OASIS (AUC = 0.647). The logistic regression-based nomogram achieved a C-index of 0.838, providing a user-friendly bedside tool for clinicians. CONCLUSION: The machine learning-based XGBoost model, incorporating ten readily available clinical variables, demonstrated excellent predictive performance for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with VTE and AKI. This model offers a practical and interpretable tool for early risk stratification and may guide proactive nutritional and therapeutic interventions in this vulnerable population.

However, reliable tools for early prediction of hypoalbuminemia in this high-risk population remain limited. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning-based prediction model for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with coexisting VTE and AKI.

title: Factors associated with mortality in patients with atrial fibrillation: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study synthesized published meta-analyses to assess the quality, bias, and strength of evidence regarding mortality risk factors in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). METHODS: Web of Science, Embase, PubMed, and Cochrane database were used to search the literature up to May 2025. Eligible studies were systematic reviews or meta-analyses investigating AF-related mortality risk factors. AMSTAR tool was used to assess methodological quality and GRADE was used to evaluate evidence certainty. RESULTS: A total of 216 risk factors were identified. Among them, 86 showed significant associations with mortality, while 130 did not. Based on GRADE ratings, 11 were high-quality significant factors, and 9 were of moderate-quality. Factors linked to increased mortality included certain medications (digoxin, dronedarone, sotalol; warfarin/VKA vs. NOAC was associated with higher mortality), comorbidities (cancer, COPD, diabetes, anemia, frailty, LVH, peripheral artery disease), demographic characteristics (older age, smoking, BMI <18.5, Latin American ethnicity), and AF subtype (persistent or non-paroxysmal). In contrast, reduced mortality was associated with NOAC or DOAC use, higher BMI (25-30 or ≥30), surgical interventions (catheter ablation, LAAC/LAAO), other medications (SGLT2 inhibitors, statins), and early rhythm control. CONCLUSION: Systematic Review Registration: This review highlights key factors associated with mortality in AF. Increased risk was observed with warfarin/VKA use (vs. NOAC), certain antiarrhythmic drugs, comorbidities, low BMI, older age, smoking, and non-paroxysmal AF. In contrast, NOAC use, surgical interventions, high BMI, statin and SGLT2 inhibitor therapy, and early rhythm-control strategies were linked to reduced mortality risk.https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42024533372, PROSPERO CRD42024533372.

title: Deep Learning-Based Versus Threshold-Based Bone Removal for CT Angiography of Head and Neck Arteriovenous Fistulas: A Retrospective Comparison of Image Quality, Key-Structure Display, and Post-Processing Time.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: p p p p p Bone overlap at the skull base limits CT angiography (CTA) in head and neck arteriovenous fistulas (hAVFs), and threshold-based bone removal fails where bone and contrast attenuation overlap. Whether deep learning-based removal improves the display of the structures that determine endovascular planning is unknown in a DSA-confirmed cohort. We therefore compared the two methods within the same CTA datasets.In this single-centre retrospective study, 35 patients with DSA-confirmed hAVF underwent head and neck CTA and digital subtraction angiography (DSA) within two weeks of each other, and each CTA dataset was post-processed with both methods on one workstation. Two blinded readers scored the fistula site, feeding artery and draining vein (0 to 2 each) and overall image quality (5-point scale). Scores were compared with paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, vessel edge sharpness and post-processing time with paired t tests, and technical visualisation with McNemar's test.Deep learning-based removal displayed the fistula site, feeding artery and draining vein more completely (median total anatomical score 6.00 versus 3.00;< 0.001 for both readers) and overall image quality was higher (5.00 versus 4.00;< 0.001). Objective vessel edge sharpness was concordant (316.47 ± 46.68 versus 273.70 ± 45.66 HU/mm;< 0.001). Technical visualisation was numerically higher (97.1% versus 88.6%) but not significantly so (= 0.248; three discordant pairs), which makes this endpoint inconclusive rather than negative. Post-processing time was shorter (40.56 ± 1.61 s versus 101.70 ± 4.39 s; mean paired difference 61.14 s, 95% CI 59.53 to 62.74 s; paired t test,< 0.001).In DSA-confirmed hAVF, deep learning-based bone removal displayed the structures that determine endovascular planning more completely than threshold-based removal and was about one minute faster per case. It does not replace DSA for definitive assessment of fistula architecture, and the apparent advantage at the cavernous sinus is exploratory and requires external validation in larger multicentre cohorts.

title: Association Between Breast Arterial Calcification on Mammography and Carotid Artery Stenosis on CT Angiography: A Retrospective Study in a Selected Cohort of Women Aged 60-65 Years.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: p p p Breast arterial calcification (BAC) is an incidental mammographic finding that may be associated with systemic vascular disease. We investigated the association between mammographic BAC and carotid artery stenosis on cervical computed tomography angiography (CTA) in a clinically selected cohort of postmenopausal women aged 60-65 years.This retrospective, single-center study screened 3421 women aged 60-65 years who underwent both mammography and cervical CTA between November 2021 and May 2025. CTA examinations requested from the emergency department or cardiology clinics, examinations not performed within the same calendar year, and prespecified clinical exclusions were removed, leaving 180 women who underwent outpatient CTA for nonspecific symptoms. The median interval between examinations was 131 days. BAC was graded on a 0-3 scale, and carotid stenosis was assessed according to the North American Symptomatic Carotid Endarterectomy Trial (NASCET) criteria, using the greater degree of stenosis on either side as the patient-level value. BAC was analyzed as an ordinal variable, as a categorical variable, and using binary definitions of presence and severity. Multivariable models were adjusted for age, diabetes mellitus, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, and smoking.Clinically significant stenosis (≥50%) was present in 44 women (24.4%). Its prevalence increased from 5.4% in BAC grade 0 to 75.0% in grade 3 (for trend < 0.001). Each one-grade increase in BAC was associated with clinically significant stenosis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 4.23; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.50-8.03;< 0.001). The corresponding aORs were 16.70 (95% CI, 4.99-73.27) for any BAC and 18.49 (95% CI, 5.93-70.46) for BAC grade ≥2. Adding BAC to the clinical model increased the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) from 0.90 to 0.96 (DeLong= 0.005); the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.95. Inter-reader agreement for BAC grading was substantial (weighted κ = 0.79).In this selected cohort of women aged 60-65 years who underwent clinically indicated CTA, BAC was associated with carotid artery stenosis independently of conventional cardiovascular risk factors. These findings do not establish BAC as a screening or prediction tool and require prospective, population-based validation.

CTA examinations requested from the emergency department or cardiology clinics, examinations not performed within the same calendar year, and prespecified clinical exclusions were removed, leaving 180 women who underwent outpatient CTA for nonspecific symptoms.

title: Development and internal validation of a clinical prediction model for postoperative venous thromboembolism after neurosurgical intervention in patients with traumatic brain injury.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a critical complication after traumatic brain injury (TBI) surgery. Conventional risk assessment tools were not developed for neurosurgical trauma populations, limiting their applicability. OBJECTIVE: To develop and internally validate an interpretable clinical prediction model for postoperative VTE in TBI surgery patients. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study enrolled 1,450 TBI patients who underwent surgery (2016-2024). Seven predictors were selected using Recursive Feature Elimination. Six machine learning algorithms were compared, with logistic regression (LR) selected as the final model. Performance was evaluated using AUC-ROC, calibration, and decision curve analysis. RESULTS: Among 1,450 patients, 205 (14.1%) developed postoperative VTE. The LR model achieved AUC-ROC of 0.868 (95% CI: 0.815-0.920) with good calibration (Brier score: 0.085). Seven predictors were identified: age, Barthel index, ASA classification, multiple surgeries, general anesthesia, limb AIS score, and serum magnesium. Compared with Caprini score (AUC: 0.686), the model showed improved discrimination (ΔAUC = 0.182; NRI: 0.559). CONCLUSION: An interpretable model based on seven routinely available variables demonstrated promising performance for postoperative VTE risk stratification in TBI surgery patients. A nomogram and web-based calculator are provided for clinical use.

title: A clinical-deep learning model for prolonged length of stay following endovascular aortic repair.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Prolonged length of stay (PLOS) after endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) for abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is associated with increased complications, resource burden, and patient distress. Early identification of high-risk patients remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a predictive model integrating clinical variables and three-dimensional deep learning (3D-DL) features from preoperative computed tomography angiography (CTA) to predict PLOS after EVAR. METHODS: A total of 788 patients with AAA who underwent elective EVAR were enrolled from two hospitals. The internal training cohort consisted of 556 patients, and the external validation cohort included 232 patients. PLOS was defined as a LOS above the 75th percentile of the distribution. A clinical nomogram was developed using LASSO regression followed by multivariate logistic regression. Deep learning (DL) features were extracted from manually segmented computed tomography angiography (CTA) images using a 3D ResNet200 network, and LASSO regression was applied to select the most informative features. An ensemble model integrating the clinical predictors and the selected DL features was constructed. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. RESULTS: LASSO combined with multivariate logistic regression identified five independent clinical predictors: age, hemoglobin, albumin, maximum aneurysm diameter, and diabetes. The clinical model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.917 in the internal cohort and 0.944 in the external cohort. From the 3D ResNet200 network, 32 DL features were extracted. LASSO regression further selected two of these features. The ensemble predictive model, which integrated the clinical predictors and DL features, demonstrated improved discrimination, with an AUC of 0.971 in the internal cohort and 0.958 in the external cohort. Internal validation with 1,000 bootstrap resamples yielded optimism-corrected AUCs of 0.911 for the clinical model and 0.966 for the ensemble model. Subgroup analyses demonstrated consistent model performance across age and diabetes strata, while performance in the female subgroup warrants further evaluation in larger cohorts. CONCLUSION: This study developed an ensemble predictive model to predict PLOS following EVAR. The model demonstrated excellent discrimination and provided significant prognostic value beyond clinical variables alone. This nomogram may serve as a preoperative tool for risk stratification and resource planning in this population. Future studies should focus on prospective validation and clinical integration.

title: Lipoprotein(a) and Triglycerides as Independent Predictors of Long-Term Aortoiliac Stent Failure After Endovascular Revascularisation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Restenosis and occlusion remain important after aortoiliac stenting, and device choice does not fully explain late patency loss. Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is implicated in atherosclerotic progression and residual vascular risk. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether baseline Lp(a) is associated with long-term restenosis or occlusion after aortoiliac stenting. METHODS: This post hoc biomarker analysis of COBEST included 125 patients and 168 treated iliac arteries randomised to the Advanta V12 covered stent (Atrium Medical Corporation, Hudson, NH, USA) or bare-metal stents for symptomatic aortoiliac occlusive disease. The primary outcome was loss of primary patency, defined as restenosis or occlusion during 5-year follow-up. Cox proportional hazards modelling and cumulative failure curves were the main analyses. RESULTS: p p p p In the Lp(a)-adjusted Cox model, covered stent use was associated with a lower hazard of restenosis or occlusion (HR, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.31-0.97;= 0.039), whereas each 1 mg/dL higher Lp(a) concentration was associated with a higher hazard (HR, 1.08; 95% CI, 1.06-1.10;< 0.001; equivalent to HR, 2.16; 95% CI, 1.79-2.59 per 10 mg/dL increase). In the biomarker-adjusted model, each 1 mg/dL higher Lp(a) concentration (HR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.02-1.08;< 0.001; HR, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.22-2.16 per 10 mg/dL increase) and each 1 mmol/L higher triglyceride concentration (HR, 1.89; 95% CI, 1.34-2.68;< 0.001) remained associated with restenosis or occlusion. CONCLUSIONS: Elevated Lp(a) and, to a lesser extent, triglycerides were independently associated with long-term aortoiliac stent failure after adjustment for stent type.

title: Advances in Design and Preparation of Biodegradable Inferior Vena Cava Filters.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with pulmonary embolism (PE) constituting its most fatal clinical consequence. Inferior vena cava filters (IVCFs) have been employed as a mechanical prophylactic strategy for patients with contraindications to anticoagulation or recurrent embolic events. However, permanent implantation and limited retrieval success are associated with device-related complications, including caval perforation, migration, fracture, and filter-induced thrombosis. Biodegradable IVCFs have been investigated as an alternative approach to provide temporary protection while avoiding the complications associated with long-term implantation. This review discusses recent advances in biodegradable IVCFs from a material perspective, focusing on material selection, structural design, degradation characteristics, and biological responses. Biodegradable polymers, degradable metallic materials, and shape-memory systems are evaluated regarding their mechanical stability, degradation behavior, vascular compatibility, and functional requirements. Strategies for improving radiopacity while preserving biodegradability are also summarized. Despite ongoing progress, key challenges remain in precisely controlling degradation kinetics, maintaining adequate mechanical support during the therapeutic period, and validating long-term safety through clinical studies. Further efforts in material optimization, biofunctional modification, and individualized fabrication may facilitate the future development of biodegradable IVCFs.

title: Redox Dysregulation in the Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Wall: Ferroptosis and Experimental Therapeutic Opportunities.
abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a spatially heterogeneous disease of the aortic wall for which no pharmacological treatment has reliably arrested enlargement. The term oxidative stress encompasses processes that differ in chemical form, anatomical location and cellular effect. This narrative review examines haem and redox-active iron, phospholipid peroxidation and antioxidant defence at the intraluminal thrombus-wall interface and within medial and inflammatory cells. We distinguish ferroptosis from redox effects on coagulation, migration and secretion and relate these functions to wall remodelling. Experimental studies show that manipulating iron uptake and ferritin turnover, membrane phospholipid susceptibility or peroxide detoxification can alter vascular smooth muscle cell survival, macrophage behaviour and aortic injury. The cellular function affected helps determine which process an intervention should preserve or suppress. Based on evidence from human tissue and animal models, we review opportunities to localise, manipulate and monitor these processes and assess their relevance to established AAA. Testing after confirmation of aneurysm formation, with target engagement in defined wall cells and parallel assessment of systemic effects, is needed to determine whether these approaches can limit continued enlargement.

title: Functional Benefit and Safety of Adjunctive Intra-Arterial Thrombolysis After Successful Endovascular Thrombectomy: An Updated and Cumulative Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: 2 p Adjunctive intra-arterial thrombolysis (IAT) after successful endovascular thrombectomy has been associated with a higher probability of excellent functional recovery in previous randomized-trial meta-analyses. Since those syntheses, the evidence base has expanded to include IAT-TOP, restricted to basilar artery occlusion, and CHOICE-2, in which 90-day mortality was 12.1% with adjunctive alteplase and 6.4% with thrombectomy alone. We therefore examined how the efficacy and mortality profiles changed as randomized evidence accumulated.This PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251006577). Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing adjunctive intra-arterial fibrinolytic therapy administered after trial-defined successful or near-successful post-thrombectomy reperfusion with no adjunctive intra-arterial fibrinolysis. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched through 15 August 2026, with ClinicalTrials.gov searched separately. Nine RCTs comprising 2828 randomized participants were included at the systematic-review level. Event counts were re-extracted from primary trial publications and pooled as risk ratios (RRs) using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals (CIs). Cumulative meta-analysis tracked how the efficacy and mortality estimates changed as evidence accumulated, while fragility analyses assessed the stability of the corresponding statistical inferences. This research received no external funding.Adjunctive IAT increased excellent functional recovery (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-1; 8 RCTs; RR 1.266, 95% CI 1.135-1.412; I= 0.0%), with a 95% prediction interval of 1.047-1.530 and a meta-analytic Fragility Index of 15. Ninety-day all-cause mortality did not differ significantly between groups (8 RCTs; RR 1.036, 95% CI 0.817-1.314); immediately before CHOICE-2 entered the cumulative synthesis, the corresponding estimate was RR 0.984 (95% CI 0.801-1.209). In the bidirectional reverse-fragility analysis, the earliest significance transition identified by the search occurred after 24 one-patient event-status modifications and was in the direction of increased mortality with adjunctive IAT (RR 1.174, 95% CI 1.002-1.377;= 0.048). No transition toward reduced mortality was identified through the same modification depth. No trial was judged to be at high risk of bias using RoB 2. GRADE certainty was moderate for excellent functional recovery, 90-day mortality, and functional independence and low for hemorrhagic outcomes.The efficacy and mortality components of the benefit-risk profile of adjunctive IAT have not evolved in parallel. The improvement in excellent functional recovery persisted as randomized evidence accumulated and remained comparatively stable to perturbation of the observed event data, whereas mortality remains unresolved. The cumulative and reverse-fragility findings do not establish a treatment-related mortality excess; however, the absence of statistical significance should not be interpreted as affirmative evidence of mortality neutrality. The current randomized evidence therefore supports a reproducible functional benefit while preserving clinically relevant uncertainty regarding survival.

title: Association of Estimated Arterial Stiffness with Collateral Status and Functional Outcome after Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Secondary Analysis of the OPTIMAL-BP Trial.
abstract: PURPOSE: Estimated pulse wave velocity (ePWV) is a surrogate of arterial stiffness that may influence stroke outcomes and potentially affect collateral circulation. We examined the association of ePWV with collateral status and 3-month functional outcome after successful endovascular thrombectomy and explored the contribution of collateral status to this relationship across blood pressure (BP) management strategies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this secondary analysis of the Outcome in Patients Treated With Intra-Arterial Thrombectomy-Optimal Blood Pressure Control trial, 285 patients were analyzed. Collateral status was assessed using the Tan scale (poor, 0-1; good, 2-3). Poor functional outcome was defined as 3-month modified Rankin Scale score of 3-6. Multivariable logistic and mediation analyses were performed to evaluate the association between ePWV and functional outcomes and to explore direct and indirect pathways. RESULTS: A total of 285 patients were included (mean age, 73.3±11.3 years; 40.4% women). Each 1 m/s increase in ePWV was associated with poor collaterals (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 1.276, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.083-1.503) and poor functional outcome (adjusted OR 1.338, 95% CI 1.121-1.597). In mediation analyses, collateral status accounted for only a small proportion of the association between ePWV and poor functional outcome (indirect effect: adjusted β 0.022, 95% CI 0.001-0.053), whereas the direct effect remained significant (adjusted β 0.237, 95% CI 0.115-0.359). Neither the direct effect of ePWV on functional outcome nor the indirect effect through collateral status differed according to BP management strategy. CONCLUSION: Higher ePWV was associated with poor collateral status and unfavorable functional outcome after successful reperfusion. Collateral status accounted for only a small proportion of the observed association between ePWV and functional outcome.

title: Vascular Access Complexity and Thrombectomy Efficiency in Proximal MCA M1 Occlusion: Evaluation of the Bovine Aortic Arch-Dolichoarteriopathy Score.
abstract: Background and Objectives: Materials and Methods: n n Results: p p p p p Conclusions: In this study, it was aimed to investigate the relationship between the Bovine Aortic Arch-Dolichoarteriopathy (B.A.D.) score and the procedural characteristics of mechanical thrombectomy, recanalization success, and 90-day functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke with proximal M1 occlusion of the middle cerebral artery (MCA).A total of 220 adult patients who underwent mechanical thrombectomy for proximal MCA M1 occlusion were included in this retrospective, single-center cohort study. The patients were divided into good B.A.D. (<2;= 143) and poor B.A.D. (≥2;= 77) groups. Admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) and Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) scores, collateral status, thrombectomy time intervals, number of passes, first-pass effect (FPE), and Modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (mTICI) recanalization grades were evaluated. The primary outcome was functional independence at day 90 (mRS 0-2). Associations with procedural and clinical outcomes were evaluated using multivariable logistic and linear regression analyses.The puncture-to-recanalization time was significantly longer in the poor B.A.D. group [67 (50.5-88.0) min vs. 43 (32.0-65.0) min,< 0.001], and the FPE rate was lower (37.7% vs. 51.7%,= 0.046). After adjustment for thrombectomy technique and clinical covariates, poor B.A.D. remained independently associated with lower odds of FPE success (aOR = 0.439, 95% CI: 0.229-0.839;= 0.013). In the procedurally adjusted linear regression model, poor B.A.D. also remained independently associated with longer puncture-to-recanalization time after additional adjustment for the number of thrombectomy passes and thrombectomy technique (B = 0.294, 95% CI: 0.188-0.400;< 0.001). Final mTICI ≥ 2b, ≥2c, and 3 recanalization rates did not differ between the groups. Although 90-day functional independence was lower in the poor B.A.D. group, the difference was not significant (51.9% vs. 63.6%,= 0.092), and no statistically significant independent association between B.A.D. status and 90-day functional independence was observed in the multivariable analysis.Poor B.A.D. anatomy was associated with greater procedural complexity during mechanical thrombectomy for proximal MCA M1 occlusion, including longer puncture-to-recanalization time and lower odds of FPE success, even after adjustment for available procedural and clinical factors. However, no statistically significant independent association was demonstrated between B.A.D. status and 90-day functional independence, and final recanalization rates did not differ significantly between the groups. These findings suggest that the B.A.D. score may have potential value as a preprocedural marker of vascular access complexity; however, prospective external validation is required before its use for procedural planning can be recommended.

title: Early outcomes of the Octapro balloon-expandable transcatheter heart valve in an unrestricted cohort of patients with aortic valve stenosis: the MyPro registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Data on early outcomes of the novel balloon-expandable (BE) Octapro transcatheter heart valve (THV) in real-world practice are limited. We sought to assess procedural safety and early outcomes of the Octapro in patients with severe native aortic stenosis (AS) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). METHODS: Between November 2024 and October 2025, consecutive patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI with Octapro in European and Indian centres were enrolled. Primary endpoints were VARC-3 technical success, device success, and early safety at 30-day. RESULTS: 2 A total of 303 patients were included (age 78.9 ± 7.4 years; bicuspid 13%). VARC-3 technical success was 97%, peri-procedural mortality 0.3% while no procedural stroke or myocardial infarction were reported. In-hospital guidelines-indicated permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) rate was 13.5%. At discharge mean gradient was 8.4 ± 4.5 mmHg, effective orifice area 1.8 ± 0.3 cm, while moderate-to-severe paravalvular leak was reported in 3.3% of the patients. At 30-day, device success was 92.4% and early safety 80%. All-cause mortality was 2.6%, stroke 0.3%, and guidelines-indicated PPI 14.2%. Mean gradient remained low (9 ± 4 mmHg). Implantation depth and baseline right bundle branch block (RBBB) were independent predictors of PPI. ROC analysis identified an implantation depth threshold of 4.75 mm associated with increased PPI risk. CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world registry, the Octapro THV demonstrated high procedural success, favourable early clinical outcomes, and excellent haemodynamic performance. Implantation depth and baseline RBBB were independent predictors of PPI, supporting optimization of implantation technique to mitigate conduction disturbances.

title: Development and Internal Validation of the Si-AAA Prognostic Score for Five-Year Overall Survival after Endovascular Aneurysm Repair in Patients with Asymptomatic Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although endovascular aneurysm repair is widely used for the treatment of asymptomatic abdominal aortic aneurysm, long-term survival is influenced by patient comorbidities and aneurysm-related characteristics. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a prognostic scoring system for predicting 5-year overall survival after endovascular aneurysm repair. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted in patients with asymptomatic abdominal aortic aneurysm undergoing endovascular aneurysm repair. Candidate predictors included demographic, clinical, aneurysm-related, and laboratory variables. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression was used to identify independent predictors of 5-year mortality. Continuous predictors were categorized using clinically interpretable thresholds derived from time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis, and a simplified point-based score was constructed from regression coefficients. Model performance was assessed using Harrell's concordance index, and internal validation was performed using 1,000 bootstrap resamples to obtain an optimism-corrected concordance index. Calibration was evaluated using bootstrap-based calibration plots. RESULTS: A total of 445 patients were screened, and 443 complete cases were included in the final analysis. During follow-up, 133 deaths (30.0%) occurred. The estimated 5-year overall survival rate was 62.8% (95% confidence interval [CI], 57.8%-68.0%). Independent predictors of 5-year mortality included age >70 years (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 1.66, 95% CI 1.06-2.62; P = 0.029), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (aHR 1.70, 95% CI 1.08-2.69; P = 0.023), unfit status (aHR 2.32, 95% CI 1.58-3.39; P < 0.001), serum albumin ≤3.5 g/dL (aHR 2.80, 95% CI 1.97-3.98; P < 0.001), and abdominal aortic aneurysm diameter ≥7 cm (aHR 1.59, 95% CI 1.07-2.38; P = 0.023). The final score ranged from 0 to 7. The apparent concordance index was 0.721, with an optimism-corrected concordance index of 0.713 after bootstrap validation. Risk stratification showed clear separation among low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups (5-year overall survival: 82.5%, 53.4%, and 23.8%, respectively; log-rank P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: A simple prognostic scoring system incorporating age, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, unfit status, serum albumin, and aneurysm diameter demonstrated acceptable discrimination and good calibration for predicting 5-year overall survival after endovascular aneurysm repair. This tool may assist in risk stratification and long-term clinical decision-making. As this score was derived and internally validated in a single-center cohort, external validation in independent cohorts is required before routine clinical implementation.

This study aimed to develop and internally validate a prognostic scoring system for predicting 5-year overall survival after endovascular aneurysm repair. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted in patients with asymptomatic abdominal aortic aneurysm undergoing endovascular aneurysm repair.

title: Sex-Based Disparities in Statin Use and Intensity among Women with Peripheral Artery Disease: A Systematic Review.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is a manifestation of systemic atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and is associated with substantial cardiovascular and limb-related morbidity. High-intensity statin therapy is recommended for patients with PAD, yet statin treatment remains underused, and sex-based differences in lipid-lowering therapy may further contribute to inequities in secondary prevention. This systematic review evaluated sex-based disparities in statxin use and statin intensity among adults with PAD. METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Cochrane CENTRAL was performed from database inception through June 6, 2026. Eligible studies included adults with PAD, reported PAD-specific statin or lipid-lowering outcomes, and compared outcomes by sex. The primary outcome was high-intensity statin use among women versus men with PAD. Secondary outcomes included any statin use, no statin therapy, guideline-concordant lipid-lowering or vascular-protective therapy, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) goal achievement. Findings were synthesized narratively because of heterogeneity in study design, PAD definition, clinical setting, and outcome reporting. RESULTS: Eleven observational studies met inclusion criteria. Only two studies reported high-intensity statin use by sex, and both found lower use among women than men. In the Medicare cohort of patients with critical limb ischemia, high-intensity statin use was lower among women than men. Similarly, in the Veterans Affairs cohort, women with PAD had lower rates of high-intensity statin use, any statin use, and statin adherence. Across studies reporting secondary lipid-lowering outcomes, women were generally less likely than men to receive statins or guideline-concordant vascular-protective therapy, including in primary care, hospital discharge, revascularization, administrative claims, and vascular registry settings. LDL-C goal achievement was not reported in the included studies. CONCLUSION: Women with PAD are less likely than men to receive statin therapy and guideline-concordant vascular-protective treatment, and the limited available evidence suggests lower use of high-intensity statins among women when statin intensity is reported. These findings highlight a persistent sex-based gap in secondary prevention for PAD. Future studies should report statin intensity, adherence, LDL-C goal achievement, treatment escalation, and standardized measures of statin tolerance or intolerance separately by sex. Quality-improvement efforts should also focus on improving statin prescribing for women with PAD.

This systematic review evaluated sex-based disparities in statxin use and statin intensity among adults with PAD.

title: Antiphospholipid syndrome: epidemiology and outcomes in the evolving criteria era.
abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is a heterogeneous autoimmune thrombo-inflammatory disorder characterized by thrombosis, pregnancy morbidity and an expanding spectrum of microvascular, cardiac, haematological and other systemic manifestations. Although research has provided considerable insights into the pathogenesis and clinical phenotypes of APS, its epidemiology remains difficult to define because estimates depend on case definitions, antibody testing, repeat-testing requirements, testing practices and data sources. Population-based studies suggest that APS is rare, and catastrophic APS is rarer and best understood through registry data. Antiphospholipid antibody positivity alone does not establish APS; transient or low-level positivity can occur without disease, whereas persistent antibodies must be interpreted alongside compatible clinical manifestations. Despite its rarity, APS causes substantial morbidity through recurrent thrombosis, organ damage and adverse pregnancy outcomes, supporting targeted evaluation in unprovoked or recurrent venous thromboembolism, stroke in younger adults and selected pregnancy complications. Apparent differences among populations can reflect ascertainment, access to testing, study design and biological variation. Standardized case definitions, antibody testing and laboratory reporting, together with longitudinal population-based research in ancestry-diverse, paediatric and low-income and middle-income populations, are needed to refine estimates of APS burden and define its clinical spectrum.

title: Mechanical Thrombectomy Versus Anticoagulation Alone in Intermediate-High Risk PE: Improved Functional 90-Day Outcomes in STORM-PE RCT.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Up to 50% of pulmonary embolism (PE) survivors experience long-term functional limitations and reduced quality of life (QoL). Reperfusion strategies can rapidly relieve right-ventricular (RV) dysfunction and prevent clinical deterioration or hemodynamic collapse; however, these approaches have never been evaluated in a randomized trial against anticoagulation alone using patient-centered outcomes. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate whether mechanical thrombectomy with anticoagulation improves functional, QoL, and safety outcomes compared with anticoagulation alone in patients with acute intermediate-high risk PE over 90 days. METHODS: STORM-PE enrolled 100 PE patients randomized 1:1 to computer-assisted vacuum thrombectomy (CAVT) with anticoagulation or anticoagulation alone across 22 international sites, with RV-to-left-ventricular (RV/LV) ratio change at 48 hours as the primary endpoint. Secondary endpoints included major adverse events within 7 days, functional and QoL outcomes, mortality, and symptomatic PE recurrence through 90 days. RESULTS: For all patients, median time from randomization to last follow-up visit was 91.0 days [Q1-Q3: 80.5-100.0]. At 90 days, 66.0% (31/47) of CAVT and 64.2% (34/53) of anticoagulation patients completed the 6-min walk test. The CAVT arm exhibited a longer 6-min walk distance compared with anticoagulation alone (478.7 ± 159.5 m vs 368.0 ± 127.8 m, P = 0.003). More CAVT than anticoagulation patients were NYHA functional class I (97.4% [37/38] vs 75.6% [34/45], P = 0.005) at 90 days. Dyspnea and QoL scores were comparable between groups, with no differences between arms for all-cause mortality, PE-related mortality, and symptomatic PE recurrence within 90 days. CONCLUSIONS: In STORM-PE, CAVT with anticoagulation resulted in improved functional outcomes at 90 days compared with anticoagulation alone, with equivalent safety rates. This trial supports CAVT as an effective and safe reperfusion strategy for intermediate-high risk PE. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: https://clinicaltrials.gov Unique Identifier: NCT05684796.

title: Recanalisation quality, not first-pass effect, drives outcomes in paediatric mechanical thrombectomy: a multicentre prospective study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: In adult endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), first-pass success is associated with better outcomes, but whether this "first-pass effect" also holds true in childhood stroke remains unknown. We investigated the association of thrombectomy pass counts with 90-day outcomes after paediatric EVT. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We analysed prospectively collected data from the international Save ChildS Pro registry (ages 0-17 years). All EVT-treated patients were included irrespective of the reperfusion grade achieved. Successful reperfusion was defined as expanded thrombolysis in cerebral infarction (eTICI) ≥ 2b and complete/near-complete reperfusion as eTICI 2c-3. The primary outcome was ordinal 90-day mRS in a proportional odds model. Single-pass and multiple-pass patients were then compared with each other within the subgroup achieving eTICI 2c-3. Logistic regression for mRS > 2 was fitted with pass count and eTICI grade as covariates. RESULTS: Of 103 patients (median age 11 years [IQR 6-15]; 55/102 [53.9%] male), median passes were 2 (IQR 1-3); 39 (37.9%) had 1 pass, 61 (59.2%) more than 1 and 3 (2.9%) recanalised without a thrombectomy pass. Multiple passes were associated with lower eTICI 2c-3 rates (30.0% vs 82.1%; P < .001), and worse 90-day mRS (common odds ratio 3.47; 95% CI, 1.63-7.38; P = .001). However, among patients achieving eTICI 2c-3 (n = 50), we detected no difference by pass count (mRS 0-2: 93.8% vs 94.4%; risk difference - 0.6%, 95% CI, -15% to +20%; P = 1.000). After accounting for eTICI, pass count was not independently associated with mRS > 2, while eTICI remained significant. CONCLUSIONS: In this analysis of the first-pass effect in paediatric thrombectomy, multiple passes were associated with worse functional outcomes, but this effect appeared to be largely mediated through recanalisation quality. Subgroup analyses were underpowered to exclude a clinically relevant residual effect of pass count, and these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating.

title: Comparative Outcomes of Carotid Artery Stenting, Transcarotid Artery Revascularization, and Carotid Endarterectomy in Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis: A Propensity-Matched Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: To compare myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, mortality, and major adverse events (MAEs) after carotid artery stenting (CAS), transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR), and carotid endarterectomy (CEA). METHODS: Using TriNetX, adults undergoing CAS, TCAR, or CEA for asymptomatic carotid stenosis from 2015 to 2025 were identified using International Classification of Diseases 10th Edition Procedure Coding System (ICD-10-PCS) codes. Asymptomatic status required no stroke or transient ischemic attack within 6 months before surgery. Propensity score matching was performed for CAS versus TCAR (5,558 pairs), TCAR versus CEA (9,666 pairs), and CAS versus CEA (13,707 pairs). Outcomes through 1 year were assessed using risk ratios (RRs) kand Kaplan-Meier analyses. RESULTS: At 1 year, CAS was associated with higher stroke risk than TCAR (5.16% vs 3.74%; RR 1.31; P = 0.002) and CEA (4.92% vs 3.47%; RR 1.44; P < 0.001), whereas TCAR and CEA were similar (3.91% vs 3.79%; P = 0.52). CAS had lower mortality than TCAR (3.78% vs 7.65%; RR 0.49; P < 0.001), but mortality was similar in the other comparisons. MI was lower after CAS than TCAR (2.03% vs 2.95%; RR 0.63; P < 0.001), with no differences otherwise. MAE was higher after CAS than CEA (7.66% vs 6.46%; RR 1.20; P < 0.001), but similar between CAS and TCAR and between TCAR and CEA. CONCLUSION: Among patients selected for revascularization, CAS was associated with higher stroke risk than TCAR and CEA, lower MI and mortality than TCAR, and higher MAE than CEA. These observational findings complement randomized evidence and require cautious interpretation given residual confounding and unavailable anatomic data.

title: Failure Modes of Endovascular Therapy for Spontaneous Isolated Superior Mesenteric Artery Dissection.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Mechanisms of failure after endovascular stenting for symptomatic spontaneous isolated superior mesenteric artery dissection (SISMAD) remain poorly characterized. We analyzed device- and procedure-related failure modes in a 17-year single-center cohort. METHODS: We reviewed 117 consecutive patients with SISMAD (2008-2025). Patients stented for persistent or escalating pain despite conservative management formed the cohort; catheter-infusion and open-surgery patients were analyzed separately. Lesions were classified by Yun morphology. Failure modes were classified a priori as type I (intraprocedural technical failure), type II (thrombotic events occurring after the procedure), and type III (in-stent restenosis or intimal hyperplasia at ≥6 months). Patency and reinterventions were recorded. RESULTS: Thirty-two patients underwent endovascular therapy (28 stenting, 4 catheter-directed infusion). In the stent cohort, uncomplicated technical success was 82.1% (23/28). Type I failures occurred in 17.9% (5/28), dominated by false-lumen deployment (10.7%) clustered in Yun III occlusions (50.0% vs. 9.1%; P = 0.050). Type II events (3 weeks; 24 months) were rescued by reintervention. Type III events developed in 22.7% (5/22), confined to multi-stent constructs (45.5% vs. 0%; P = 0.035). Primary patency was 81.8% (18/22) at a median 19-month imaging follow-up; secondary patency was 100% after 3 reinterventions. Greater baseline true-lumen stenosis and Yun III morphology predicted composite events. No patient died; the only bowel resection preceded secondary stenting. CONCLUSION: Endovascular therapy for SISMAD fails in characteristic, morphology-dependent patterns. The proposed three-type classification is exploratory and requires validation in larger cohorts.

title: Contemporary Outcomes of Isolated Common Femoral Endarterectomy in the Endovascular Era.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Common femoral endarterectomy (CFE) remains the reference treatment for common femoral artery (CFA) occlusive disease, yet contemporary real-world data focused specifically on isolated CFE remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical profile, operative characteristics, and outcomes of isolated CFE performed in a tertiary vascular surgery center, with particular emphasis on postoperative complications, reintervention and occlusion, as well as the possible influence of wound closure technique and hemostatic adjunct use on local morbidity. METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted including consecutive patients who underwent isolated CFE between January 2013 and December 2023. Baseline characteristics, clinical presentation, lesion complexity, operative details, postoperative complications, reinterventions, and postoperative occlusion were analyzed. Lesions were classified according to Trans-Atlantic Inter-Society Consensus II (TASC II). Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to assess freedom from occlusion, while Cox regression was performed to explore factors associated with postoperative occlusion. Fisher's exact test was used to assess associations between wound closure technique, hemostatic adjunct use, and postoperative complications. RESULTS: A total of 96 patients underwent 100 isolated CFEs. The mean age was 68.5 ± 9 years, 89% were male, and 63% presented with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). Most lesions were classified as TASC A-B (68%). The median follow up was 3.5 years (95% confidence interval [CI], 3.2-3.9). Early postoperative complications were predominantly local, including groin hematoma (4%), lymphatic leakage (4%), lymphocele (5%), pseudoaneurysm (2%), and infection (8%). Overall, 18% of procedures required reintervention, with 14% undergoing open and 4% endovascular reintervention. Nine occlusive events occurred during follow up. Estimated freedom from occlusion was 100% at 30 days, 96% at 1 year, and 86% at 5 years. TASC C-D lesions showed a numerically higher occlusion rate than TASC A-B lesions (12.5% vs. 7.4%; OR, 1.80), although this difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.462). In univariable Cox regression, aspirin therapy was the only variable significantly associated with lower risk of postoperative occlusion (hazard ratio [HR], 0.20; P = 0.026). Neither intradermal wound closure nor hemostatic adjunct use was significantly associated with postoperative complications. CONCLUSION: Isolated CFE remains a safe and durable treatment for CFA occlusive disease, with low rates of early local complications, acceptable reintervention rates and good freedom from occlusion during follow up. These findings support the continued role of isolated CFE as the reference treatment for CFA disease in the endovascular era.

title: Use of smart glasses for ultrasound-guided central venous catheterization in adults: a randomized clinical trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Head-mounted displays can be integrated with ultrasonography to overlay the image in the operator's field of view, improving hand-eye coordination during invasive procedures. The clinical efficacy of smart glasses for central venous catheterization (CVC) remains uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate whether using smart glasses can improve efficiency compared to conventional ultrasound-guided CVC. METHODS: This prospective, single-blinded, controlled study enrolled adult patients who underwent elective surgery requiring CVC. Patients were assigned to either the ultrasound screen (control) or smart glasses group using stratified randomization according to operator qualification. The primary outcome was the overall CVC procedural time. Secondary outcomes included ultrasound scanning and venous access time, number of needle redirections and probe repositionings, procedural success and complication rates. RESULTS: In total, 124 patients were analyzed. The overall procedural time was significantly reduced in the smart glasses group compared to that in the control group (158 [140, 189] s vs. 134 [117,150] s; median difference, 26.0 s; 95% CI, [16.0-37.0] s, P < 0.001). Specifically, the ultrasound scanning time (median difference, 3.0 s, P = 0.004), venous access time (median difference, 2.0 s, P = 0.013), number of needle redirections (median difference, 1.0, P = 0.003) and probe repositionings (median difference, 0.0, P = 0.005) were significantly reduced in the smart glasses group compared to those in the control group. However, the success and complication rates were comparable between groups. CONCLUSIONS: Smart glasses modestly improved procedural efficiency in ultrasound-guided CVC, potientially for novices, without improving success or complication rates. Larger-sample studies with more diverse operators and patients are warranted. title: Endovascular Management With a Fenestration Technique of an Iatrogenic Thoracic Chronic Type B Aortic Dissection.
abstract: We report the case of an 86-year-old woman who developed an intraoperative type B aortic dissection during ascending aortic replacement for an ascending aortic aneurysm. Postoperative imaging demonstrated an uncomplicated dissection extending to the infrarenal aorta. At 10 weeks, follow-up imaging revealed rapid aneurysmal expansion of the false lumen. Thoracic endovascular aortic repair was performed with adjunctive cerebrospinal fluid drainage, rapid pacing, and image fusion guidance. An intimal fenestration technique was used to optimize the distal sealing zone, extending the disruption from a pre-existing re-entry tear. A type Ib endoleak necessitated additional stent-graft deployment, which in turn caused occlusion of the left renal and superior mesenteric arteries. The STABILISE technique (stent-assisted balloon-induced intimal disruption and relamination in aortic dissection repair) with a PETTICOAT (Provisional Extension To Induce Complete Attachment) bare stent restored renal perfusion, and targeted stenting re-established mesenteric flow. A postprocedural pseudoaneurysm was managed conservatively and resolved with spontaneous thrombosis within 48 hours. The patient was discharged on postoperative day seven, asymptomatic, with complete exclusion of the dissection, patent visceral vessels, and no endoleak confirmed at six-week follow-up. This case illustrates that combining distal flap fenestration with STABILISE relamination and a comprehensive endovascular toolkit can successfully manage complex chronic type B aortic dissections, even in elderly, high-risk patients-provided that adequate perioperative safety measures and a broad endovascular armamentarium are available to address unanticipated complications.

Postoperative imaging demonstrated an uncomplicated dissection extending to the infrarenal aorta. At 10 weeks, follow-up imaging revealed rapid aneurysmal expansion of the false lumen.

title: Sequential Arch-Tear Eligibility for Uncovered Aortic Arch Stent in Acute DeBakey Type I Aortic Dissection.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Because an uncovered arch scaffold does not provide a covered seal across an unresected arch tear, we evaluated a source-adjudicated sequential eligibility framework separating study-defined stop gates from residual-risk modifiers. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 266 patients with acute DeBakey type I dissection treated by hemiarch repair alone (No. = 160) or hemiarch plus AMDS (No. = 106). Blinded preoperative CT-scan re-review validated Gate 1 (visible arch tear), and operative-report review confirmed Gate 2 (tear directly observed at open inspection). Supra-aortic false-lumen communication was assessed only after both gates were negative. RESULTS: p p p Sixty-nine patients (25.9%) passed both study-defined gates (AMDS = 32; hemiarch = 37). Twelve-month CT-scan was available in 45/69 (65.2%; AMDS 24/32, hemiarch 21/37). Among imaged patients, complete zone 2-3 false-lumen exclusion occurred in 20/24 (83.3%) after AMDS and 0/21 after hemiarch (risk difference +83.3 percentage points, 95% CI +58.7 to +93.3;< 0.001). DANE occurred in 4/32 (12.5%) and 16/37 (43.2%), respectively (= 0.007). Under the adverse opposing missingness scenario, the exclusion risk difference narrowed to +19.3 percentage points (95% CI -4.2 to +39.9;= 0.148). CONCLUSIONS: These findings are hypothesis-generating and apply to a selected post hoc subgroup; treatment comparisons are non-causal. Prospective external validation of the study-defined hierarchy remains required.

title: Baricitinib Efficacy Through 4 Years in Responders and Safety up to 5 Years in Adults with Severe Alopecia Areata: Final Results from BRAVE-AA1 and BRAVE-AA2.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Long-term efficacy and safety data are imperative for therapies used to treat severe alopecia areata (AA) because the disease is chronic, loss of response can be devastating to patients, and the safety profile needs to support long-term therapy. Baricitinib, a selective JAK inhibitor, has been approved for severe AA in adults and is being studied in pediatric patients. This study evaluates the final long-term efficacy and safety of baricitinib in adults with severe AA. METHODS: Efficacy was assessed for patients randomized to baricitinib 4 mg or 2 mg who achieved response (Severity of Alopecia Tool [SALT] score ≤ 20) at Week 52 (4 mg, N = 133; 2 mg, N = 72) and stayed on the same dose through Week 200. Proportions of patients maintaining a SALT score ≤ 20 and achieving a Clinician-Reported Outcome Measure for Eyebrow/Eyelash (EB/EL) Hair Loss™ score of 0 or 1 with ≥ 2-point improvement from baseline were reported using the modified last-observation-carried-forward method. Safety is reported as incidence rates (IR) per 100 patient-years at risk for the All BARI AA group (N = 1303) and Extended BARI AA group (N = 948) through 248 weeks of exposure RESULTS: For baricitinib 4 mg and 2 mg, respectively, among Week 52 responders, 115/133 (86.5%) and 61/72 (84.7%) maintained a SALT score ≤ 20 at Week 200. Regrowth of EB/EL hair continued beyond Week 52 and was maintained through Week 200. In up to 5 years of exposure with baricitinib, the IR for serious infections, nonmelanoma skin cancer malignancies, deep vein thrombosis/pulmonary embolism, and major adverse cardiovascular events remained low relative to background rates. No deaths occurred, and adverse event rates remained stable over time. CONCLUSIONS: Within this population, ~ 85% of responders maintained SALT scores ≤ 20 through approximately 4 years with continued benefit for EB/EL. Baricitinib's safety profile remained consistent over 5 years of treatment, in line with prior BRAVE program findings. title: Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis in Hospitalized Medical Patients: A Narrative Review of Risk Stratification, Treatment Duration, and Bleeding Trade-Offs.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains a leading preventable cause of morbidity and mortality in hospitalized medical patients, yet decisions about who should receive prophylaxis - and for how long - remain far from settled. This review synthesizes evidence from 22 sources, including randomized trials, prospective and retrospective cohorts, systematic reviews, and major society guidelines, addressing risk stratification, in-hospital anticoagulant prophylaxis, extended-duration direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), the associated bleeding trade-offs, and real-world implementation. The evidence broadly supports pharmacologic prophylaxis during hospitalization for appropriately selected, acutely ill medical patients with acceptable bleeding risk, with the strongest randomized evidence favoring low-molecular-weight heparin during the inpatient period. That benefit comes with trade-offs worth weighing carefully, since even well-supported regimens carry a measurable increase in bleeding risk alongside their protective effect. Commonly used risk-assessment tools have real limitations as well: the Padua and IMPROVE scores offer a useful clinical framework, but head-to-head comparison shows both discriminate poorly between patients who will and won't develop VTE, and real-world implementation data reveal frequent misclassification and inconsistent dose administration. Extended-duration anticoagulation after discharge follows a similar pattern across the major DOAC trials in this space - fewer thrombotic events, but more bleeding, without a clear survival benefit. Taken together, this evidence points toward a risk-adapted rather than protocol-driven approach: assess VTE and bleeding risk at admission, initiate appropriate inpatient prophylaxis, reassess as the clinical picture changes, confirm that prescribed doses are actually being given, and reserve extended anticoagulation after discharge for carefully selected patients rather than applying it as a default. Meaningful progress in this area will likely come less from another static risk score and more from models that can track mobility, bleeding risk, and treatment response dynamically over the course of a hospital stay.

title: Artificial Intelligence in 3D Aortic CTA Segmentation for Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Management: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Computed tomography angiography (CTA) is the reference imaging modality for diagnosis, endovascular planning, and surveillance of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs), but conventional assessment remains time-consuming, operator-dependent, and limited by complex anatomy. This narrative review examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in three-dimensional aortic CTA segmentation for AAA management. The narrative synthesis drew on literature identified through PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and the Cochrane Library, with the original search covering January 2000 to July 2026. Ten primary studies from the existing bibliography were characterized in a study-level table, and reported Dice coefficients were displayed for nine studies. Current evidence indicates that AI-based segmentation, particularly using convolutional neural networks, U-Net-derived models, and nnU-Net frameworks, can improve the speed and reproducibility of aortic lumen, wall, thrombus, branch vessel, endograft, and aneurysm sac delineation. These techniques may support more accurate morphometric measurements, device sizing, procedural planning, quantitative surveillance, and the development of advanced imaging biomarkers. However, available studies remain heterogeneous in datasets, anatomical evaluation, imaging protocols, validation strategies, and reported performance metrics, limiting direct comparison and clinical generalizability. AI-assisted 3D segmentation represents a promising tool for transforming CTA from descriptive imaging into quantitative decision support, but robust multicenter validation, workflow integration, and expert supervision remain essential before widespread clinical adoption.

title: Selective endovascular aortic repair in connective tissue disease patients within a multidisciplinary program achieves comparable outcomes in high-risk patients.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Endovascular aortic repair (ENDO) in patients with connective tissue disease (CTD) has historically been discouraged in society guidelines because of durability concerns. However, high-volume aortic centers increasingly employ ENDO strategies in carefully selected high-risk patients across scenarios such as rupture, dissection-related pathology, or hostile anatomy. Herein, we describe temporal ENDO adoption at our multidisciplinary CTD aortic program. METHODS: In this study, 92 patients with CTD undergoing aortic intervention at a single high-volume aortic center between 2005 and 2023 were analyzed. Patients were stratified by ENDO (n = 50) vs open repair (OPEN; n = 42). The primary outcome was freedom from aortic-related mortality (ARM). The secondary outcomes included technical success, complications, secondary aortic intervention (SAI), and overall survival. A prespecified contemporary analysis (2018-2023) was conducted to evaluate the outcomes following the establishment of a multidisciplinary CTD aortic program. The Kaplan-Meier method was used to estimate survival and freedom from SAI. RESULTS: The mean age was 48 ± 16 years, and 34% (n = 31) were female. Diagnoses included Marfan syndrome (69%), Loeys-Dietz syndrome (15%), familial aortopathy (11%), and vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (5%). Patients who underwent ENDO more frequently had prior sternotomy/open cardiac surgery (68% vs 19%; P < .0001), prior aortic surgery (70% vs 33%; P = .0007), and urgent presentation (50% vs 14%; P = .0004). Overall, 60% of these patients were deemed unfit for open repair by the multidisciplinary aortic team because of physiologic risk, anatomic complexity, or urgent presentation. The technical success rate was lower after ENDO (82% vs 98%; P = .02), and the 30-day reintervention rate was higher (16% vs 0%; P = .01). The median follow-up period was 2.3 years [interquartile range, 1.1-4.7]. SAIs occurred more frequently following ENDO (56% vs 12%; P = .0001), including planned staged procedures (ENDO: 28.6% vs OPEN: 20%; P = 1) and unplanned reinterventions (ENDO: 71.4% vs OPEN: 80%; P = 1). In the full cohort, patients undergoing ENDO had lower 3-year survival rates (71% ± 7% vs 92% ± 4%; log-rank P = .03). In the contemporary cohort, survival at 2 years following ENDO (n = 17) was poorer than that after OPEN (n = 42), although the difference did not reach significance (71% ± 14% vs 92% ± 4%; log-rank P = .1). Similarly, the rate of freedom from ARM was lower, but not significantly different (88% ± 12% vs 98% ± 2%; log-rank P = .4). CONCLUSIONS: Open repair remains the gold standard for connective tissue disease-associated aortic disease. In carefully selected high-risk patients, ENDO serves as a complementary strategy with acceptable contemporary survival and comparable freedom from ARM. Higher secondary intervention rates reflect both planned staged repair and unplanned surveillance-detected failure modes, underscoring the need for lifelong follow-up within multidisciplinary programs.

title: Impact of Undertreated Antithrombotic Therapy on Adverse Patient Outcomes: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
abstract: Antithrombotic therapy undertreatment includes omission, nonadherence, underdosing, and clinical circumstances that result in subtherapeutic antithrombotic levels. Antithrombotic undertreatment has profound implications for patient safety, public health, and healthcare costs. Due to deviation from evidence-based clinical practice, misperceptions of bleeding versus thrombotic risk, and inequities in healthcare access, many patients with atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism, or peripheral artery disease remain untreated or receive suboptimal anticoagulant dosing. Antithrombotic undertreatment has been shown to increase rates of ischemic stroke, systemic embolism, recurrent thrombosis, and mortality. Real-world data continue to highlight substantial gaps in care, which appear to be magnified in patients with inequity in social determinants of health. The emergence of antithrombotic stewardship, in concert with growing bodies of literature on antithrombotic agent underdosing, represents a transformative opportunity to address these gaps through structured, interprofessional, and evidence-based approaches. Through interdisciplinary collaboration, healthcare professionals are well positioned to enhance patient health and safety by recognizing and recommitting to reducing antithrombotic undertreatment.

title: Beyond the Threshold: Continuous Creatinine Change and Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy for Acute Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) worsens outcomes in acute ischemic stroke, but threshold-based definitions do not capture prognostic information from subthreshold changes. We tested whether early creatinine change within 48 hours of EVT conveys graded prognostic information beyond dichotomous CA-AKI. METHODS: We performed a secondary analysis of the CAN-REST registry (Contrast-Associated Nephropathy After Endovascular Stroke Treatment), a retrospective multicenter observational cohort study of 6638 EVT-treated adults with acute ischemic stroke enrolled at 73 centers in 16 countries between January 1 and December 31, 2023. Early creatinine change was quantified as the natural logarithm ratio of 48-hour creatinine to baseline creatinine (ln[48-hour/baseline creatinine]), with CA-AKI defined per Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes criteria (≥0.3 mg/dL or ≥1.5× baseline rise within 48 hours). Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for prespecified baseline and periprocedural covariates examined associations with 90-day modified Rankin Scale shift and in-hospital mortality; linear versus restricted cubic spline specification was selected by likelihood ratio testing, and contrasts were estimated at ±10%, ±25%, and ±50%. RESULTS: Greater creatinine worsening within 48 hours of EVT was independently associated with an unfavorable 90-day modified Rankin Scale shift (adjusted common odds ratio per 1-unit log-ratio increase, 1.48 [95% CI, 1.07-2.04]; linear) and in-hospital mortality (nonlinear dose-response, of larger magnitude). A 10% increase in creatinine at 48 hours-well below Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes threshold-was associated with worse functional outcome (adjusted common odds ratio, 1.04 [95% CI, 1.01-1.07]) and death (adjusted odds ratio, 1.22 [95% CI, 1.13-1.32]); a 10% decrease in creatinine at 48 hours was associated with lower odds of both outcomes (adjusted common odds ratio, 0.96 [95% CI, 0.93-0.99]; adjusted odds ratio, 0.74 [95% CI, 0.65-0.86]). The functional-outcome association concentrated at upper modified Rankin Scale cut-points (severe disability, death); effect modification by baseline renal function was not significant. CONCLUSIONS: Early creatinine change after EVT conveys graded, outcome-specific prognostic information extending below formal CA-AKI thresholds, with a dose-response detectable at changes as modest as ±10%, complementing binary CA-AKI as a framework for post-EVT renal risk assessment. title: Artificial intelligence for the detection of large vessel occlusion stroke and workflow optimization: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: To evaluate the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) tools on workflow efficiency, treatment times, and clinical outcomes in patients with large vessel occlusion (LVO) stroke. METHODS: We included observational studies that assessed the implementation of AI-based tools in the management of patients with suspected or confirmed LVO stroke. Eligible studies reported workflow, treatment, safety, or functional outcomes. Data were extracted on thrombolysis rates, CTA-to-arterial puncture time, door-to-puncture time, endovascular treatment (EVT) access, reperfusion success, symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH), mortality, and functional independence (mRS 0-2) at 90 days. Random-effects models were applied to calculate pooled mean differences (MD) or risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: Thirteen studies were included. AI implementation significantly reduced workflow delays: CTA-to-puncture time decreased by -40.20 minutes (95% CI -66.41 to -13.99; P<0.01) and door-to-puncture time by -23.17 minutes (95% CI -38.71 to -7.63; P<0.01). Thrombolysis administration showed no difference (RR 0.79; 95% CI 0.57-1.09; P=0.15). Similarly, no significant effects were observed for EVT access (RR 0.97; 95% CI 0.66-1.44; P=0.89), reperfusion success (RR 1.06; 95% CI 1.00-1.12; P=0.06), sICH (RR 0.63; 95% CI 0.30-1.35; P=0.23), or mortality (RR 0.72; 95% CI 0.38-1.37; P=0.32). However, AI-based workflows significantly improved functional independence at 90 days (RR 1.55; 95% CI 1.12-2.15; P=0.008). CONCLUSIONS: AI tools significantly improve treatment times and functional independence in acute LVO stroke without increasing adverse events.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: To evaluate the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) tools on workflow efficiency, treatment times, and clinical outcomes in patients with large vessel occlusion (LVO) stroke. METHODS: We included observational studies that assessed the implementation of AI-based tools in the management of patients with suspected or confirmed LVO stroke. Eligible studies reported workflow, treatment, safety, or functional outcomes.
