title: AngioJet rheolytic thrombectomy under superior vena cava filter protection for acute upper extremity deep vein thrombosis in patients with cancer: a single-center, retrospective analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The incidence of upper extremity deep vein thrombosis (UEDVT) is increasing, and percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy (PMT) is receiving more attention as a treatment option. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and clinical outcomes of PMT combined with superior vena cava (SVC) filter protection in cancer patients with acute UEDVT. METHODS: This study included all patients with acute UEDVT who underwent treatment with an 8-Fr AngioJet thrombectomy system (Boston Scientific) under the protection of a retrievable SVC filter between January 1, 2020, and October 1, 2025. The evaluation indicators included technical success rate (defined as a thrombus clearance rate >80%), intraoperative adverse events, degree of limb swelling relief, incidence of pulmonary embolism, and thrombus recurrence during follow-up. RESULTS: A total of 19 patients (10 female; mean age 60.84 ± 11.30 years) were included. All patients had secondary UEDVT and a history of malignant tumors, with 14 cases (73.7%) having a history of central venous catheterization. All procedures achieved technical success, with no severe adverse events such as major bleeding occurring intraoperatively, nor were there any new symptomatic pulmonary embolisms. The average circumference of the affected limb 10 cm above the elbow before surgery was 29.83 ± 2.20 cm, which decreased to 26.98 ± 2.0 cm on the second postoperative day. During the 6-month follow-up, one patient with advanced lung cancer developed swelling of the upper limb on postoperative day 136, confirmed by ultrasound to be a recurrence of deep vein thrombosis; another patient was found to have an asymptomatic mural thrombus on ultrasound examination on postoperative day 28. CONCLUSION: PMT with the 8-Fr AngioJet system and SVC filter protection appears to be a safe and effective treatment option for cancer patients with acute UEDVT.

This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and clinical outcomes of PMT combined with superior vena cava (SVC) filter protection in cancer patients with acute UEDVT. METHODS: This study included all patients with acute UEDVT who underwent treatment with an 8-Fr AngioJet thrombectomy system (Boston Scientific) under the protection of a retrievable SVC filter between January 1, 2020, and October 1, 2025.

title: Perioperative Lactate, Survival, and Complications Following Lung Transplantation.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To examine perioperative lactate and its association with survival and postoperative complications following lung transplantation (LTx). DESIGN: Single-center retrospective cohort study. SETTING: Academic tertiary-care transplant center. PARTICIPANTS: Adult patients undergoing LTx between February 2018 and January 2023. INTERVENTIONS: None. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Serum lactate was measured at 6-hour intervals from the start of surgery, and the maximum value within the first 0 to 6 hours was recorded. Patients were categorized into the high-lactate group (upper quartile, ≥4.2 mmol/L) and low-lactate group (lower 3 quartiles). Primary outcomes were 1-year and overall survival. Secondary outcomes included renal failure, venous thromboembolism (VTE), primary graft dysfunction grade 3 (PGD3), mechanical ventilation duration, intensive care unit (ICU) and post-transplant length of stay, and in-hospital mortality. Among 225 recipients (median age, 62.3 years; 34.2% female), high lactate was not associated with 1-year or overall survival. However, recipients with high lactate had higher rates of PGD3 at 72 hours (42.1% v 13.1%, p < 0.001), longer mechanical ventilation duration (3 days v 2 days, p = 0.003), longer ICU stay (11.6 days v 7 days, p = 0.013), and higher in-hospital mortality rate (7% v 0.6%, p = 0.019). No significant differences were observed in renal failure, VTE, or post-transplant length of stay. CONCLUSIONS: Elevated perioperative serum lactate was associated with PGD3 at 72 hours, prolonged mechanical ventilation, longer ICU stay, and in-hospital mortality but not 1-year or overall survival following LTx. These findings suggest that perioperative lactate may aid in identifying high-risk patients early in their postoperative course despite its lack of association with long-term survival.

title: Hemodynamic Analysis of Modified Splenic Arteriovenous Shunt in Pancreas Transplantation.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of a modified splenic arteriovenous shunt technique in pancreas transplantation through intraoperative hemodynamic monitoring and postoperative follow-up. METHODS: A total of 12 patients undergoing simultaneous pancreas-kidney transplantation were enrolled. Under three consecutive intraoperative states (spleen preserved, splenic arteriovenous clamped, and splenic arteriovenous shunt created), color Doppler ultrasound was used to measure peak systolic velocity (PS) and volumetric flow (VF) of the splenic artery and vein at the same point in the distal pancreatic tail, while portal venous pressure was recorded using an intravascular pressure transducer. Postoperative graft function, thrombotic events, and complications were regularly followed up. RESULTS: Compared with the spleen-preserved state, the clamped state showed significant reductions in splenic arterial PS and VF (15.24 ± 4.43 cm/s, 16.62 ± 6.84 mL/min) and splenic venous PS and VF (16.31 ± 3.82 cm/s, 60.32 ± 16.07 mL/min) (P < 0.001). In the shunt state, splenic arterial (54.47 ± 3.45 cm/s, 157.39 ± 11.24 mL/min) and venous (49.27 ± 6.61 cm/s, 177.89 ± 14.15 mL/min) flow parameters showed no significant differences compared with the spleen-preserved state (P > 0.05), but were significantly higher than those in the clamped state (P < 0.001). Portal venous pressure showed no significant differences among the three states (P > 0.05). At a median follow-up of 5 months, no graft thrombosis, pancreatitis, or gastrointestinal bleeding was observed, and patient and graft survival rates were both 100% at the last follow-up. Glycated hemoglobin decreased from 7.37% ± 0.68% preoperatively to 5.81% ± 0.32% (P < 0.005), and left ventricular ejection fraction increased from 59.50% ± 3.23% to 67.33% ± 2.84% (P < 0.005). CONCLUSION: The modified splenic arteriovenous shunt maintains physiological perfusion of the pancreatic allograft without elevating portal venous pressure, and may mitigate the hypoperfusion and blood stasis associated with conventional splenic vessel ligation. Based on the short-term results of this study, this modified technique appears safe and feasible, and may contribute to reducing early thrombotic complications after pancreas transplantation.

title: Vascular Management Strategies and Outcomes of Infectious Arterial Complications Involving the Kidney Transplant Vasculature: A Systematic Review and Evidence-Informed Treatment Framework.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Infectious arterial complications involving the kidney transplant (KT) vasculature are rare but life-threatening and frequently result in KT loss. The lack of evidence-based guidance for vascular management strategies underscores the need for systematic synthesis to inform clinical decision-making. METHODS: A systematic search was performed from database inception through August 22, 2025, for reports of culture-proven infectious vascular complications-including arterial rupture, detachment, pseudoaneurysm, aneurysm, thrombosis, or stenosis-involving the transplant renal artery, iliac vessels, or arterial anastomosis in KT recipients. Eligible studies reported vascular management strategies. Due to methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively using proportion-based comparisons. RESULTS: Eighty reports (1972-2025) comprising 139 cases were included. Candida species were most frequent, followed by Pseudomonas, Aspergillus, and Staphylococcus species. Pseudoaneurysm and arterial rupture were the predominant clinical presentation, typically occuring within the first month after transplantation. Outcome patterns differed by transplant nephrectomy status, with vascular management strategies performed without transplant nephrectomy demonstrating higher reported proportions of uneventful follow-up. Autologous interposition grafting demonstrated the most favorable outcome pattern (86.7% uneventful recovery; 6.7% reintervention and mortality), even when transplant nephrectomy is unavoidable. Covered stent placement was the most frequently reported intervention andshowed favorable outcomes in selected KT-preserving cases (75% uneventful recovery). Primary surgical repair had the highest reintervention proportion (59.1%), whereas arterial ligation had the highest mortality (43.8%) and accounted for all reported limb loss. CONCLUSION: Across five decades of case-based evidence, autologous interposition grafting demonstrated the most favorable outcome pattern and may represent the preferred vascular management strategy when durable arterial reconstruction is feasible, including when transplant nephrectomy is required. Covered stent placement may provide a useful option in selected cases or as a temporizing strategy for hemorrhage control. These findings should guide rather than define management decisions given the heterogeneous evidence base. HIGHLIGHTS: First systematic synthesis of management strategies for infectious arterial complications involving the kidney transplant vasculature Candida was the most frequently reported pathogen; pseudoaneurysm and arterial rupture were the predominant presentations Vascular management strategies performed without transplant nephrectomy demonstrated higher reported proportions of uneventful follow-up Autologous interposition grafting showed the most favorable reported outcome pattern, even when transplant nephrectomy is unavoidable Ligation and primary repair were associated with higher reported mortality and reintervention, respectively.

The lack of evidence-based guidance for vascular management strategies underscores the need for systematic synthesis to inform clinical decision-making. METHODS: A systematic search was performed from database inception through August 22, 2025, for reports of culture-proven infectious vascular complications-including arterial rupture, detachment, pseudoaneurysm, aneurysm, thrombosis, or stenosis-involving the transplant renal artery, iliac vessels, or arterial anastomosis in KT recipients.

title: Intended Thrombectomy for Basilar Artery Occlusion with Mild Deficits: Evidence from a Multicenter Prospective Registry.
abstract: P Supplemental material is available for this article. Background The role of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) in basilar artery occlusion (BAO) with mild deficits (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] score < 10) remains uncertain. Purpose To compare the outcomes of EVT combined with best medical management (BMM) versus BMM alone in individuals with BAO and mild deficits. Materials and Methods Consecutive eligible patients treated at eight stroke centers between September 2023 and March 2025 were enrolled in a prospective registry. The primary outcome was 90-day functional independence (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] score of 0-2). Secondary outcomes were 90-day excellent outcome (mRS score of 0-1), death, and early neurologic deterioration (END), defined as a four-point or greater increase in NIHSS score within 72 hours. Primary analyses followed an intention-to-treat-like framework with inverse probability weighting (IPW). As-treated and per-protocol sensitivity analyses were used to assess the robustness of the results and the impact of treatment crossover (EVT after END). Results Among 401 participants (mean age, 64.9 years ± 8.9 [SD]; 278 male participants), the median onset-to-arterial-puncture time in the EVT group was 402 minutes (IQR, 271-583 minutes). After multivariable adjustment in the IPW-adjusted data, EVT was associated with higher odds of functional independence (odds ratio [OR], 1.55 [95% CI: 1.17, 2.06]) and excellent outcome (OR, 1.48 [95% CI: 1.09, 2.03]) and lower odds of death (OR, 0.65 [95% CI: 0.45, 0.77]) and END (OR, 0.35 [95% CI: 0.20, 0.61]). Subgroup analyses demonstrated EVT-related functional benefit in participants with NIHSS scores of 6-9 but not in those with NIHSS scores of 0-5 (for interaction = .02 for functional independence); however, in participants with NIHSS scores of 0-5, EVT was associated with lower odds of END and death. Sensitivity analyses accounting for treatment crossover showed attenuated functional advantage for EVT. Conclusion In participants with BAO and mild deficits, EVT plus BMM was associated with better outcomes than BMM alone; however, functional benefit was observed in those with NIHSS scores of 6-9 but not those with NIHSS scores of 0-5. title: Stroke and Bleeding Risk in Long-Term Care Residents With Atrial Fibrillation Who Discontinue Anticoagulation.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Atrial fibrillation (AF) leads to more than 100 000 cases of stroke yearly and is particularly prevalent in long-term care (LTC) residents. Anticoagulation (AC) is the mainstay of stroke prevention, but given its risks, clinicians and residents may consider discontinuation at the time of LTC entry. OBJECTIVE: To estimate the association between AC discontinuation and stroke and bleeding risk among LTC residents with AF. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This comparative effectiveness research study with target trial emulation used claims data (2020-2021) from LTC facilities in the US serving Medicare beneficiaries. Medicare beneficiaries with AF receiving AC who entered LTC between April 1 and December 31, 2020, were included; those with additional indications for AC, including prosthetic heart valve or venous thromboembolism, were excluded. Analysis was performed in August 2026. EXPOSURE: Discontinuer vs continuer assignment. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The main outcomes were stroke (including ischemic stroke, transient ischemic attack, and systemic embolism) and bleeding, assessed using Medicare claims. A target trial emulation was conducted with clone censor weighting (CCW) analysis. Specifically, eligible LTC residents were assigned (cloned) to each of 2 strategies: AC discontinuation or AC continuation. Clones were then censored when they deviated from their assigned strategy, and inverse probability of censoring weighting was applied to address informative censoring: residents who deviated differing systematically from those who did not. Subdistribution hazard ratios (sHRs) for stroke and bleeding were then calculated to account for competing mortality and a cause-specific hazard ratio (HR) for death. RESULTS: This study included 15 426 LTC residents (mean [SD] age, 82.6 [7.6] years). Most were female (62.6%). AC discontinuers had 187 strokes, 297 bleeding events, and 3684 deaths over a mean (SD) of 128.9 (177.9) days. AC continuers had 321 strokes, 493 bleeding events, and 5475 deaths over a mean (SD) of 279.6 (204.9) days. Discontinuers had similar stroke risk (sHR, 1.07; 95% CI, 0.93-1.23) and bleeding risk (sHR, 1.02; 95% CI, 0.92-1.13) compared with continuers, but discontinuers had higher mortality risk (HR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.23-1.31). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this target trial emulation with CCW in a cohort of LTC residents with AF, AC discontinuation was not associated with higher stroke or bleeding risk. Very high mortality, unmeasured confounding, and reliance on claims-based outcome ascertainment may have limited the ability to better understand the consequences of AC discontinuation on stroke and bleeding.

title: A single-cell census of pulmonary endarterectomies tissue across different anatomical regions in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) remains one of potentially curative options for chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH). The operation can remove proximal thromboembolic materials and their secondary branches. However, the cellular landscape and pathological features across different anatomical regions remain limited understood. METHODS: Ten patients with CTEPH undergoing PEA surgery and six reference distal pulmonary arteries were conducted single-cell transcriptomics to profile the cellular composition of the main and its bifurcate portion. RESULTS: Pronounced muscularised and fibrotic thrombi organisation were presented in the main portion, and the proportion of mononuclear phagocytes was significantly increased. Inflammatory response and pro-inflammatory activity were attributed to CD8+ effector T cells and nature killer cells subsets and a M1-like (high IL1B and TNF, minimal IL6) phenotypic macrophage subcluster. The colander-like lesions were dominant in the bifurcate portion, and the percentage of plasma cells was markedly increased. Immune dysregulation was induced from CD4 naïve T cells, and a downregulation of M2-like macrophage infiltration into the vascular wall. The expression of plasminogen activator, urokinase receptor, urokinase receptor (PLAUR; plasminogen activator) were observed in M2-like (high MRC1 and CD163, virtually no IL1B or TNF) macrophage in bifurcate portion. Notably, one of smooth muscle cells (SMCs) subclusters in the bifurcate portion gained more significantly myofibroblast markers than those in the main portion, and other subclusters remained the function of SMCs. CONCLUSIONS: The regions with colander-like lesions changes had more obviously T cell and macrophages driving immune-inflammatory response and SMCs differentiation, suggesting that combining therapeutic interventions after surgical removal of accessible thrombus may be beneficial. KEY POINTS: This study reveals the comprehensive cellular composition in main/lobar and bifurcate pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) specimens at the single-cell level. The bifurcate regions with colander had more obviously T cell and macrophages driving immune-inflammatory response and smooth muscle cells (SMCs) differentiation, however, the remodelling of distal or micro-vessels still remained.

title: Evaluating the Impact of Therapeutic Anticoagulation Management in Head and Neck Free Tissue Transfer: A Retrospective Study of 126 Cases.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Existing literature on anticoagulation in head and neck free flap reconstruction largely focuses on postoperative thromboprophylaxis. Less is known about preoperative therapeutic anticoagulation, including how perioperative anticoagulation holds, timing of resumption, and anticoagulant class relate to hemorrhagic, thromboembolic, and flap-related complications. This study evaluates these outcomes in anticoagulated patients undergoing head and neck free flap reconstruction and compares complication rates with matched non-anticoagulated controls. METHODS: A retrospective chart review was performed on patients who underwent free flap reconstruction between 2009 and 2023 and had been on therapeutic anticoagulation for over 1 month preoperatively. A matched control group of non-anticoagulated patients was included for comparison. RESULTS: 126 anticoagulated patients (mean age 71.8 years, 75.4% male) were included. The most common indications for anticoagulation were atrial fibrillation (62.7%) and venous thromboembolism (30.2%). Anticoagulation medications included warfarin (49.2%), apixaban (36.5%), rivaroxaban (12.7%), and dabigatran (1.6%). Anticoagulation was stopped an average of 4.4 days preoperatively and resumed 7.8 days postoperatively. Hemorrhagic complications occurred in 14 patients (11.1%), including hematomas and unrelated bleeding. Thromboembolic complications occurred in 9 patients (7.1%), 6 of which resulted in flap failure. On matched cohort analysis, controls had lower odds of any complication (OR 0.41, 95% CI 0.21-0.81, p = 0.010), hemorrhagic or thromboembolic complications (OR 0.27, 95% CI 0.11-0.63, p = 0.003), and hemorrhagic complications specifically (OR 0.26, 95% CI 0.09-0.81, p = 0.020), while thromboembolic complication odds were not significantly different between groups (OR 0.47, 95% CI 0.15-1.44, p = 0.19). CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights the challenges of managing therapeutic anticoagulation in head and neck free flap surgery, where thromboembolic risk during interruption and hemorrhagic complications upon resumption point to the need for clearer guidelines. Evidence-based protocols are needed to replace discretionary practices and improve outcomes.

This study evaluates these outcomes in anticoagulated patients undergoing head and neck free flap reconstruction and compares complication rates with matched non-anticoagulated controls.

title: Association between admission D-dimer levels and post-stroke epilepsy risk: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Post-stroke epilepsy (PSE) is a severe complication following acute ischemic stroke (AIS), yet early identification of patients at high risk remains challenging. This study evaluated the association between baseline D-dimer levels and incident PSE within one year after AIS. METHODS: 2 In this secondary analysis of a multicenter retrospective cohort, 21,459 patients with first-ever AIS were included. D-dimer was modeled as a log-transformed continuous variable. Multivariable logistic regression with progressive adjustment, restricted cubic spline analysis, and sensitivity analyses were performed. Internal validation was conducted using bootstrap resampling. RESULTS: The median baseline D-dimer level was 0.92 mg/L (IQR 0.65-1.49). PSE occurred in 936 patients (4.36%). After full adjustment, each doubling of D-dimer was associated with a 3.3-fold increase in PSE odds (OR 3.33, 95% CI 2.94-3.78). The association remained consistent in sensitivity analyses excluding patients with deep vein thrombosis (OR 3.86, 95% CI 3.37-4.43), atrial fibrillation (OR 3.50, 95% CI 3.04-4.04), or extreme D-dimer values (OR 3.41, 95% CI 2.99-3.91). A non-linear relationship was observed, with PSE risk rising more steeply at higher D-dimer levels. The C-statistic for the fully adjusted model was 0.968. CONCLUSION: Elevated baseline D-dimer levels were independently associated with an increased risk of PSE within one year after AIS. As a routinely available biomarker, D-dimer may inform risk assessment in acute stroke units; however, external validation in independent cohorts with prospective PSE ascertainment is required before clinical implementation.

title: Short-Term Outcomes of Lower-Extremity Surgical Revascularization for Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia Among Yemeni Patients: A Prospective Observational Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) carries a high risk of amputation and mortality. We evaluated short-term clinical, hemodynamic, and quality-of-life outcomes after open lower-extremity surgical revascularization in a Yemeni cohort. METHODS: This single-center prospective observational cohort study was conducted at Al-Thawra Modern General Hospital, Sana'a, Yemen. We enrolled 39 consecutive adults with CLTI (Rutherford categories 4-6) who were selected for and considered fit to undergo open lower-extremity surgical revascularization between December 2022 and September 2024; follow-up was completed in December 2024. The study protocol was reviewed and approved by the Al-Thawra Hospital Ethics Committee (approval no. 33-2026), and written informed consent was obtained from all participants. The study was not registered. This was an exploratory consecutive cohort; no formal sample-size calculation was performed, and no contemporaneous endovascular, nonoperative, or primary-amputation comparator group was included. Primary endpoints were graft patency and limb salvage at three months. Secondary outcomes were secondary patency, postoperative complications, and changes in ankle-brachial index (ABI) and Vascular Quality of Life Questionnaire-6 (VascuQoL-6) scores. Paired comparisons used Wilcoxon signed-rank tests; Fisher's exact tests were used for categorical comparisons. RESULTS: The mean age was 60.9 years (SD 9.7), and 30 patients (76.9%) were male. Diabetes mellitus and hypertension were present in 34 (87.2%) and 30 (76.9%) patients, respectively. Nineteen patients (48.7%) had ischemic rest pain, and 20 (51.3%) had tissue loss. Great saphenous vein (GSV) and polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) grafts were used in 28 (71.8%) and 11 (28.2%) patients, respectively. At three months, primary patency was 84.6% (33/39 grafts; 95% CI 70.3%-92.8%), secondary patency was 89.7% (35/39 grafts; 95% CI 76.4%-95.9%), and limb salvage was 89.7% (35/39 patients; 95% CI 76.4%-95.9%). Given the small cohort, the confidence intervals around these estimates were relatively wide. Among the 35 patients with limb preservation, mean ABI increased from 0.35 (SD 0.11) to 0.55 (SD 0.12; mean difference 0.21, 95% CI 0.19-0.23; p<0.001), and mean VascuQoL-6 score increased from 10.3 (SD 2.9) to 16.6 (SD 4.0; mean difference 6.3, 95% CI 5.6-7.1; p<0.001). Complications occurred in nine patients (23.1%). In an exploratory unadjusted subgroup analysis, GSV use was associated with higher primary patency than PTFE use (92.9% vs 63.6%, p=0.042). CONCLUSION: In this single-center prospective cohort, open surgical revascularization was feasible and was associated with 89.7% limb salvage and 84.6% primary patency at three months. Improvements in ABI and VascuQoL-6 were observed among patients with limb preservation. Autologous GSV use was associated with higher primary patency; this finding requires confirmation in larger, adjusted studies.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) carries a high risk of amputation and mortality. We evaluated short-term clinical, hemodynamic, and quality-of-life outcomes after open lower-extremity surgical revascularization in a Yemeni cohort. METHODS: This single-center prospective observational cohort study was conducted at Al-Thawra Modern General Hospital, Sana'a, Yemen.

title: Transcatheter Electrosurgical Aortic Septotomy Across the Spectrum of Type B Aortic Dissection: Feasibility, Technical Lessons, and Bailout Strategies.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Transcatheter electrosurgical aortic septotomy (TEAS) has been introduced to optimise luminal geometry during endovascular repair of complex type B aortic dissection (TBAD), but data across dissection phases and on complication management remain limited. This study reports early outcomes, quantitative common lumen creation, and bailout strategies from a consecutive single centre experience. METHOD: Eight consecutive patients underwent TEAS, between December 2024 and January 2026, as an adjunct to thoracic endovascular aortic repair or physician modified fenestrated endograft for acute, subacute, or chronic TBAD, including post-type A repair and genetic aortopathy. Pre-procedural and follow up computed tomography angiography (CTA) quantified true lumen and common lumen cross sectional area. Septotomy technical success, peri-operative outcomes, complications, and early follow up were assessed. RESULTS: 2 2 The mean age was 51.1 ± 17 years; five were men. Two patients were acute, two subacute, and four chronic; two had Marfan syndrome, both redo cases after previous open repair. Septotomy technical success was 100%. The median cross sectional area increased from 174.5 mm(pre-procedural true lumen) to 1 007 mm(follow up CTA common lumen) after TEAS (5.3 fold increase). There were no 30 day, in hospital, or aortic related deaths. Three major procedure related complications (38%) occurred, all in non-acute cases and all managed endovascularly: one iliac lamellar dislodgement requiring kissing stents, one external iliac rupture treated with stent grafting, and one delayed superior mesenteric artery occlusion managed with stenting. All acute cases were uneventful. Median clinical follow up was 32 days (range 22 - 308) and median imaging follow up was 20 days (range 2 - 265), with no late deaths, no aortic re-interventions, and no aneurysmal dilatation of the non-stented TEAS treated segment. CONCLUSION: TEAS may be considered across acute, subacute, and chronic TBAD, including redo and connective tissue disease cases, enabling reproducible common lumen creation and landing zone optimisation. All complications were recognised and managed endovascularly and were observed only in non-acute dissections, although the sample size precluded meaningful assessment of any relationship between dissection phase and technical risk. These findings support TEAS as a feasible adjunct in carefully selected complex dissections, offer practical principles for safe adoption, and reflect an early experience that may be influenced by the learning curve of this technically demanding procedure.

METHOD: Eight consecutive patients underwent TEAS, between December 2024 and January 2026, as an adjunct to thoracic endovascular aortic repair or physician modified fenestrated endograft for acute, subacute, or chronic TBAD, including post-type A repair and genetic aortopathy.

title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Single-Cell Analyses Identify CCR2-Dependent Monocyte-Smooth Muscle Cell Crosstalk in Aortic Aneurysm.
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Aortic aneurysm (AA) involves inflammatory recruitment and vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) remodeling, but the cellular contribution of candidate chemokine receptors remains unclear. We prioritized reproducible AA-associated genes, localized their cellular sources, and tested whether monocyte CCR2 influences human aortic smooth muscle cells (HASMCs). METHODS: Differentially expressed genes shared by GSE57691 and GSE7084 underwent enrichment, protein-protein interaction, regulatory-network, and drug-gene analyses. Hub genes were assessed in GSE9106 and localized in GSE166676 single-cell RNA-sequencing data. CCR2-silenced THP-1 monocytic cells were indirectly co-cultured with HASMCs. CCR2 knockdown was verified by quantitative PCR; HASMC remodeling-related proteins and 24-h scratch-wound closure were evaluated. RESULTS: p p p We identified 107 common upregulated genes and ten immune-related hubs. CCR2 was monocyte-enriched and higher in AA cells overall (= 0.00799) and AA monocytes (= 0.00440). THP-1 co-culture increased COL3A1 and SPP1, decreased α-SMA and TPM, and increased HASMC wound closure. CCR2 silencing partially reversed these changes and decreased wound closure versus siNC-THP-1 cells (< 0.01). CONCLUSIONS: Multi-omic evidence and non-contact co-culture support CCR2-dependent monocyte-HASMC paracrine crosstalk in AA-associated remodeling. The responsible mediators and in vivo relevance require further study.

title: Cardiovascular and mortality outcomes with JAK versus TNF inhibitors in rheumatoid arthritis: a target trial emulation (CARDINAL-RA).
abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aims to compare cardiovascular and mortality outcomes of Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi) versus tumor necrosis factor inhibitors (TNFi) in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) at elevated cardiovascular risk using target trial emulation. METHODS: Within TriNetX, adults with RA aged ≥50 years and ≥1 cardiovascular risk factor initiating JAKi or TNFi were compared in a new-user, active-comparator design. Improved 1:1 propensity score matching incorporated demographics, cardiovascular risk factors, comorbidities, individual conventional synthetic DMARDs, oral corticosteroids, prior non-TNF biologic exposure, and baseline inflammatory markers. The primary outcome was MACE (nonfatal myocardial infarction or nonfatal ischemic stroke); the secondary outcomes were all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, and venous thromboembolism (VTE), with cataract as a prespecified negative control. Follow-up began 90 days after initiation. Cox models estimated hazard ratios, with 5-year Kaplan-Meier cumulative incidences and absolute risk differences per 1,000. Cohorts were separately matched by agent, sex, cardiovascular-risk stratum, and index era; E-values quantified sensitivity to unmeasured confounding. RESULTS: p In 18,757 matched pairs, JAKi was not associated with excess MACE (HR 1.002, 0.923-1.088; +2.11 per 1,000). All-cause mortality, a secondary outcome, was higher with JAKi (HR 1.158, 1.058-1.268; = 0.0014; +10.4 per 1,000; E-value 1.586), whereas heart failure hospitalization (HR 1.019, 0.955-1.088) and VTE (HR 1.054, 0.961-1.156) did not differ; the negative control showed no excess (HR 0.934, 0.867-1.007). No agent showed a significant excess in MACE or mortality (mortality HR 1.052 tofacitinib, 1.213 baricitinib, and 1.090 upadacitinib); the only nominally significant agent-level finding was VTE with baricitinib (HR 1.364, 1.028-1.809; 198 events). A three-component composite including death was non-significant (HR 1.058, 0.992-1.127). No consistent effect modification was seen by sex, cardiovascular risk burden, or index year. CONCLUSION: JAKi initiation was not associated with excess MACE (primary outcome), heart failure hospitalization, or VTE. A modest excess in all-cause mortality was observed as a secondary outcome, with no signal for any individual agent. This association was of modest robustness (E-value 1.586) and was not reproduced in any agent-specific cohort, so residual channeling bias cannot be excluded. The null MACE result should not be read as class-wide cardiovascular safety reassurance nor the mortality signal as an established causal effect.

title: Drug-Eluting Resorbable Scaffolds for Infrapopliteal Peripheral Artery Disease: A State-of-the-Art Review.
abstract: Drug-eluting resorbable scaffolds (DRS) have been developed to overcome the key limitations of conventional endovascular therapies for below-the-knee (BTK) peripheral artery disease (PAD), including acute recoil, restenosis, and the sequela of long-term permanent metallic implants. DRS provides a temporary mechanical support and localized antiproliferative drug delivery after which the scaffold is gradually resorbed, ultimately restoring native vessel architecture to preserve future revascularization options. Over the past decade, numerous prospective and observational studies have evaluated both polymer- and magnesium alloy-based DRS platforms and have demonstrated favorable patency, wound healing, and limb salvage outcomes in patients with advanced infrapopliteal PAD. Most recently, randomized evidence from the LIFE-BTK trial has demonstrated superior patency and reduced rates of revascularization with DRS-treated lesions as compared with plain balloon angioplasty. In this state-of-the-art review, we summarize the existing evidence evaluating DRS devices for BTK PAD and present an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical outcomes for DRS-based endovascular interventions.
englishSummary: Drug-eluting resorbable scaffolds (DRS) have been developed to overcome the key limitations of conventional endovascular therapies for below-the-knee (BTK) peripheral artery disease (PAD), including acute recoil, restenosis, and the sequela of long-term permanent metallic implants. DRS provides a temporary mechanical support and localized antiproliferative drug delivery after which the scaffold is gradually resorbed, ultimately restoring native vessel architecture to preserve future revascularization options. Over the past decade, numerous prospective and observational studies have evaluated both polymer- and magnesium alloy-based DRS platforms and have demonstrated favorable patency, wound healing, and limb salvage outcomes in patients with advanced infrapopliteal PAD.

title: Venous thromboembolism in patients with distant-stage uterine cancer: a comparison of primary cytoreductive surgery versus neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare the incidence and temporal distribution of venous thromboembolism in patients with distant-stage uterine cancer treated with primary cytoreductive surgery followed by adjuvant chemotherapy versus neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by interval cytoreductive surgery. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Program-Medicare data to identify women aged ≥65 years with Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Program Summary Stage distant uterine cancer diagnosed from 2008 to 2017 who underwent both hysterectomy and chemotherapy within 6 months of diagnosis. Treatment was classified by the sequence of surgery and chemotherapy within 6 months of diagnosis. Venous thromboembolism, comprising pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis, was identified from claims. Patients with baseline venous thromboembolism (6 months before through the month of diagnosis) were excluded from the primary analysis. Cumulative venous thromboembolism incidence was estimated using competing risk methods (death as a competing event) and compared via Gray's test. Multi-variable analysis evaluated factors associated with venous thromboembolism during the first 6 months after diagnosis, adjusting for demographic, clinical, and tumor characteristics. Landmark, time-varying treatment-phase, and first-treatment-anchored sensitivity analyses were performed to address immortal time and time-zero misalignment. RESULTS: Of 1977 patients, 186 (9.4%) had venous thromboembolism prior to diagnosis and were excluded, leaving 1791 patients for analysis: 74.7% underwent primary cytoreductive surgery and 25.3% received neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy use increased from 17.6% (2008) to 35.5% (2017). Neoadjuvant chemotherapy patients had higher baseline venous thromboembolism prevalence (14.7% vs 7.5%, p<.001) and comorbidity burden. Overall, 568 venous thromboembolism events occurred; cumulative venous thromboembolism incidence was 20.1% at 6 months, 33.6% at 24 months, and 49.3% at 60 months. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy patients had higher early cumulative venous thromboembolism incidence (23.0% vs 19.1% at 6 months; 40.8% vs 31.5% at 24 months), with convergence by 60 months (46.5% vs 49.2%; Gray's test p=.054). In multi-variable analysis, the adjusted risk ratio for early venous thromboembolism with neoadjuvant chemotherapy versus primary cytoreductive surgery was 1.21 (95% confidence interval 0.97-1.51), an imprecise estimate that does not exclude a clinically meaningful increase in early risk. CONCLUSIONS: Among older patients with distant-stage uterine cancer, venous thromboembolism was common, affecting approximately 1 in 5 patients within 6 months and nearly 1 in 2 within 5 years. The cumulative venous thromboembolism incidence did not differ significantly between primary cytoreductive surgery and neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Events occurred earlier in the neoadjuvant chemotherapy group, a pattern that may reflect baseline differences between the groups and differential ascertainment as much as treatment sequence. Our findings support the need for a prospective evaluation of treatment-phase-specific thromboprophylaxis.

title: Genetic Patterns in Familial Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm Disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: We examined familial patterns and phenotypes of thoracic aortic aneurysms and dissections (TAAD) in the 3746 patients currently populating our Yale Aortic Institute Database. METHODS: Patient charts and electronic medical records were retrospectively reviewed for the entire cohort. TAAD disease was categorized as syndromic (with extra-aortic manifestations) or non-syndromic (without) for each patient. Family patterns and whole exome sequencing results were assessed. Family history was considered 'proven' when a patient's relative(s) had an arterial aneurysm or dissection confirmed by an imaging study, surgical treatment, or postmortem examination. Family history was termed 'likely' when at least one relative suffered sudden death at ages ≤50 for males and ≤60 for females, and 'possible' with a history of sudden death at any age. RESULTS: p p p p Of the 3746 patients in the database, family history of aneurysm or dissection and connective tissue status was able to be determined for 3113 patients, divided into 109 (3.5%) syndromic and 3004 (96.5%) non-syndromic TAAD patients. Findings were as follows: (1) In the syndromic group, 46 (42.2%) patients had a 'proven' family history, 6 (5.5%) had a 'likely' family history, 4 (3.7%) had a 'possible' family history, and 18 (16.5%) had 'none'. For 35 patients (32.1%) their family history was unknown. (2) In the non-syndromic group, 587 (19.5%) patients had 'proven' family history, 147 (4.9%) had 'likely' family history, 210 (7.0%) had 'possible' family history and 1444 (48.1%) had no family history, thus representing sporadic TAAD. A total of 616 (20.5%) had an unknown family history. (3) There was a significant difference between the rate for 'proven' and 'none' family history between the syndromic and non-syndromic groups (42.2% vs. 19.5% and 16.5% vs. 48.1%, respectively;< 0.001). (4) Syndromic patients presented at a significantly younger age than non-syndromic or sporadic patients (41.2 vs. 63.3 or 63.6;< 0.001). (5) There was no significant difference in age of presentation between familial non-syndromic (patients with 'proven', 'likely', and 'possible' family history) and sporadic patients (63.3 vs. 63.6;= 0.64). (6) Overall, of the 3746 patients in the database, 631 patients (25 syndromic, 552 non-syndromic, and 54 with unknown status) underwent Whole Exome Sequencing (WES). Sequencing revealed 170 disease-causing or suspicious variants [13 pathogenic, 16 likely pathogenic, 7 not classified, and 134 Variants of Uncertain Significance (VUS)] found in the exomes of 141 (22.3%) patients (12 syndromic, 103 non-syndromic TAAD patients plus a remaining 26 of unknown connective tissue status). Seventy (49.6%) of these patients had a 'proven' family history. (7) Familial TAAD patients were more likely to find a variant in their WES result than patients without a family history (70 vs. 26;< 0.001). Recognition of these strong familial patterns, even in non-syndromic cases, encourages intensive investigation of family in order to save lives by detecting silent TAA disease. CONCLUSIONS: Our large-scale, clinical and sequencing-based study clearly demonstrates the strongly familial and genetically mediated nature of thoracic aortic disease. We vividly demonstrate and characterize this familial nature of TAAD, both clinically and by genetic sequencing. Our findings strongly support vigorous family investigation when a new patient is diagnosed with thoracic aortic aneurysm, as well as vigorous application of whole exome sequencing for these families.

title: Anatomical Predictors of Endovascular Technical Success in Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia: The Role of GLASS and Diabetes.
abstract: Background: Methods: Results: Conclusions: n n p p p p p p Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) is associated with high rates of major adverse limb events and mortality, particularly in patients with diabetes mellitus (DM). The Global Limb Anatomic Staging System (GLASS) standardizes anatomical assessment and supports revascularization planning. This study evaluated the association of anatomical complexity and diabetes with immediate technical success after infrainguinal endovascular treatment.This single-center retrospective study included 136 patients undergoing infrainguinal endovascular procedures for CLTI between May 2021 and May 2023, stratified into diabetic (= 85) and non-diabetic (= 51) groups. Anatomical complexity was assessed using GLASS. Technical success was defined as restoration of inline flow to the foot. Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed.Technical success was achieved in 74.3% of procedures, without significant differences between diabetic and non-diabetic patients (75.3% vs. 72.5%,= 0.723). Success declined progressively from 86.3% in GLASS stage I to 75.5% in stage II and 53.1% in stage III (= 0.003; trend= 0.001). In multivariable analysis, GLASS FP (femoropopliteal) grade ≥2 (adjusted OR 8.068, 95% CI 3.018-21.562;< 0.001) and tibioperoneal trunk occlusion (adjusted OR 4.874, 95% CI 1.271-18.687;= 0.021) were independently associated with technical failure, whereas diabetes was not. The model showed good discrimination (AUC 0.820, 95% CI 0.744-0.897;< 0.001).Anatomical complexity was associated with immediate technical success in CLTI, whereas no independent association with diabetes was detected in this cohort. GLASS may provide clinically relevant preprocedural risk stratification and support endovascular planning.

title: One-year outcomes of percutaneous deep vein arterialization in the Dutch LimFlow registry.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Percutaneous deep vein arterialization (pDVA) offers a potential endovascular alternative for reducing the risk of major amputation in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) who have no standard revascularization options "no-option" CLTI (NO-CLTI). METHODS: In this prospective, multicenter registry conducted in the Netherlands between May 2020 and June 2024, patients with NO-CLTI underwent pDVA using the LimFlow system (Inari Medical). The primary end point was amputation-free survival at 12 months. Secondary outcomes included limb salvage, overall survival, patency, pain scores, wound healing, transcutaneous oxygen pressure, and quality of life (QoL). RESULTS: A total of 26 limbs of 23 patients with NO-CLTI (mean age, 64 ± 12 years; 20 men) were included, all classified as Rutherford category 5 and 17 (77.3%) as Wound Ischemia and foot Infection stage 4. Thirteen (53.8%) patients suffered from diabetes mellitus and six (21.7%) from renal insufficiency. Technical success was 100%. Amputation-free survival was 69.2%, limb salvage 80.8%, and overall survival 88.5% at 12 months. Primary patency, primary-assisted patency, and secondary patency rates at 12 months were 6.6%, 27.3%, and 35.7%, respectively. Reinterventions were performed to maintain patency in 85% of the limbs and 58% for maturation of the pDVA. Median time to wound healing was 6.9 months, with 73.4% healed at 12 months. Pain scores decreased significantly (P <.001) in 12 months. QoL improved from a mean of 37% to 68% on the VascuQoL-25, though these analyses were based on limited available data. CONCLUSIONS: pDVA in patients with NO-CLTI is safe and effective at 12 months, preventing major amputation and mortality in the majority of patients. QoL also appeared to improve following pDVA. These observations warrant confirmation in larger studies. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This study strengthens existing evidence on the effectivity and safety of percutaneous deep vein arterialization using the LimFlow system (Inari Medical) in patients with "no-option" chronic limb-threatening ischemia. Our data demonstrated a 100% technical success rate and comparable amputation-free survival and limb salvage to other percutaneous deep vein arterialization studies. Notably, this prospective and well-phenotyped cohort uniquely incorporated patient-reported outcome measures, showing improvements in pain, transcutaneous oxygen pressure and quality of life.

METHODS: In this prospective, multicenter registry conducted in the Netherlands between May 2020 and June 2024, patients with NO-CLTI underwent pDVA using the LimFlow system (Inari Medical). The primary end point was amputation-free survival at 12 months.

title: Analysis of real-world multicenter experience with the large-bore CLEANER-Vac Thrombectomy System: An analysis of 200 patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE), encompassing deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, represents a significant clinical entity associated with elevated morbidity and mortality rates. Conventional therapeutic approaches, such as systemic anticoagulation and thrombolytic agents, frequently yield suboptimal thrombus resolution. Mechanical thrombectomy has introduced a paradigm shift, enabling expeditious thrombus extraction while mitigating the chronic outcomes of suboptimally treated VTE and sequelae inherent to fibrinolytic therapies. The CLEANER Vac Thrombectomy System (Argon Medical Devices) is designed for controlled percutaneous venous thrombectomy. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the real-world procedural efficacy, safety profile, and clinical utility of the CLEANER Vac system in a multicenter cohort comprising 200 patients presenting with symptomatic venous thrombus. METHODS: This retrospective, multicenter investigation included data from 200 patients who underwent intervention between October 2024 and January 2026 across 26 U.S. institutions. Eligible participants were adults aged ≥18 years with imaging-confirmed acute (<14 days) or subacute (14-28 days) VTE. Primary end points included thrombus clearance efficacy, segmented venous involvement, estimated blood loss, and intraprocedural adverse event incidence. RESULTS: The study cohort had a mean age of 64.5 (range, 25-90) years, with a gender distribution of 52% female (n = 104) and 48% male (n = 96). An average of 2.2 venous segments were treated per patient (range, 1-5). Mean preprocedure clot burden was 88.0%, which decreased to 10.5% postprocedure, culminating in a mean thrombus clearance of 88.0%. Overall, 76.0% of patients (n = 152) achieved ≥90% clot resolution. Adjunctive rotational maceration was used in 30% of cases, balloon venoplasty in 38%, and stent placement in 15%. Mean device utilization time was 8.0 minutes, with an average of 2.4 device passes per patient. Mean estimated blood loss was 320 (range, 50-750) mL. The overall complication rate was 2.4% (n = 5), consisting exclusively of minor access-site hematomas not attributed to the device. No serious adverse events were device-attributable within the 200-patient cohort. Procedures were predominantly classified as peripheral venous interventions (70%), with the remaining 30% encompassing alternative indications (eg, in-stent restenosis and transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt revisions). CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort of 200 patients, the CLEANER Vac system demonstrated high procedural efficacy (88.0% mean clot clearance, 76% achieving ≥90% resolution) and a favorable overall safety profile. The findings support the potential role of this system in enabling rapid, single-session VTE treatment with constrained hemorrhagic liability and morbidity compared with catheter-directed thrombolysis. Prospective, longitudinal studies are warranted to evaluate long-term outcomes and delineate optimal patient stratification.

title: Outcomes of thoracic endovascular aortic repair for uncomplicated subacute type B aortic dissection in the IRAD registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) for uncomplicated type B acute aortic dissection (TBAAD) remains controversial. Compared with best medical therapy (BMT), TEVAR has demonstrated benefits for aortic remodeling; however, this intervention has procedure-related risks. METHODS: The International Registry of Acute Aortic Dissection database was queried from January 1996 to September 2023 for all uncomplicated TBAAD cases. Patients receiving TEVAR during the subacute phase (sTEVAR; 15-90 days) and BMT were included in this study. Baseline comorbidities were recorded. The primary outcome was survival at 4 years. The secondary outcomes included delayed aortic interventions, progression of aortic disease, new dissection, rehospitalization, rupture, and stroke. RESULTS: During the study period, 1373 patients with uncomplicated TBAAD were entered into the registry and had follow-up data available. In addition, 63 patients (4.6%) underwent sTEVAR, and 1310 (95.4%) received BMT. The 4-year survival rate was similar between the groups (sTEVAR 87% vs BMT 84%, P = .925). At 3 years, the sTEVAR group had higher rates of new dissection (13.9% vs 4.8%, P = .002), all within 1 year of TEVAR. Progression of dissection, aneurysmal degeneration, reintervention, rupture, stroke, and rehospitalization were comparable between the groups. CONCLUSIONS: Compared with BMT, sTEVAR led to similar survival rates. New dissection was higher in the sTEVAR group. TEVAR may have a role in uncomplicated subacute TBAAD, and further randomized trials are essential to identify which patients benefit from this intervention.

title: The Effectiveness of Autologous Platelet-Rich Plasma Topical Application Versus Injection in the Healing of Chronic Venous Ulcers.
abstract: Introduction Chronic venous leg ulcers (VLUs) are common lower-limb wounds associated with delayed healing, recurrence, pain, impaired mobility, reduced quality of life, and increased healthcare costs. Although compression therapy remains the standard treatment, many ulcers heal slowly or remain resistant, highlighting the need for effective adjunctive therapies. Autologous platelet-rich plasma (PRP) is rich in platelets and growth factors that promote angiogenesis, fibroblast proliferation, collagen synthesis, granulation tissue formation, and re-epithelialization, making it a promising regenerative therapy for chronic venous ulcers. However, existing evidence is limited due to small sample sizes, methodological heterogeneity, and variability in PRP preparation. Systematic reviews have therefore recommended well-designed prospective randomized trials to establish its efficacy and safety. Aims and objectives The study aims to evaluate the clinical efficacy of PRP topical application, PRP injection, and saline dressings in chronic VLUs, with the primary objective based on complete ulcer healing and percentage reduction in ulcer size, while assessing ulcer recurrence and early treatment-related complications constituted the secondary endpoints. Recurrence here is defined as re-appearance of the ulcer after its complete healing at the same site. Methodology This prospective randomized controlled trial was conducted over 18 months at JSS Medical College and Hospital, Mysuru, Karnataka, India. A total of 63 adults with chronic VLUs (>6 weeks) were randomly allocated into three groups: group A (topical PRP dressing), group B (local PRP injection), and group C (saline dressing). All patients received a standard four-layer compression therapy. Autologous PRP was prepared using a double-spin centrifugation technique and administered weekly for four weeks. Patients were followed for six months. Primary outcomes included complete ulcer healing and percentage reduction in ulcer area, while recurrence and treatment-related complications were assessed as secondary outcomes using SPSS Version 28 (p < 0.05). Results Baseline comparability was noted among groups for age, sex, BMI, HbA1c, platelet count, ankle-brachial pressure index, ulcer duration, and initial ulcer area. At six weeks, complete healing of the ulcer was much greater in group B (33.3%) than in group A (9.5%) and group C (0%) (p = 0.0064). At three months, the mean ulcer area was minimal in group B (1.30 ± 1.61 cm²) compared to group A (3.15 ± 3.01 cm²) and group C (6.19 ± 4.49 cm²) (p < 0.0001). The percentage reduction in ulcer area at three months was highest in group B (91.80 ± 8.05%), followed by group A (78.29 ± 17.68%) and group C (62.34 ± 19.06%). The mean healing duration was the shortest in group B (11.20 ± 2.18 weeks) (p = 0.0001). The rates of recurrence and complications were minimal and similar. Conclusion Autologous PRP is a safe and effective adjunct for chronic VLUs. Both PRP topical application and injection improved healing compared with saline dressing, while PRP injection achieved earlier healing, greater ulcer area reduction, and shorter healing time, making it the preferred PRP delivery method.

title: Perioperative Predictors and Temporal Trajectories of Postoperative Cognitive Decline After Carotid Endarterectomy: A Prospective Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Carotid artery stenosis is a well-established risk factor for vascular cognitive impairment. Although carotid endarterectomy (CEA) reduces the risk of ischemic stroke, its effect on cognitive function remains uncertain. Most previous studies have relied on mean changes in cognitive scores and have not defined postoperative cognitive decline using patient-level thresholds for the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA). Moreover, few studies have integrated perioperative variables across baseline, intraoperative, and postoperative domains to examine heterogeneity in cognitive outcomes. We therefore defined postoperative cognitive decline using threshold-based MoCA changes and prospectively evaluated perioperative factors associated with distinct cognitive outcomes after CEA. METHODS: We prospectively enrolled older patients undergoing elective CEA under general anesthesia. Of 183 patients screened, 162 were ultimately enrolled and analyzed. All patients were managed according to standardized anesthetic and surgical protocols. Preoperative clinical, laboratory, and imaging variables, intraoperative hemodynamic parameters, and postoperative clinical indicators were collected. The primary outcome was cognitive decline at discharge, defined as a decrease of ≥2 points from baseline in the MoCA score. The secondary outcome was cognitive decline at 30 days, defined as a ≥3-point decrease in the telephone MoCA (t-MoCA) score relative to the corresponding baseline domains. RESULTS: Among the 162 enrolled patients, preoperative triglyceride level, preoperative cerebral hypoperfusion volume, surgical laterality, intraoperative mean arterial pressure (MAP) decline, and visual analogue scale (VAS) on postoperative day 1 were independently associated with early postoperative cognitive decline. A prediction model incorporating these five factors achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.752 (95% CI: 0.670-0.835) for cognitive decline before discharge. For 30-day cognitive decline, the model demonstrated an AUC of 0.717 (95% CI: 0.606-0.828). All patients with complete 30-day follow-up were stratified into four cognitive trajectory subtypes, and their longitudinal cognitive changes were visualized using a Sankey diagram. CONCLUSIONS: A perioperative model incorporating metabolic, cerebral perfusion, surgical, hemodynamic, and pain-related variables may help identify patients at increased risk of cognitive decline after CEA. The trajectory analysis further reveals heterogeneous postoperative cognitive patterns, including transient, delayed, and persistent decline. These findings support individualized perioperative risk assessment and structured cognitive follow-up. However, no internal or external validation was performed, and further testing is required in larger multicenter cohorts.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Carotid artery stenosis is a well-established risk factor for vascular cognitive impairment. Although carotid endarterectomy (CEA) reduces the risk of ischemic stroke, its effect on cognitive function remains uncertain. Most previous studies have relied on mean changes in cognitive scores and have not defined postoperative cognitive decline using patient-level thresholds for the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA).

title: The Current State of Digital Variance Angiography: A Literature Review.
abstract: Digital variance angiography (DVA), also referred to as kinetic imaging angiography, is an imaging technique that enhances vascular visualization by analyzing contrast flow motion. Although digital subtraction angiography (DSA) remains the current standard of care, DVA has demonstrated potential improvements in image quality and reductions in both radiation exposure and contrast use. This literature review aimed to evaluate currently available literature focusing on the use of DVA during angiographic procedures. The review was conducted using PubMed, EMBASE, and Web of Science, with the process being reflected in a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA) flowchart. Across multiple clinical applications, DVA consistently demonstrated higher objective image quality metrics including contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) as compared with DSA. Several studies reported that expert reviewers observed improved subjective image quality and substantial reductions in radiation exposure. In addition, DVA has also been shown to facilitate reduced use of contrast, potentially decreasing contrast-related complications and healthcare costs. Collectively, current evidence suggests that DVA represents a promising advancement in angiographic imaging, with the potential to deliver superior image quality with reduced radiation exposure and contrast use.

title: Long-Term Cardiovascular, Thromboembolic, and Malignancy Safety of Janus Kinase (JAK) Inhibitors in Dermatologic and Rheumatologic Populations: A Narrative Comparative Review.
abstract: Janus kinase inhibitors are increasingly used in dermatology and rheumatology, but concerns about cardiovascular events, thromboembolism, and malignancy continue to influence long-term treatment decisions. This narrative comparative review examines evidence from randomized trials, integrated safety analyses, long-term extensions, selected observational studies, and regulatory sources, focusing on rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, atopic dermatitis, and alopecia areata. Topical agents and selective tyrosine kinase 2 inhibition are considered separately because of important differences in systemic exposure and pharmacology. The original, informally assembled evidence base was supplemented by a targeted literature update. ORAL Surveillance identified an important safety signal for tofacitinib compared with tumor necrosis factor inhibitors in patients with rheumatoid arthritis and cardiovascular risk factors. Long-term dermatology studies have generally reported low absolute event rates, although younger study populations, restrictive eligibility criteria, limited long-term comparator data, and treatment discontinuation affect how these findings should be interpreted. Observational studies in dermatology have produced mixed results, including thromboembolic associations that warrant further investigation. Psoriatic arthritis provides additional evidence across the clinical boundaries of both specialties. Differences in patient populations, study design, outcome definitions, and statistical measures limit direct comparisons across studies. Treatment decisions should follow indication-specific prescribing requirements and consider cardiovascular disease, prior thrombosis, smoking, age, malignancy history, and available alternatives. Additional long-term comparative studies are needed to better distinguish patient-, disease-, and treatment-related risks.

title: Chronic Venous Disease as a Prognostic Factor for Venous Thromboembolism: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This systematic review aimed to evaluate chronic venous disease as a prognostic factor for subsequent venous thromboembolism. DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were systematically searched. REVIEW METHODS: This systematic review was conducted according to Cochrane Prognosis Methods Group guidance and reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. The primary outcome was venous thromboembolism, defined as deep vein thrombosis and/or pulmonary embolism. Certainty of the evidence was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. RESULTS: 2 2 2 2 Seven longitudinal, prognostic factor studies including 3 760 257 participants were included, of whom 702 325 had chronic venous disease and 3 057 932 served as controls. Six studies evaluated varicose veins, whereas one more broadly evaluated chronic venous disease. Pooled unadjusted analysis identified an increased risk of venous thromboembolism (risk ratio [RR] 2.25, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.09 - 2.43, I= 0%; p = .83, moderate certainty of evidence) and deep vein thrombosis (RR 5.23, 95% CI 4.92 - 5.56, I= 64.6%; p = .059, moderate certainty of evidence) among chronic venous disease individuals compared with controls. Crude time to event analysis replicated these findings, demonstrating an increased venous thromboembolism hazard among the chronic venous disease group (hazard ratio [HR] 2.52, 95% CI 1.88 - 3.37, I= 0%; p = .80, moderate certainty of evidence). However, in the adjusted time to event analysis, which included two studies comprising 2 320 327 participants, the association was attenuated and fell marginally short of statistical significance (adjusted HR 1.76, 95% CI 0.97 - 3.19, I= 74.0%; p = .050, very low certainty of evidence). CONCLUSIONS: Although the available evidence, predominantly derived from studies evaluating varicose veins, consistently indicated higher unadjusted venous thromboembolism estimates among chronic venous disease individuals, adjusted prognostic data were limited and heterogeneous, resulting in very low certainty. Chronic venous disease may represent a clinically relevant marker of subsequent venous thromboembolism, but the magnitude and independence of this prognostic effect remain uncertain, highlighting the need for adequately adjusted longitudinal studies.

title: [Effects of digital-driven cardiac rehabilitation on clinical outcomes in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement].
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effects of digital-driven cardiac rehabilitation on clinical outcomes in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). This study has been registered with the U.S. National Library of Medicine Clinical Trials Registry under the identifier NCT02803294. METHODS: Data from 1012 patients who underwent TAVR at the Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine, between March 2013 and January 2023 were retrospectively analyzed. Patients receiving conventional rehabilitation were assigned to the control group, whereas those receiving a digital-driven cardiac rehabilitation program, comprising preoperative screening and functional preparation, intraoperative eligibility assessment, postoperative stepwise rehabilitation management, and intelligent home-based rehabilitation, were assigned to the observation group. Propensity score matching was performed to adjust for baseline confounding. Postoperative intensive care unit (ICU) stay and hospital stay, the incidence of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular adverse events at 30 days, 1 year, and 2 years after TAVR, and functional outcomes, including the five-meter walking test, six-minute walking test, and Katz index, were compared between the two groups. RESULTS: vs P vs P P P After propensity score matching, 251 patients were included in each group. Compared with the control group, the observation group had shorter postoperative ICU stays [0 (0, 1) h. 0 (0, 0) h,<0.01] and postoperative hospital stays [8 (7, 11) d. 3 (1, 7) d,<0.01]. No apparent increase in the incidence of adverse events was observed in the observation group at 30 days, 1 year, or 2 years after TAVR. The time required to complete the five-meter walking test was shorter in the observation group than in the control group at 30 days, 1 year, and 2 years after TAVR (all<0.01). Results of six-minute walking test and Katz index showed no significant differences between the groups (both>0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Digital-driven cardiac rehabilitation may shorten hospital stay and improve selected functional outcomes in patients undergoing TAVR without increase in postoperative cardiovascular and cerebrovascular adverse events.

title: Apparent Diffusion Coefficient Fraction Predicts Endovascular Thrombectomy Benefit in Large Ischemic Core.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) is recommended for large ischemic core stroke, but which patients within this population derive meaningful benefit remains uncertain. We investigated whether the fraction of apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC)-defined infarct volume within the ischemic lesion predicts EVT outcomes in large ischemic core stroke. METHODS: 3 -6 2 This retrospective study included patients with diffusion-weighted imaging volume ≥50 cmand large vessel occlusion within 24-hour of onset (2016-2024; EVT:130, no-EVT:192). The ADC fraction was defined as the volume of ADC <540 × 10mm/s divided by initial diffusion-weighted imaging volume. Overlap weighting (OW) with doubly robust estimation corrected for indication bias. Primary outcomes were modified Rankin Scale shift and favorable outcome (modified Rankin Scale score 0-3) at 3-month. The relationship between ADC fraction and EVT treatment effect was examined using overlap-weighted restricted cubic spline interaction analysis, and treatment effects were subsequently quantified above and below the crossover point. RESULTS: 3 3 P interaction A total of 322 patients were included (age, 73.8 years, 51.9% men). Before OW, patients with EVT were younger with lower National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score and smaller diffusion-weighted imaging volumes (EVT: 93.8 cm, no-EVT: 129.9 cm). After OW, all covariates were well-balanced. The doubly robust-OW analysis demonstrated attenuation of EVT effect on ordinal modified Rankin Scale score shift (odds ratio, 1.37 [95% CI, 0.85-2.21]) and favorable outcome (odds ratio, 1.73 [95% CI, 0.91-3.28]). ADC fraction significantly modified the EVT treatment effect (=0.009), with a crossover at 48%, identified as a data-derived exploratory threshold. Below this threshold, EVT was associated with a favorable ordinal modified Rankin Scale score shift (odds ratio, 1.85 [95% CI, 1.05-3.26]), whereas above it the direction of the association was reversed (odds ratio, 0.42 [95% CI, 0.19-0.95]). CONCLUSIONS: In large ischemic core stroke, the association between EVT and functional outcome varied according to infarct tissue composition. The ADC fraction distinguished patients in whom EVT was associated with more favorable outcomes from those in whom this association was not observed, supporting its potential as an imaging biomarker to inform individualized treatment decisions.

title: Clinical Improvement, No Improvement, and Worsening at 24 Hours Following Reperfusion in Patients With Stroke due to Large-Vessel Occlusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Restoring blood flow to ischemic tissue is the cornerstone of acute stroke therapy and is usually beneficial. However, when reperfusion is achieved for severely injured tissue, it is often futile and may occasionally cause harm. We aim to determine the prevalence and variables associated with clinical no improvement or acute worsening at 24 hours despite reperfusion in patients with large-vessel occlusion stroke treated with endovascular thrombectomy. METHODS: Data are from ESCAPE-NA1 (Safety and Efficacy of Nerinetide [NA-1] in Subjects Undergoing Endovascular Thrombectomy for Stroke), a randomized trial of nerinetide in patients with acute large-vessel occlusion stroke undergoing endovascular thrombectomy. Patients with unsuccessful recanalization (expanded Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction <2b), infarcts in new vascular territories, vessel perforation, or remote parenchymal hemorrhage were excluded. Clinical outcomes after reperfusion were classified by 24-hour National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale changes compared with baseline: improvement (≥4-point improvement), no improvement (±3-point from baseline), and worsening (≥4-point worsening). Baseline variables associated with worsening were identified using logistic regression. In the computed tomography perfusion subgroup, prevalence of parenchymal hemorrhage (any parenchymal hematoma) and infarct progression (final infarct volume exceeding the initial hypoperfused region) were evaluated. RESULTS: A total of 833 patients were included (median age, 70.9 years [interquartile range, 60.7-79.4]; 51.4% men). After reperfusion, 669 (80.3%) patients improved, 135 (16.2%) showed no improvement, and 29 (3.5%) worsened. Independent predictors of worsening were longer onset-to-reperfusion time (adjusted odds ratio, 1.02 [95% CI, 1.00-1.04] per 10-minute increase) and greater degree of sedation (adjusted odds ratio, 1.78 [95% CI, 1.29-2.46] per category of none, conscious sedation, and general anesthesia). In the computed tomography perfusion subgroup (n=414), among patients with worsening after reperfusion, parenchymal hemorrhage was seen in 5 patients (31.3%) and infarct progression in 4 patients (25%). CONCLUSIONS: Clinical worsening in the acute period (ie, early neurological deterioration) despite reperfusion and the absence of procedure-related complications was rare in this selected large-vessel occlusion stroke cohort (3.5%). Factors associated with worsening after reperfusion were a longer time from symptom onset-to-reperfusion and a higher degree of sedation.

We aim to determine the prevalence and variables associated with clinical no improvement or acute worsening at 24 hours despite reperfusion in patients with large-vessel occlusion stroke treated with endovascular thrombectomy.

title: Venous Thromboembolism in Severe Renal Insufficiency: 20 Years of Contemporary Management and Clinical Outcomes.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with severe renal insufficiency have been systematically excluded from randomized trials of anticoagulation for venous thromboembolism (VTE), leaving uncertainty regarding their management in clinical practice. OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to describe the clinical profile, temporal trends in management, and phase-specific outcomes of patients with acute VTE and severe renal insufficiency. METHODS: We analyzed 5,763 patients with acute VTE and creatinine clearance < 30 mL/min enrolled in Registro Informatizado de Enfermedad TromboEmbólica (2005-2024). Baseline characteristics, anticoagulant strategies, and 90-day outcomes were evaluated across 4 calendar periods and during the early (days 0-10) and late (days 11-90) treatment phases. RESULTS: Mean age was 81 years; 69% were women, 56% presented with pulmonary embolism (PE), 16% had creatinine clearance <15 mL/min, and 3.6% were receiving hemodialysis. Over time, severe renal dysfunction and hemodialysis became more frequent. Initial treatment remained predominantly low-molecular-weight heparin, whereas vitamin K antagonist use declined and direct oral anticoagulant use increased. At 90 days, recurrent VTE occurred in 1.3% of patients, major bleeding in 5.1%, and 20% died. During the first 10 days, fatal PE exceeded fatal bleeding (2.0% vs 0.3%), whereas during days 11 to 90 fatal bleeding exceeded fatal PE (0.7% vs 0.3%). CONCLUSIONS: Patients with VTE and severe renal insufficiency are elderly, medically complex, and experience high short-term mortality. The relative balance between fatal PE and fatal bleeding changes over time, with fatal PE predominating early and fatal bleeding thereafter, while real-world management frequently differs from product labels and guideline recommendations.

OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to describe the clinical profile, temporal trends in management, and phase-specific outcomes of patients with acute VTE and severe renal insufficiency. METHODS: We analyzed 5,763 patients with acute VTE and creatinine clearance < 30 mL/min enrolled in Registro Informatizado de Enfermedad TromboEmbólica (2005-2024).

title: The association of rural residence with aneurysm presentation and loss to follow-up after endovascular aneurysm repair in the Vascular Quality Initiative.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Early recognition, timely access to care, and diligent follow-up are essential components of care for patients with aortic aneurysms. Rural patients have significant barriers to care and may present for surgery with larger aneurysms and be more likely to be lost to follow-up (LTFU). The purpose of this study was to assess the effects of rurality on clinical presentation of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA) and follow-up after endovascular aortic aneurysm repair. METHODS: The Vascular Quality Initiative's U.S. endovascular aortic aneurysm repair module (2003-2021) was used for analyses (n = 62,503). Patients were categorized as residing in an urban or rural area using rural-urban commuting area codes. Univariate analyses were performed to describe differences in sociodemographic, intraoperative, and follow-up factors. We fit unadjusted and adjusted logistic regression models to assess the association between rurality and aneurysm size, symptomatic presentation, adverse cardiovascular events, death, loss to follow-up, and follow-up type. RESULTS: A total of 79% (n = 49,372) of patients were classified as urban and 21% (n = 13,131) as rural with several significantly different demographic variables. On multivariable analyses, residing in a rural compared with urban area was significantly associated with 9% higher odds of undergoing repair with an aneurysm diameter of >6.5 cm [adjusted odds ratio (aOR), 1.09; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.03-1.15], an 18% increase in the odds of presenting with an urgent AAA compared with elective (aOR, 1.18; 95% CI, 1.11-1.24) and a 14% increase in the odds of being LTFU (aOR, 1.14; 95% CI, 1.05-1.23). Finally, of the patients who did follow-up, rural compared with urban residence was associated with a 10% lower odds of having in-person follow-up (aOR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.86-0.95), but was associated with 13% higher odds of having any follow-up imaging (aOR, 1.13; 95% CI, 1.04-1.23). CONCLUSIONS: This study found that rural patients had higher odds of large aneurysms at time of repair, higher odds of requiring urgent repair, and being LTFU. When they did have follow-up, it was less likely to be in-person. This suggests geographic disparities in quality of and access to appropriate AAA screening, repair and follow-up. Addressing this disparity will require coordinated multidisciplinary efforts, efficient referral pipelines, and reliable surveillance mechanisms postoperatively. Future efforts should aim to develop and implement evidence-based care delivery strategies for AAA care for patients in rural settings, such as primary care clinician education, telehealth platforms and travel assistance.

Rural patients have significant barriers to care and may present for surgery with larger aneurysms and be more likely to be lost to follow-up (LTFU).
